### Native light

Plan Task 7 (2026-10-08): the first lit pixels. With `--fable2_native_light=on`, now the default, the clay pass lights the terrain and the objects that carry a colour stream with the game's own ambient, baked and sun light, in linear space, without shadows. Code: `clay_logic.h` "Native light" (the pure mirrors `AmbientFactor`, `AmbientAxis`, `AmbientT`, `LightPow`, `FacingGate`, `SunGateSingle`, `LightTerrainLayer`, `LightTerrainFar`, `LightObject`, `ClayLit`; `ClayFrameConstants`, `ClayObjectConstants`, `SetClayTerrainLight`, `LightFamilyDrawn`, `LightVertexNeed`, `FormatLightDrawnText`; the light flag of `PlanTerrain`), `fable2_native_shaders.h` (the blocks `Frame` and `Object`, the light functions, the lit paths of the vertex shader and of three pixel shaders), `clay_pass.cpp` (`PrepareLight`, `PrepareTerrain`, `FinishTerrain`, `Render`), `geometry_cache.cpp` (`Normals`, `Colours`, `Indices`), `tools/xdk_sigmatch/light_check.py` (`--multi-sun`), `tools/xdk_sigmatch/terrain_replay.py` (`--lit`). Tests: `test_clay_logic.cpp` cases 420 to 484, `test_native_shaders.cpp` codes 31, 35 to 40, 45, 46, 64, 69 and 80 to 97, `tests/test_light_check.py` (`PinnedForTheRenderer`, `MultiSun`), `tests/test_terrain_replay.py` (the `lit` tests). Evidence: `task7\`.

**What is lit.** A drawn record is lit when the switch is on, its frame has a light block the pass can use, its pair of shaders has one of the families below, and everything the family reads is there:

| Family (`LightInputs`) | Pixel shaders | What the pass needs per draw | Function |
|---|---|---|---|
| `terrain-layer`, with its two- and four-light forms | `0x9C21...`, `0x4755...`; `0x4524...`, `0xAF1E...` (two lights), `0x04F2...`, `0x5783...` (four) | the vertex normals of its grid (tf17), the base map tf3 with `base_valid` inputs, `c11.x`, the facing literal 8 | `LightTerrainLayer` |
| `terrain-far` | `0x7DDA...`, `0x2F8A...` | the same without the literal | `LightTerrainFar` |
| `object` with vertex shader `0xECD6...` (`LightVertexKind::kStream`), with its two- and four-light forms | `0x8D90...`, `0x2FD2...`; `0x648B...` (two), `0x7892...` (four) | the stream normals and the colour stream's colours, the world rotation with a direction, `c27.w`, `c49.xyz`, `c26.xyz`, the power 2.2 | `LightObject` |
| `object` with probe colours (`kProbe`: vertex shaders `0x79EA...`, and the bone-skinned `0xD4D5...`, `0xA1F7...`), with its two- and four-light forms (plan Task 8a) | the same four | the normals (a skinned mesh's after its bones), the probe buffer (four weights and a set index per vertex), the twelve probe registers `c28..c39`, the world rotation with a direction, `c27.w`, `c49.xyz`, `c26.xyz` | `LightObject` with the probe colour |
| `tree-trunk` (`kProbe`: vertex shader `0x475E...`), with its two- and four-light forms (plan Task 8a) | `0x00E0...`; `0x58D3...` (two), `0x2FBE...` (four) | as the probe objects (the trunk's scale `c7.w`, 0.67 to 1.53, is inside the rows) | `LightObject` with the probe colour |
| `plant` (`kInstance`: vertex shaders `0x8123...`, `0xFC4F...`, `0x48D3...`), with its two-light form (plan Task 8b) | `0xA7E4...`, `0x2605...`; `0xE99F...` (two) | the flat normals, the copies' colours and the bend inputs (the copy's up axis and the vertex's height per flat position), the three bend constants `c45.xyz` | `LightPlant` with the vertex side's ambient and the bent normal |
| `plant-lit` (`kInstance`: vertex shaders `0xB636...`, `0x6AD4...`, `0x36B5...`, `0x33C0...`), with its two-light form (plan Task 8b) | `0x165E...`; `0xF525...` (two) | the same | `LightPlantLit`: the object form with the copy's colour, `c27.w` = 1 and `c49` = 1, and the bent normal |
| `tree-leaf` (`kProbe`: vertex shaders `0xA584...`, and `0xD7DD...`, `0x2D40...` with two and four lights; plan Task 8c) | `0x7CD5...` | as the trunks (normals, the probe buffer, the twelve probe registers, the world rotation with a direction, `c27.w`, `c49.xyz`, `c26.xyz`), and the world translation (`c4..c6` .w), the wrap `c50.w` and the frame's eye | `LightLeaf` with the vertex side's ambient and the sun's two scalars on the side the viewer sees |

Everything else is drawn as the materials picture draws it, the unlit linear colour, and counted by reason (`ClayUnlit`): `light-off` (the switch, or the texture path off: the light is of the material), `light-block` (the frame has no block: every draw of it), `light-unknown` (no light inputs, a family the pass does not light; a missing buffer, base map or value; a world rotation without a direction; a ground square unlit as a whole) and `normal-unsupported`. Nothing is lit from a guessed value: every number that reaches a shader is checked to be a number of usable size (`LightValueUsable`: magnitude at most 1,024; the captured values are below 2) by `MakeClayFrameConstants`, `MakeClayObjectConstants` (an object's, a trunk's and, since plan Task 8b, a plant's) and `SetClayTerrainLight`, each of which refuses as a whole.

**The two- and four-light forms** (controller amendment C2). These shaders compute light 0 in another form (`sun_gate_multi` of `lighting-formulas.md`) and the sun is not their light 0. Where it stands, from the rows' `"pfull"` of the two captures of plan Task 6's final runs (`task7\multi_slots.py`, `multi_slots_bridge_trees.txt`): in all 1,520 `-multi` main-scene rows of eight frames at the bridge and all 944 by the trees `c112` is one-hot, the light at its slot is the frame's sun (`xyz` bit-equal to `c109.xyz`, `w` = 0, `c94` = 0 there, direction and colour equal to the frame row's block in every frame that has one), and every other light with a colour is a lantern (`w` = 1, `c94` = 1). Every draw of a two-light shader has one lantern in slot 0 and the sun in slot 1; every draw of a four-light shader has two lanterns and the sun in slot 2. `light_check.py --multi-sun` then runs each pair's microcode with exactly that light set (the sun in the slot, the lanterns dark as spec ruling 5 has them, everything else of a trial random, the screen mask random too) against the family's ONE-light function fed that sun: all nine pairs of the terrain, object and trunk families agree in 400 of 400 trials at every slot behind light 0 (slot 1 for the five pairs of a two-light shader, slots 1 to 3 for the four pairs of a four-light one; largest relative difference 1.5e-15; `task7\light_check_multi_sun.txt`). The check fails when any one property of that light set is taken away (a lantern with its light, the mask on the lantern, range and cone on the sun, the sun as a position: `tests/test_light_check.py`, `MultiSun`). So the pairs in scope here, the four layer pairs and `0x648B...` / `0x7892...` with `0xECD6...`, are drawn with the frame's sun through the one-light function, without their lanterns; the trunks' two pairs passed the same check for plan Task 8.

**As drawn.** The HLSL functions are those of `tools/xdk_sigmatch/light_formulas.py` statement for statement and carry its names and argument lists; the C++ mirrors in `clay_logic.h` are pinned to numbers computed by the Python functions, the same literals in `tests/test_light_check.py` (`PinnedForTheRenderer`) and `test_clay_logic.cpp` (cases 420 to 431).

- *Terrain, vertex shader.* The normal is the game's: `(x, y)` from the record's buffer (t8), `z = sqrt(|1 - x^2 - y^2|)`, not normalised. For a lit record the vector of the ambient factor is made per vertex as the game makes it, `axis = lerp(n, C, (1 + n . C) / 2)` with `C` the block's `axis` (pixel `c23.xyz`, equal to vertex `c19.xyz`), and interpolated.
- *Terrain layer, pixel shader.* `N = normalize(n)`, `t = sat(normalize(axis) . N)`, `L = c22 + (1 - c22) t^2`; `colour = A * c11.x * (pow(tf3, c21.w) * c21.xyz * L + c20.xyz) + A * c87.xyz * sat(N . sun) * sat(8 * (N . sun)) * 1`, `A` the layer's linear colour (`tf0^2` or the steep-ground mix), tf3 the base map at the base coordinate, the last 1 the screen mask. The layer's alpha (weight times fade) is not lit.
- *Far terrain.* `t = sat(N . c23.xyz)` with the constant as it is, `colour = F * (pow(tf3, c21.w) * c21.xyz * L + c20.xyz) + F * c11.x * c87.xyz * sat(N . sun)`; the underlay `0x2F8A...` then multiplies by its fade.
- *Object, vertex shader.* `o1 = M n` with `M = world_rot * world_scale` (the game's `(R n) * c7.w`; the scalar is inside the rows the shader gets, so its sign counts), not normalised; `axis = lerp(o1, C, (1 + o1 . C) / 2)`; the colour is the stream's red, green and blue (bytes 0 to 2 of the cache's entry) over 255, raised to the draw's power 2.2. A draw whose `M` has no direction (`ClassifyRotation`: degenerate) is not lit; mirrored and skewed ones are lit with the game's own `M n` (ruling of 2026-10-08), and the classes are still counted in the `Light inputs:` line.
- *Object, pixel shader.* `colour = (A * c27.w * (pow(vcolour, c21.w) * c21.xyz * L + c20.xyz) + A * c87.xyz * sat(N . sun) * 1) * c49.xyz`, then times `c26.xyz`. `A` is the albedo squared, after the division by its alpha where the shader has it and clamped to [0, 1] before the square, as the materials picture clamps it (the game does not clamp there).
- *A zero normal* is never made a direction: `light_normalize` gives zero for a vector without a length, so `N . sun` and `t` are 0: no sun and the ambient at its floor, which is what the game's saturating dot products give. The power of a zero base is 0 by a select, and nothing is divided.
- *The sun* is one vector for `c80.xyz` and `c109.xyz` (`ClayFrameConstants::sun_dir`): the block is valid only where the two are bit-equal.
- *Blue has no ambient floor*: the block carries `c22.xy`, and `c22.z` is taken as 0, which it is in every captured row.

**Scale.** The value written is the formula's value without the game's output scale `c20.w` (16): the game multiplies every scene shader's colour by it and its later passes take it back; here the exposure of the lit output stands in its place ("The exposure", next). `c49.xyz` is inside the object's function. `c26.xyz`, which the game applies together with `c20.w` after its fog, multiplies the function's result. Both are (1, 1, 1) in every captured row.

*Note of 2026-10-10 (post sub-project, Task 8b; ledger ruling 30).* The exposure 2.22 and every terrain figure of this section are of the base map tf3 read as stored, which made the ambient part of lit ground 1.8 to 2.5 times the game's. Since commit `5d0f974` the pass reads it through its fetch constant's gamma curve; the exposure is deliberately not fitted again, and at 2.22 the dirt patch reads 0.83 of the adapting game's where it was fitted to 1: section 17, "The base map's gamma sign".

**The exposure.** `ClayExposure(on)` is `kLitExposure`, 2.22, calibrated in plan Task 9 ("Validation" below; it was 1 until then, and the figures of the runs before that task in this subsection are under exposure 1). It is the lit draws' alone (the final fix wave, 2026-10-08). `MakeClayFrameConstants` puts it into a lit frame's block (`ClayFrameConstants::exposure`, cbuffer `Frame`'s `f_exposure` at byte 44; 0 in a frame without light, where no draw reads it), and the three pixel shaders that light multiply their value by it in front of the bound: `clay_lit(lit * f_exposure)` in the textured shader, `clay_lit(colour * f_exposure)` in the terrain shaders' common output. Nothing else takes it: an unlit draw writes its colour as it is, the clear is the clear, and the output mapping multiplies by its own word, which the pass sets to 1 in every frame (`kClayMapExposure`). So lit and unlit values have one unit in the target, a blend of a lit and an unlit draw is consistent, and what is not lit in a lit frame is shown exactly as with the light off. *As built in plan Task 9* the exposure was the mapping's word, `ClayFrameExposure`, 2.22 for a lit frame and 1 for a frame without light. That was a defect, found by the whole-branch review: the mapping multiplied every pixel, so the clear of a lit frame showed levels (30, 30, 37) for (20, 20, 25) and every unlit draw of a lit frame was `sqrt(2.22)` = 1.49 times too bright on the display ("Validation", "The exposure", has the figures). What the fix changes in the compiled programs: nothing in the vertex shader (every one of its 128 fixed-mode programs and the whole program are line for line those of commit `24c1751`), nothing in any pixel program without bit 2, the flat shader, the mapping and the composite; one `mul` by `cb2[2].w` in the lit pixel programs; no load, no binding and no buffer size (`fix\programs_fix_a.txt`; shader test code 166 holds the same against the text as it was). Tests: case 418 (the clear at its levels in a lit frame, an unlit level d shown as d, a lit v as `sqrt(min(v * E, 1))`), cases 442 to 444 (the frame's constants carry the exposure when lit and 0 otherwise), shader codes 38, 83, 89, 161 and 166.

**Where the values reach the shaders.**

- *The frame's block*: cbuffer `Frame` at register b2 (`ClayFrameConstants`, 96 bytes: sun direction, sun colour, tint, exponent, added light, floor, axis, and `light_on`; 112 since plan Task 8c with the eye; since the final fix wave the word at byte 44, a padding word until then, is the exposure of the lit output), in slot 0 of the frame's constant buffer, bound once per `Render` for the vertex and pixel stages. It is made from the scene's own block and from nothing else, so a frame is lit by its own light or not at all.
- *Per draw, in the root constants* (cbuffer `Draw`, 144 bytes as before): two of the three free words are `light_mode` (bit 0: the vertex shader forms the terrain normal from t8; bit 1: it reads an object's normal at t9 and its word at t10 and the rows of `Object`; bit 3, with bit 1: the word is the vertex's probe set and the colour is the probe colour, with the weights at t11 and the probe registers of `Object`; bit 2: the draw is lit; bit 4, with bit 1, since plan Task 8b: the draw is an instanced plant, whose normal goes through no rows, whose word at t10 is the colour of the vertex's copy and whose t11 holds the bend inputs; bit 5, with bit 4: the plant's family is the one with the ambient factor) and `light_count` (elements the light's buffers hold: a buffer is read only for a vertex below it). One word stays free.
- *Per draw, in a constant buffer slot at register b1*: the root signature has 64 words and holds 56 now (36 of constants, 2 for each of seven buffers and two constant buffers, 1 for each of two texture tables; 54 before plan Task 8a added t11), so the object's nine matrix values, `c27.w`, `c49`, `c26` and the power (17 values) do not fit the root constants. They are cbuffer `Object` (`ClayObjectConstants`: 80 bytes, since plan Task 8a 272 with the twelve probe registers and since plan Task 8c 288 with the leaf's register, in a slot of 512 bytes: "Probe colours" below) in a slot of the constant buffer that already held one 256-byte slot per terrain record; a lit terrain record's values (`t_base_uv`, `t_base_sampler`, `t_c11x`, `t_facing_scale`) are appended to its cbuffer `Terrain` (`ClayTerrainConstants`, 192 bytes, was 160). The buffer is one per frame, pooled as before: slot 0 the frame, then the terrain records, then the lit objects. It is taken for every frame that draws anything (before: only for a frame with terrain records), so that the two registers the vertex shader declares, b1 and b2, are bound at every draw whether or not the draw reads them. Without it (an allocation that fails) the frame has no terrain material, as before, and no light.
- *Buffers and textures*: t8 the terrain normals (float2; until now the steep-ground block read them through the UV register t2, which holds UVs only again), t9 an object's normals (float3), t10 its colours (uint; for a probe object or a leaf the set index of each vertex, for an instanced plant the colour of the vertex's copy), t11 (float4; `probe_or_bend` in the shader since the final fix wave, `probe_weights` before) a probe object's or a leaf's weights (plan Task 8a) or an instanced plant's bend inputs (plan Task 8b); t7, the fourth entry of the terrain texture table, the base map. **Every draw binds all of them** (t8, t9, t10, and t11 since plan Task 8a; the sentences that follow were written for the first three and hold for the four): its own buffer where its `light_mode` names it, else its own positions (as t2 for a draw without UVs), and the vertex shader loads from them only inside `[branch]` blocks on `light_mode` and `light_count`. Both are needed and both are tested: a buffer bound by its address (a root descriptor) has no bounds check on the GPU, and without the attribute the compiler turns the `if` into a select and loads all three for every vertex of every draw, at that draw's vertex indices, from whatever an earlier draw left bound (the first build did exactly that and its three lit runs ended in a removed device; that this was the cause is likely and not proven by an A/B, see "In the game"). The positions hold 16 bytes for every vertex a draw can name, as much as the largest of the four elements (8, 12, 4 and, at t11, 16), so even an unguarded load would lie inside them. The binding layout is made from one table, `kClayBindings` (`clay_logic.h`: kind, register, count, stage for the root parameters: eleven, twelve with t11, which is the backend's limit), and the shader tests hold every resource each compiled shader declares against that table for its stage, that no shader has a loop instruction, that every load from t8, t9, t10 and t11 is inside a branch while those from t0, t1 and t2 are not, and that no pixel shader loads from a buffer (codes 150 to 159, each with a control that fails; since plan Task 8c for each of the 128 values of `light_mode`). Which of the four is a draw's own is one pure rule, `LightBufferSources(light_mode)` (cases 485 to 489 and 533), and the pass binds the four in one loop over it. Two rules of the draw path were tightened in fix round 1, both for the same reason (nothing the shader is given may be unbound or out of range). *The index rule has a low end*: a record is drawn only if every vertex its triangles name lies inside the positions, `min_index + base_vertex >= 0` as well as `max_index + base_vertex < count` (`IndexRangeValid`; the index entry keeps the smallest index of its list; a record failing it is skipped as `bad-index`). Until then the low end was left to the vertex shader's own check, which compiles to a select after the load, so a negative base vertex with an index below it would have loaded from before the start of the positions and UVs (the review counted 0 of 10,236 captured rows with a negative base vertex; not recounted here). *A frame without its constant buffer draws nothing*: b1 and b2 are views of the frame's constant buffer, and when that buffer cannot be made (an allocation failure) no record of the frame is drawn (`ClayRecordsWithoutConstants`; counted under `render-other`, logged once); the targets are still cleared and mapped, so the native view shows the clear colour for that frame and never a stale picture. Until then such a frame drew its records flat with b1 and b2 unset. A draw without light also reads no light input, in either stage. That is tested on the program such a draw runs: each shader is compiled once more with `light_mode` a constant (0: no light, no steep ground; 1: steep ground without light), and what the compiler leaves must read neither cbuffer `Frame` nor (outside the terrain shaders, whose b1 is the terrain block) `Object`, load from no light buffer the mode does not name, and not sample the base map; the lit constants (6, 5) must read them, and two controls (an unlit colour and a vertex output that take a value from `Frame`) must be reported (codes 160 to 162). So what an unlit draw shows cannot depend on what b1, b2, t7, t9 and t10 hold, on any adapter. And the light paths themselves are pinned as text, because tests that look for single statements cannot see one that is added between them. Since plan Task 8a the pins are six pieces that leave no statement between a shader's inputs and its lit output outside them: the shared light block (cbuffer `Frame` and every light function, `light_normalize` to `clay_lit`, in each of the four shaders that light), the vertex shader's whole `main`, the textured pixel shader from `clay_linear` to the end of `main`, the terrain shaders' common functions (`sample_colour`, `sample_base`, `terrain_fade_in`, `terrain_out`), the layer shader from `sample_side` to the end of `main`, and the far shader's whole `main` (codes 163 to 165). Outside them are the declarations, which reflection holds against their tables and the layout, and `alpha_passes`. (As first written, in fix round 1 of plan Task 7, the pins were the five lit blocks alone, and the re-review showed that the same kind of change placed one line outside a block passed: a statement inside `LightObject`, `LightTerrainLayer`, `light_sun`, `AmbientAxis` or `sample_base`, the layer's normal negated or the far colour squared above the lit branch, the vertex colour halved above the textured shader's branch, the far shader's base coordinate replaced. Those nine are controls now, with the first review's five and with an insertion, a deletion and two reorderings inside the probe colour's block: 25 changes, each of which compiles and must be reported by the piece it is in.) Every reflection test holds a block's compiled layout against a table beside the HLSL and the table against the C++ struct, field by field (`kClayFrameFields`, `kClayObjectFields`, `kClayTerrainFields`; codes 88 to 97, cases 440 to 464).

**Probe colours** (plan Task 8a, 2026-10-08; in the game: the end of this paragraph). The objects without a colour stream and the trunks take their baked term from a colour the game's vertex shader makes per vertex: `o6 = c[28 + a0].xyz + (c[29 + a0] . w, c[30 + a0] . w, c[31 + a0] . w)`, four-component dot products, `w` the vertex's four weights and `a0` (0, 4 or 8) the set its position names (`lighting-formulas.md`, "Objects", `probe_colour`). *The power it takes*: none in the vertex shader (the colour stream's 2.2 is `0xECD6...`'s own literal); the pixel shader's `pow(x, c21.w)` is the only one, and the game computes it as `exp2(c21.w * log2(|x|))`: the logarithm's operand is the absolute value in all seven pixel shaders (`log r6.x, r_abs[6].x` in `0x8D90...`, instructions 37 to 39; `r_abs[6]` in `0x2FD2...`, `0x648B...`, `0x7892...`; `r_abs[8]` in the trunks' `0x00E0...`, `0x58D3...`, `0x2FBE...`). So a colour that the signed weights make exactly zero has no baked term (the added light and the sun remain), and a negative one is lit like its mirror image: no clamp at zero, no `max`, no NaN. `light_pow` and `LightPow` are that rule, and the mirrors are pinned to `light_formulas.py` on 0, -1e-8, -0.06 and on a probe set that gives exactly 0 and -0.0625 (cases 490 to 494; `PinnedForTheRenderer`, `test_probe_object`, `test_probe_colour_zero_and_negative`). *As drawn*: the clay vertex shader, under `light_mode` bit 3, reads the vertex's word at t10 as the set index, clamps it to 8 (`min(word, 8u)`; the buffer holds 0, 4 or 8 only, and the clamp keeps any other word inside the twelve registers), reads the weights at t11 and forms the colour from `o_probe[a0]` to `o_probe[a0 + 3]` of cbuffer `Object`; the pixel shader is the colour-stream objects' program unchanged (compiled with the mode fixed at 14 and at 6 the two listings are identical). A bone-skinned mesh's normals are in the cache after its bones (`normalize(B3 n)`) and go through the draw's rows `M` like any other object's. *Registers*: t10 is one `uint` per vertex whichever kind it is; for a probe object the pass binds the probe buffer there from `ProbeSetOffset(probe_count)`, the buffer's second region (a multiple of 256 bytes: the first buffer the pass binds from an offset that is not 0), and the same buffer from byte 0 at t11, the twelfth and last binding parameter. `LightBufferSources` names the four sources per `light_mode` and `LightBufferOffset` the offset; the count is the one the probe buffer was built with, never the draw's `light_count`, which is the smaller of that and the normals' count and bounds every load. *Constants*: `ClayObjectConstants` is 272 bytes with the registers, so a lit object's slot is 512 bytes (`kClayObjectSlotBytes`); the small slots (the frame's, the terrain's) stay 256 and the objects' follow them (`ClayObjectSlotOffset`). No view has a size, and the vertex shader declares the 272-byte block for every draw, so the buffer holds 512 bytes from the start of every slot the pass binds: without objects the last small slot is padded (`ClayConstantBufferBytes`; case 499, with the count at which the unpadded size ends exactly on a 64 KB step). `MakeClayObjectConstants` refuses the whole block when one of the forty-eight probe components, or any value the colour-stream block was refused for, is not a number of magnitude at most 1,024 (cases 495 to 497), and a record is lit only with the second buffer of its own vertex kind (`LightObjectReady`: an instanced record's colours light nothing; case 498). *The compiled vertex shader, read* (`task8a\disasm\kClayVs.asm`; vs_5_0, the runtime's flags): seven structured-buffer loads. t1, t0 and t2 (the indices, the positions, the UVs) are outside every block, as before. t8 is inside `if_nz` of `(light_mode & 1) && in range && v < light_count`. t9 and t10 are inside `if_nz` of `(light_mode & 2) &&` the same bound. t11 is inside that block and inside a second `if_nz` of `light_mode & 8`, after `umin` of the word with 8; the four constant-buffer reads there are `cb1[r + 5]` to `cb1[r + 8]` with `r` at most 8, inside the seventeen registers the shader declares (`CB1[17], dynamicIndexed`). No `else` side holds a load. The colour stream's power is read in the `else` of the inner block (`cb1[4].w`). Compiled once for each of the sixteen values of `light_mode`, the program loads from exactly the light registers at which `LightBufferSources` has the draw's own buffer (and not from t8 where the object bit is set too, a mode the pass never makes), declares no register of `Object` without the object bit, five (80 bytes, fixed index) with it and all seventeen only with the probe bit, and has the `umin` only with the probe bit (code 160; `task8a\disasm_summary.txt`). No pixel shader loads from a buffer, and the textured one declares five registers of `Object`. *What the attribute does here*: with the text of plan Task 7, taking the two `[branch]` attributes away made the compiler load from t8, t9 and t10 outside every block, the form of the three hung runs; with the present text it keeps every light load inside its test with or without the attributes (`task8a\flat_control.txt`). The attribute stays as the promise in the source, the compiled program is what is held, and the test's controls now put a load outside its test by hand (code 158; one of them, a load as a vertex output's default, the compiler moves into the `else` of the object's test, where a count of blocks does not see it and the program of a draw without light does: the reason the check is made per `light_mode`). *The pairs*: `light_check.py` was run on five pairs that were not in the table, `0x2FD2...` with `0xECD6...` and `0x648B...` / `0x7892...` with the skinned `0xD4D5...` / `0xA1F7...` (400 of 400 trials each, largest relative difference 8.9e-16; with `--multi-sun` every two- and four-light pair of the terrain, object and trunk families, thirteen now, is its one-light function at every slot behind light 0: `task8a\light_check_object.txt`, `light_check_object_multi.txt`, `light_check_multi_sun.txt`); they are entered. Of the five only `0x648B...` with `0xA1F7...` is in a capture so far (2 draws a frame at the third spot). *The debug layer's messages*: `--fable2_native_d3d_messages=true` (off by default) writes the Direct3D debug layer's errors, corruption and warnings to the game log as `[native] d3d ERROR id N (seen k): text` (at most 4 lines per severity and id, 400 in a run) and a count line with every 300th clay frame's lines, `[native] d3d messages: errors E, warnings W`, so that a run under `--d3d12_debug=true` shows a rejected call, or that there was none, without a debugger (`D3dMessageLog`, `render/d3d_messages.cpp`; plan Task 7 had a temporary form of it). *In the game* (runs 324 to 328 of 2026-10-08, made by the controlling agent with the user at the machine, `RUN UNCHECKED`; logs and shots `task8a_*`, the analysis in `task8a\`: `runs_summary_task8a.txt`, `pictures.txt`, `figure_colours.txt`, `third_hero.txt`, `same_programs.txt`). On the software adapter with the debug layer and the message switch (run 324; the user closed the window at 251 s, so there is no shot): the layer's queue was available, the world ran lit for about two minutes (`lit 738 (terrain-layer 492, terrain-far 72, object 144, tree-trunk 30)`), and the layer reported no error and no corruption: `d3d messages: errors 0, warnings 14`, later `15`, all of the two ids plan Task 7's run on that adapter had (1328, a buffer's initial state ignored at its creation; 1008, one resource in two barrier descriptions), neither of which names a root parameter, a view or a shader. So t10 bound from the probe buffer's offset is accepted as it is; the fallback (a buffer of its own for the set indices) was not needed and is not built. On the GPU (runs 325 bridge, 326 third spot, 327 trees, 328 bridge with the light off): no device removal, no skipped record, `Light inputs: ready N of N` with every world rotation a rotation and no refused probe buffer. Lit share of the drawn records: bridge 738 of 921 to 923 (80%; 74% before this task), third spot 766 of 977 to 979 (78%; 70%), trees 721 or 722 of 863 to 866 (83% to 84%; 66%); objects 144 / 161 / 207 or 208 (120 / 133 / 120 before) and trunks 30 / 49 / 68 (none before). The pixel shaders of the object and trunk families are gone from the `unknown` list; what it holds now is the plants (`0xA7E4...`, `0x165E...`, `0xE99F...`, `0x2605...`, `0xF525...`), the leaves (`0x7CD5...`), the blended characters (`0x401A...`) and the water. The pictures. The window of these runs was 1920 x 1080 where every baseline run's was 1280 x 720, so nothing could be compared pixel for pixel: the comparisons are of pictures brought to 1280 x 720, by region means. *What was lit before did not change*: at the bridge and the third spot the regions of plan Task 7 (planks, dirt, hills, far hill, lake, grass, stockade) read 0.997 to 1.005 of their luminance in runs 322 and 315, the same 1.001 to 1.004 the light-off pair of runs reads against run 323 (the resampling's own bias); and compiled with `light_mode` fixed at 0, 1, 5 and 6, each of the five clay shaders is instruction for instruction the program it was before this task (20 of 20 listings identical), so an unlit draw, lit ground and a lit colour-stream object run the code they ran. (That sentence is true of the fixed-mode compiles, which are not what the GPU is given. The whole programs, with the mode a root word, were compared by the review of this task, commit `753e5c0` against `1ea0351`: the four pixel shaders are instruction-identical and the vertex shader differs only inside the object block, after the load from t10; so a draw with the light off and a terrain draw execute the same instructions in the real program too.) At the trees the camera stood about 6 pixels from where run 316's stood (the stick plan under another frame pacing) and the posts' fixed rectangles read 3% to 6% lower: that comparison is not one of like with like, and the trees rest on the identical programs alone. *Light off* (run 328 against run 323): region means 1.001 to 1.004, mean difference outside what moves 1.4 levels where resampling one picture two ways gives 1.0; that it is pixel-equal, as it was in every earlier task, could not be shown with a window of another size. *The newly lit*, against the emulated shot taken four seconds before each lit one. The trunk at the bridge: 1.72 times the planks' luminance while it was unlit, 0.90 lit, 0.99 in the emulated frame; its colour went from pale beige (red : green : blue 1.06 : 1 : 0.78) to the emulated frame's dark grey-green (0.78 : 1 : 0.86 against 0.77 : 1 : 0.81); the trunks by the trees likewise, dark where they were the brightest things in the picture. The hero: at the bridge, in full sun, about as bright as when unlit (shirt 1.52 times the planks against 1.56; emulated 1.85) with the hue now the emulated one (0.89 : 1 : 0.85 against 0.88 : 1 : 0.85; unlit it was 0.89 : 1 : 1.03, too blue); from the front at the third spot his face reads 1.39 times the rail in front of him (1.63 unlit, 1.54 emulated), his trousers 1.01 (1.27; 0.95), the vest 0.81 (0.84; 0.70), the dog's chest 1.69 (2.04; 1.75). No figure, trunk or prop is black, white or of a wrong colour in the three lit shots viewed with their crops: the zero and negative probe colours leave no mark that can be seen. What stays wrong beside them: no shadows (the hero under the trees gets the sun the canopy would take), the plants and leaves unlit and brighter than what is lit, the dog without its fur shells, and the whole lit picture darker than the emulated one (the exposure is 1). *Cost*, within these runs: 30.0 fps in every view at all three spots (frame medians 32.9 to 34.3 ms, the display's pacing; the baseline runs were made in another display state and are not comparable); the clay pass's largest total over 300 frames, once a spot has loaded, 3.0 to 5.4 ms at the bridge, 4.5 to 6.5 at the third spot, 4.7 to 5.0 by the trees, none above its baseline window; the frame's constant buffer 262,144 bytes at all three spots (565 small slots and 174 object slots at the bridge; 196,608 before, with 685 slots of 256 bytes); geometry resident 39.3 MB at the bridge (35.9 in run 322, and 39.3 in the light-off run of this build too; the third spot's and the trees' runs read 36.4 and 36.5 MB at the same place in their first window, so it is no cost of this task and it is not explained), 45.9 MB at the third spot (45.7 after plan Task 5b), 76.1 MB by the trees (76.8). The shader test's executable is built as `native_shaders_task8a.exe` on the development machine until a file its antivirus restored is deleted (`tests\run_native_tests.cmd` itself is unchanged).

**Plants** (plan Task 8b, 2026-10-08; run in the game on 2026-10-08: "In the game" at the end of this paragraph). The instanced plants (ferns, grass, flowers, bushes: seven vertex shaders of kind `instance`) are lit in two families, `plant` and `plant-lit`, each with its two-light form. Evidence: `task8b\`. *What the game computes*, read in `0x8123C16DBF583F92` and checked by machine for all seven vertex shaders with instance rows that are no rotation (`plant_colour_check.py`, `plant_bend_check.py`, 400 trials each, every shader 400 of 400; and `plant_normal_check.py` of plan Task 5b for the normal). (1) The colour of the vertex's copy (the 8_8_8_8 element of the instance stream, channels z, y, x of the fetch: instruction 17) is raised to vertex `c18.w` as it is, through the logarithm of its absolute value (26 to 32), and multiplied by `c18.xyz`; the three shaders paired with the pixel shaders that have no ambient factor add `c54.xyz` (33: `mad r7, r7, c18, c54`) and export the whole ambient (`0x8123...` and `0xFC4F...` in interpolator `o4`, `0x48D3...` in `o3`); the four paired with the pixel shaders that have the factor export the product without the added light in `o7` and the factor's vector `lerp(N, c19, (1 + N . c19) / 2)` in `o5`. No other power: not 2.2 times `c18.w`, not `c18.w` over 2.2 (both are wrong candidates the check tells apart by 0.55 and more). (2) The normal `N = normalize(M n)` of the copy's rows ("Normals", "The transform"). (3) The bend of the normal: the height blend `h = sat(z * c45.y + c45.z)` of the mesh vertex's third position component in the copy's space (38: `mad_sat r1.w, r0.x, c45.y, c45.z`), the copy's up axis `U`, which is the third COLUMN of the rows' 3 x 3, normalised (the three squares and their sum: 40 to 42, 45, 46; the reciprocal root: 48; the three products: 49, 51), `bent = normalize(lerp(N, U, h))` (53, 55, 56, 59, 60), and the export `(c45.x * bent, c45.x * h)` (61; `o3` in `0x8123...` and `0xFC4F...`, `o2` in `0x48D3...`, `o6` in the four others). All seven compute it in this one form: the third row in the place of the third column, an axis that is not normalised, another position component, a blend that is not saturated and a lerp that is not normalised each differ from the microcode by 0.49 to 8.4 over the same trials, and with `c45.x` = 0 the interpolator is (0, 0, 0, 0) in every trial: such a set does not bend. The pixel shaders (`0xA7E4...` 11 to 26) normalise the interpolated normal, blend it towards the bend's direction by `sat` of its fourth component, normalise again, and compute `A * amb + A * c87 * sat(Np . c80) * mask` (`plant`) or the object form with that normal and the vertex side's colour (`plant-lit`, where `t = sat(normalize(axis) . Np)`: the vector of the factor is made from the UNBENT normal, the dot product is with the bent one). *The vertex side's constants are the frame's*: vertex `c18` is (pixel `c21.xyz`, 2.2 x pixel `c21.w` as a float) bit for bit in all 1,080 and 608 main-scene rows of the seven shaders in the two captures whose rows carry the followed vertex registers (`task1_bridge3_capture`, `task1_trees2_capture`; `vertex_copies_8b.txt`), and vertex `c54` is pixel `c20`, all four components, in all 688 and 376 rows of the three shaders that read it; the GPU's own values say the same at 18,840 + 14,040 and 20,572 + 31,528 draws ("The vertex side"). So the block gives the tint, the exponent (times `kInstanceColourPower` = 2.2), the added light and the axis; an observation of two scenes, not a rule read from the game. And every plant row of the three captures of plan Task 8a's runs has the frame's block in its own pixel registers (`c20`, `c21`, `c22`, for `plant-lit` `c23`, the sun's direction and colour; 1,080, 1,208 and 584 rows, none disagrees: `plant_rows_check.txt`). *The bend constants* `c45` are the draw's, from the device's vertex bank: the bank equals the followed value at `c45` in all 1,688 rows above (the registers where it does not are the light set's and the literals). Values seen: (0, 0, 0, 0) in 472 of the bridge capture's 1,080 plant rows (504 of 1,208 at the third spot, 280 of 584 by the trees), else (1, -200, 100, 0), (1, -134, 100, 0), (1, -100, 100, 0), (1, -381.6, 100, 0) for `plant` and (1, 141.4, 2.775, 0), (1, -25.63, 79.56, 0), (1, -42.40, 78.70, 0) for `plant-lit`: steep ramps, so most of a bending plant is either fully bent or not at all. *The pairs.* Thirteen: `0xA7E4...` with `0x8123...` and `0xFC4F...`, `0x2605...` with `0x48D3...`, `0xE99F...` with `0x8123...` and `0xFC4F...`, `0x165E...` with `0xB636...`, `0x6AD4...`, `0x36B5...`, `0x33C0...`, `0xF525...` with `0xB636...`, `0x6AD4...`, `0x33C0...` (these twelve were in the table since plan Task 4; each is in the bridge capture of run 325) and `0xF525...` with `0x36B5...`, which the third spot's capture of run 326 draws once a frame and which had no family: run and entered now. `light_check.py` on all thirteen: 400 of 400 trials each, largest relative difference 1.8e-15 (`light_check_plants.txt`). *The two-light forms.* In all 200, 360 and 136 plant `-multi` rows of the three captures `c112` is one-hot at slot 1, the light there is the frame's sun (`w` = 0, `c94` = 0, direction and colour equal to the frame row's block) and light 0 is a lantern (`plant_rows_check.txt`); `light_check.py --multi-sun`, extended to the plant families for this task, runs each of the six pairs with that light set against the family's one-light function: 400 of 400 at slot 1 (`light_check_multi_sun.txt`; the check fails for the plant pairs too when a lantern is lit, the mask is on the lantern, the sun has a cone or is a position: `tests/test_light_check.py`, `MultiSun`). So the six are drawn with the frame's sun through the one-light function, without their lantern, as the other families' are. *As drawn.* Vertex stage: under `(light_mode & 18) == 18` (the object bit and the instance bit) and the vertex bound, the normal from t9 as it is (no rows: the flat normals are in the world already, and the block is exclusive of the object's, whose test is now `(light_mode & 18) == 2`), the copy's colour from t10, the bend inputs (`U.xyz`, `z`) from t11, `o.bend = PlantBend(n, U, PlantHeight(z, c45.y, c45.z), c45.x)`, and by family `InstanceAmbient(colour, tint, 2.2 * c21.w, add)` with no vector, or `InstanceAmbient(colour, tint, 2.2 * c21.w, 0)` with `AmbientAxis(n, axis)`. The bend is a seventh interpolator (`float4 bend : TEXCOORD6`, the vertex shader's last output and the textured pixel shader's last input; every draw that is no plant writes zeros to it). Pixel stage (the textured shader, under `light_mode` bit 4 inside its lit branch): `Np = PlantNormal(normal, bend)`, then `LightPlant(A, vcolour, Np . sun, sun colour, 1)` or `LightPlantLit(A, vcolour, add, floor, AmbientT(axis, Np), Np . sun, sun colour, 1)`; `A` is the albedo squared after its division by the alpha, as for every textured draw; no `c26`, `c27` or `c49` (these shaders have none). The mirrors (`InstanceAmbient`, `PlantHeight`, `PlantBend`, `PlantNormal`, `LightPlant`, `LightPlantLit` in `clay_logic.h`) are pinned to `light_formulas.py` (`instance_ambient`, `plant_normal`, `plant`, `lit_object`) on a bent, an unbent and a half-bent normal, half the strength, `c45.x` = 0 and a negative strength (no bend), an instance colour of 0 (the added light and the sun remain), a zero normal (bent: the up axis; unbent: no direction, no sun, `t` = 0) and a copy without an up axis (cases 500 to 508; `PinnedForTheRenderer`, `test_plant`, `test_plant_lit`, `test_plant_zero_inputs`). *The bend inputs* are a buffer of the geometry cache, one `float4` per flat position (`ExpandInstanceBend`, `GeometryCache::InstanceBend`, key `InstanceBendKey`, kind 14: the mesh's position stream with its layout and the instance set as the flat normals have it, not its offset; content hash of the two streams): the up axis of the position's copy (zero for a copy whose third column has no direction: none is made up) and the vertex's height as it is. A height that is not a number in a vertex the draw names refuses the whole buffer (`value`); an entry without a position (an index the constants do not map, a vertex past the mesh, a copy past the stream) is zero. A plant record is ready, and lit, only with its normals, its copies' colours AND its bend inputs (`LightObjectReady`); a refusal is counted with the probe and instance colour refusals, and the `Light inputs:` line ends with `| bend inputs: N records, X MB` (the buffers' bytes; 16 a flat position). Expected from the flat positions of a frame (four times the instance colours' bytes of plan Task 5b's count): about 4.0 MB at the bridge, 4.5 MB at the third spot, 2.9 MB by the trees. *Registers*: no new one (the layout is full: twelve parameters). `LightBufferSources` gives a plant its copies' colours at t10 and its bend inputs at t11 (`ClayLightBuffer::kInstanceColours`, `kBend`), both from byte 0; the instance bit decides before the probe bit, as in the shader. *Constants*: a plant has no rows, so its three bend constants ride in the fourth components of the three rows of cbuffer `Object` (zero for every object and trunk), and `o_colour_power` holds 2.2; everything its shader path reads lies in the block's first 80 bytes (`kClayPlantConstantBytes`), and the pixel stage reads none of it. So a lit plant takes a SMALL slot (256 bytes) among the frame's and the terrain's (`ClaySmallSlotOffset`), not a 512-byte one. The frame's buffer, by arithmetic from the counts of runs 325 to 327: bridge 565 + 135 small slots and 174 object slots, 268,288 bytes, allocated 327,680 (262,144 before); third spot 557 + 152 and 210, 289,024, allocated 327,680; trees 447 + 73 and 276, 274,432, allocated 327,680: one 64 KB step more at each, far below the pool's 4 MB. `MakeClayObjectConstants` refuses a plant's block as a whole on a bend constant that is not a number of magnitude at most 1,024 and carries nothing else of the inputs (cases 509 to 512). *The compiled shaders, read* (`task8b\disasm\`, `programs_8b.txt`; vs_5_0 / ps_5_0, the runtime's flags). The vertex shader has ten structured-buffer loads. t1, t0 and t2 are outside every block, as before. The vertex is compared with `light_count` by `ult r, v, cb0[8].z`, and the mode's bits 0 and 18 are taken by one `and`; the terrain's block is under `if_nz` of bit 0 and the bound and holds the one load of t8; the object's block is under `if_nz` of `(mode & 18) == 2` and the bound (`ieq ..., l(.., 2, 18)`) and holds one load of t9, one of t10 and, inside its second `if_nz` of bit 3, after `umin` with the literal 8, the load of t11; the plant's block is under `if_nz` of `(mode & 18) == 18` and the bound and holds the three loads of t9, t10 and t11, the `mad_sat` with `cb1[1].w` and `cb1[2].w`, the product with `cb1[0].wwww` into the bend's output, and the exponent `cb2[1].w * cb1[4].w`. No load is outside its block, and no `else` side holds one; the `else` of the plant's block writes the zero bend. Compiled once for each of the sixty-four values of `light_mode`, the vertex program loads from exactly the light registers at which `LightBufferSources` has the draw's own buffer, of the kind whose path it takes; declares no register of the slot at b1 without the object bit, seventeen (indexed) for a probe object and five (fixed index) for a stream object and for a plant, which reads the three fourth components and the power and no row; has the `umin` with 8 for a probe object alone, a power for a stream object and a plant alone, the comparison with `light_count` wherever it loads a light buffer, and writes the bend from its inputs for a plant alone and zeros for every other mode; the textured pixel program loads from no buffer, reads the slot at b1 for a lit object or trunk alone (five registers) and never for a plant, declares the bend's input for a lit plant alone, and is the same program for every mode with the same lit, instance and plant-lit bits (codes 155 to 161). The `[branch]` attributes are on the plant's vertex block, on its family test and on the pixel shader's plant test (the pixel shader's family test is a plain `if`, which the compiler makes a select: with the attribute on both, the compile with the mode fixed fails, error X3524, because the folded outer test leaves its attribute on the inner one). *Against the parent commit* (`1ea0351`; `programs_8b.txt`). With `light_mode` fixed at each value the pass made before this task (0, 1, 5, 6, 14): the flat, textured, layer and far pixel programs are line for line the parent's (20 of 20 listings); the vertex program differs in exactly two lines at each of the five values, `dcl_output o7.xyzw` and `mov o7.xyzw, l(0,0,0,0)`, the bend's output and its zero: the new interpolator is the one thing a draw of the old kinds gets, and it is why "line for line" does not hold for the vertex stage. The whole programs (the mode a root word): the flat, layer and far pixel shaders are identical; the vertex shader and the textured pixel shader differ in most lines as the compiler prints them, because it numbers its temporaries anew, so they were compared in a form that leaves the choice of register and component out (each read named by how many lines up its value was written; four-component operands cut to the components used; operands of order-free instructions sorted). In that form the vertex shader's terrain block, the object's block with the stream colour and the probe colour, and everything before them are the parent's lines but for: the mode tests (the object's is `(mode & 18) == 2` where it was `mode & 2`, and the default normal's select takes `mode & 2` by an instruction of its own), three loads and three moves that read the vertex index or a value from more lines up than before, and the stream colour's bytes converted by two `utof` instructions where there was one; new are the bend's output, the plant's block and the zero bend in its `else`. The textured pixel shader: new are the bend's input, the test of bit 4 and the plant's path; the object's path is the parent's lines (now in the `else` of that test) but for four reads from more lines up. *Tests*: `test_normal_decode.cpp` cases 400 to 413 (`ExpandInstanceBend`), `test_clay_logic.cpp` cases 459, 467, 485 to 489, 498 (changed on purpose: plants are lit now) and 500 to 517, `test_native_shaders.cpp` codes 31, 80, 82, 83, 98, 99, 155, 157, 158, 160, 161, 163 to 165 (the pins hold the plants' functions, the vertex block and the pixel path; twelve more controls), `tests/test_light_check.py` (`MultiSun` with the six plant pairs, `PinnedForTheRenderer`). Mutation run (`mutate_8b.py`; every mutant applied to a copy, the real test built from it): `clay_logic.h` 83 of 83 (two survived the first run and got their cases: the ambient's result not made finite, the normal not normalised before the pixel side's blend), `ExpandInstanceBend` 20 of 20, the checker and the tables 11 of 11, the shaders, the pins and the layout as the shader test sees them 49 of 49 (one survived the first run and got its check: sources of the probe kind where the shader takes the plant's path). *In the game* (2026-10-08, runs 329 to 333, made by the controller with the user at the machine: `RUN UNCHECKED`; logs, shots and driver output `task8b_<name>_*` in `out\native-evidence\lighting\`, the files named here in `task8b\`). No run lost its device, none has a `d3d ERROR` or `CORRUPTION` line or a window with the freeze signature; run 329, on the software adapter with the debug layer, reads `errors 0, warnings 14` after `lit 873 (... plant 86, plant-lit 49)`. Lit share of the drawn records: bridge 873 of 921 to 923 (95%; 80% before), third spot 917 of 976 (94%; 78%), trees 795 of 863 to 867 (92%; 83 to 84%); `Light inputs: ready N of N` in every line; `bend inputs:` 135 records 3.9 MB, 152 records 4.5 MB, 73 records 2.9 MB (`runs_summary_task8b.txt`). Still unlit: the leaf cards `0x7CD5...` (22 / 35 / 41 draws), `0x401A...`, the water `0xF6D9...` and a few small ones. Light off: run 333 against run 328, 0 pixels differ outside what moves, at 42 s and at 74 s (`off_compare_333_328.txt`). What was lit before: at the bridge and under the trees the lit shots equal plan Task 8a's pixel for pixel outside the plants (bridge: 2.2% and 2.3% of the client area differ by more than 2 levels, which is the grass, the ferns, the bushes and the dog, while planks, dirt, hills, lake, trunk and the tree's leaves differ in 0.0%; trees: post tops and wall 0.0%; `pictures_8b.txt` and the pictures `where_8b_8a_*.png`, looked at). At the third spot the walk ends a little elsewhere than in run 326, and the debug window is open in the shots of runs 331 and 332, so there only region means outside it compare (planks 0.999, stockade 0.995, lake 0.993 of run 326's). The plants themselves change little in the mean: luminance of the lit picture over plan Task 8a's on the changed pixels has median 1.04 to 1.06, 5th percentile 0.70 to 0.76 and 95th 1.13 to 1.14, and none is near black or white (`plant_pixels_8b.txt`); the unlit picture drew a plant at 0.75 to 1 of its albedo, and most plants are lit from above. Against the emulated shots they stay darker by about the factor the ground beside them does (bridge, of 255: grass strip 67.5 against 81.7, dirt 87.7 against 129.8, planks 49.6 against 63.4; the emulated picture has the post-processing the native one has not). Replay (`plant_replay_8b.py`, `plant_raster_8b.py` and their outputs): every vertex of the 135 plant rows of the bridge capture and of the 73 of the trees capture went through the game's own vertex microcode and the family's formula, and the result was held against the lit shot's pixel over plan Task 8a's at the same place (the two differ by the unlit shade, so the ratio is predicted to lie in 1 to 1.333 and not to depend on how much sun the replay gives the pixel). Where a draw is the nearest plant and the replayed sun factor is above 0.25 that holds: trees, sets that do not bend, 134,005 pixels, 1.15 / 1.08 / 1.08 / 1.07 from the least sun to the most; bridge 1.19 / 1.07 / 1.07 / 1.03 (3,187 pixels) and, for the sets that bend, 1.20 / 1.05 / 1.07 / 1.11 (35,410 pixels). **Not confirmed**: the pixels where the replay has almost no sun (factor below 0.25: 2,480 pixels at the trees, 1,013 at the bridge), where the picture is 1.3 to 1.8 times the replay, and small dense clumps, which do not follow the replay (correlation near 0). A card's cut-away texture and a second card on the same place facing the other way would both do that, and the replay has neither the texture nor the cull state: an inference, not shown. (Corrected after the review of this task and plan Task 9b. The cull state IS in the captures: every plant row has `rs` `2205` = `0x00218006`, cull back with front clockwise, and the native pass draws with it; the game neither flips nor wraps a plant's normal. What the replay lacked was registration: it points at the wrong pixel where the wind, which the pass does not have, has moved the plant. Fern stems fit the picture at a steady shift of about 8 to 17 pixels with measured over predicted 1.15 to 1.27, and of the ten largest bright blobs by the trees, with the alpha test applied, three are cut-away texture, four fit at a shift of 17 to 20 pixels and three, 363 pixels, are unexplained (`task9b\`). And one thing seen that is no fault of the replay: under the trees the lit fern stems go dark, darker than the game's. Their normals point along the stem, away from the sun, and the game brightens them with what this pass does not draw: the mask's soft edge, in-scatter and the post chain; inference from the pictures.) Cost: 30.0 fps in every view after loading in all four runs on the graphics card; the pass's largest total over 300 frames 3.5 to 4.7 ms at the bridge, 5.1 to 7.3 ms at the third spot, 4.9 to 5.5 ms under the trees (plan Task 8a: 3.0 to 5.4, 4.5 to 6.5, 4.7 to 5.0); geometry resident 43.2 / 54.3 / 89.9 MB (39.3 / 45.9 / 76.1). **Open**: in run 329's one shot (software adapter, 135 s) the dog is pure red (red 162 to 254, green and blue 0) while the rest of the picture is as on the graphics card, where the dog looks as in plan Task 8a's shots; there is no earlier shot from the software adapter to hold it against, and the cause is not known.

**Tree leaves** (plan Task 8c, 2026-10-08). The leaf cards of the trees (pixel shader `0x7CD5...` with the vertex shaders `0xA584...`, `0xD7DD...`, `0x2D40...`: one, two and four lights; 22, 35 and 41 draws a frame at the three spots, the largest unlit group that was left) are lit in one family, `tree-leaf`. Evidence: `task8c\`. *What the game computes* (`lighting-formulas.md`, "Tree leaves"; instruction numbers of `0xA584...`). Everything but the texture and the screen mask is the VERTEX shader's: the normal through the rows `c4..c6`, times `c7.w`, not normalised (83, 87, 95, 96), and negated where it faces away from the eye `c9` (the predicate of 108 to 110); the ambient `pow(|probe colour|, c18.w * 0.4545) * c18.xyz + c54.xyz` of the probe colour the trunks have (115 to 117, 122; the power through the logarithm of the absolute value: 124, 126 to 132; interpolator `o1`); and per light two scalars times the light's colour: `front = sat((L . N + c50.w) / (1 + c50.w)) * spot` (`o2`) and `back = sat(-(L . N)) * (1 - (1 - sat(V . N))^2) * spot` (`o3`), V the unit vector to the eye, `spot` the light's cone and range. The pixel shader adds them on the albedo squared (divided by its alpha squared): `(A * (o1 * c27.w + m1 * o2) + green * A * m2 * o3) * c49`, `green` 1 where the texel's green is at least its red (the back light passes through leaf texels, not through twigs), `m1 = 0.6 * mask + 0.4`, `m2 = 0.6 * m1 + 0.4`; then `c26` with the output scale. So there is no translucency term beyond that back light, no wrap but `c50.w`, and one power. *The cull state* (the review of plan Task 8b asked): register 0x2205 is `0x00218000` in every main-scene leaf row of four captures (176, 328, 176, 328 rows), no culling, where every trunk row and every plant row has `0x00218006` (cull back, front clockwise; `leaf_cull.txt`): a card is drawn from both sides and the shader turns the normal to the viewer, so the side he sees is lit as its own front. The native pass draws with the captured state and turns the normal the same way, per vertex. *The vertex side's light set* is the game's own registers `c76..c107`, which the device's vertex bank does not hold; the two captures of plan Task 1 whose rows carry the followed vertex registers do (`task1_bridge3_capture`, `task1_trees2_capture`; `leaf_rows_check.txt`): at all 176 and 328 main-scene leaf rows the frame's sun stands in the set bit for bit (`c(76 + s).xyz` its direction, `w` = 0; `c(83 + s).xyz` its colour; `s` = 0, 1, 2 for one, two and four lights, in every row), `c90` is 0 at `s` (no cone, no range: `spot` = 1), every slot before `s` is a lantern (`w` = 1, `c90` = 1), vertex `c9.xyz` is pixel `c19.xyz`, `c18` is (pixel `c21.xyz`, 2.2 x pixel `c21.w` as a float), `c54` is pixel `c20`, all bit for bit; `c50` is (1, 100, 1, 0.4); pixel `c27`, `c49`, `c26` are ones. So the frame's block gives the sun, the eye, the tint, the exponent and the added light; observations of two daylight scenes of one area, not a rule read from the game. *The check.* `light_check.py` now runs all three pairs with the shaders' own literal tables (`"vs_lit"` / `"ps_lit"` of those captures: `leaf_literals.txt`; pixel `c255` = (1, 0, 0.4, 0.6); the 1 / 2.2 is `c249.w`, `c248.w`, `c255.x` in the three vertex shaders): families `tree-leaf` and `tree-leaf-multi`, 400 of 400 trials each, largest relative difference 5.8e-16 (`light_check_leaves.txt`); `--multi-sun`: with the game's set the two- and four-light pairs are the ONE-light function of the sun, 400 of 400 at every slot (`light_check_multi_sun.txt`), and not with a lantern lit, a cone on the sun or the sun as a position. *The tables.* One entry: `0x7CD5...` is `tree-leaf` with the three vertex shaders (`FABLE2_PS_LIGHT(..., 7, 0, 0.0f)`); the family has no `-multi` form there, because the lights are the vertex shader's and the pixel shader is one program (the generator refuses `tree-leaf-multi`). The three vertex shaders are of kind `probe` (normal fetch 1, weights fetch 6, the set in the position's source z, scale `c7.w`). The tables hold 21 pixel shaders, 18 vertex shaders and 40 pairs, exactly `FAMILIES`' (37 before). The vertex shader's three mesh blocks are exclusive siblings: the object's under `(light_mode & 82) == 2`, the plant's under `(light_mode & 82) == 18`, the leaf's under `(light_mode & 90) == 74`, each with the vertex bound (82: the object, instance and leaf bits; 90: those and the probe bit). Constant buffer, by arithmetic: inside the 327,680 bytes at all three spots. *Two limits of the leaf path* (from the review of this task, its measurements): (1) the vector to the eye is formed from the unswayed position where the game uses the swayed one: over 3,300 leaf vertices of the bridge no vertex's turn changed, and the back scalar differs by more than 0.05 in 0.03% of them; (2) the cache's normals are normalised where the game puts the element through the rows as it is stored: the difference is at most 0.2% of the normal's length.

**The base map.** tf3, the region's baked light (one 768 x 768 DXT1 texture for all 492 layer records and 59 of the 75 far records of a bridge frame, four smaller ones for the other far records; clamped, linear filter), is resolved through the texture cache like the other terrain textures, only in a lit frame and only for a record whose light inputs, normals and `base_valid` inputs are there. Its coordinate is `world.xy * base_uv.xy + base_uv.zw` from the inputs kept since the materials sub-project, scaled into the host texture; its sampler is the one its fetch constant asks for; it is fetched with explicit derivatives, formed outside the light's branch. A record whose base map is not usable this frame (not resolved, over the upload budget, a format the cache does not decode) is not lit. **A ground square is lit as a whole or not at all**: `TerrainPlanItem` carries a light flag, in "can be lit", out "is lit", and `PlanTerrain`, after it has decided which records keep their material, marks a square unlit when one layer drawn with its material in it cannot be lit, ties squares through a layer draw of several patches as it does for the material, and takes the light from every layer of an unlit square. That was added to the plan's own pass rather than made a second fallback of the material: an unlit square keeps its material. A draw of the adaptive builder is lit or not by itself; where a lit underlay fades into an unlit square the two differ across the ring of the cross-fade (counted as `light-unknown`, not hidden).

**What an unlit draw looks like beside lit ones.** The unlit linear colour of the materials picture, unchanged: the albedo with the facet shade, squared. The spec's table had "the frame's ambient with the baked term 1 and L = 1" for such draws, `A * (c21.xyz + c20.xyz)`. Measured with the block of the bridge capture (`task7\lit_object_survey.py`, `lit_object_survey_bridge.txt`: the object function with `A` = 1 on every vertex of the 120 colour-stream object draws of a frame, 295,717 vertices, not weighted by area): the mean light factor of a lit object is (0.343, 0.401, 0.345), luminance 0.385, of which the sun is 0.209 (half of the vertices face it); the plain albedo is the factor 1, 2.6 times that; the frame ambient with baked term 1 is (1.131, 1.459, 1.982), luminance 1.43, 3.7 times that and blue. Real baked terms are far below 1, so that form is the brightest ambient there could be. For the ground (`terrain_lit_unlit_means.txt`, four replayed squares): lit against unlit luminance 1.20 and 1.00 on the two flat squares in the sun, 0.81 and 0.70 on the two that hold a bank facing away from it. So the plain albedo is the less conspicuous of the two: as bright as lit ground in the sun, and brighter than a lit object by 1.6 times as displayed. It is still visible, and it will be until the families of plan Tasks 5b and 8 are lit.

**The facet shade** is a display-space factor and stays inside the square for an unlit draw. A lit draw has none: its light is the game's, and the shade would shade it a second time. The light multiplies the linear colour, outside the square (`LightObject(clay_linear(albedo), ...)`, never `clay_linear(albedo * light)`).

**What a lit draw may write.** Lit values exceed 1 (a lit value is its albedo squared times up to about 2.4 with the captured block), so the clamp at 1 is gone for them and the mapping clamps after the exposure. What is kept is `clay_lit`: a NaN and a negative value give 0 by a comparison and a mask, and the value is at most 64 (`kClayLitMax`). The bound is what keeps an infinity out of the target, from which a blend factor of zero would make a NaN that stays: 1,008 blended draws of 64 over one pixel are still below 64,512, the largest value of the target's 10-bit channel, and a frame has about 500 blended draws in all. The compiled shaders keep the comparison, the mask and the bound (code 69). An unlit draw keeps its clamps to [0, 1] exactly as they were, and the lit branch is a real branch on `light_mode`, so with the light off the shaders execute the statements of the linear-target build. Alpha is never lit, never squared, and clamped only where it is written.

**Rounding.** The target is `R11G11B10_FLOAT`, and this GPU rounds toward zero when it stores (review of plan Task 6): every blend loses up to 1/64 of the value in red and green and 1/32 in blue, always downward. A ground square is the sum of about five blended layers, so a lit square reads darker than the formula's sum by up to a few such steps; a comparison of a native shot with the replay has to allow for it (the replay computes in double precision).

**Smaller things changed with it.** (1) The light buffers of a mesh record have to hold the vertices its indices name, its largest vertex plus one (`LightVertexNeed`, the capture's own rule for the streams), no longer every vertex of the position stream: meshes share streams, and a colour stream ends where its last mesh ends. (2) A terrain record's light inputs are counted (`Light inputs: ready R of L`) after the plan, when it is known that the record keeps its material. (3) The comment on `kMirrored`: for an orthonormal matrix the inverse transpose is the matrix, sign included.

**The Light line** (F3's sixth line; `[native] clay: Light: ...` every 300 frames): `Light: on, block valid, lit N (terrain-layer a, terrain-far b, object c, tree-trunk d, plant e, plant-lit f), unlit U {light-unknown: u, normal-unsupported: v}, unknown {0x<pixel shader>: n, ...}, sun (x, y, z) colour (r, g, b)`; `block missing` and `unlit U {light-block: U}` for a frame without a block; `Light: off` with `unlit U {light-off: U}`.

*The red dog on the software adapter* (`task7\warp_dog.py`, `warp_dog.txt`, `warp_dog_x4.png`). In that run's one shot (280 s, native view) the dog is a flat red silhouette; in the GPU run's shots it is the dark textured dog of every earlier native shot. Measured: 5,124 pixels, red 231 to 238 of 255 for nine tenths of them (median 235), green and blue exactly 0 in 96% (the rest is the edge). The dog's body is `0xD4D5...` with pixel shader `0x8D90...`: not lit in this task (it has no colour stream: counted under `light-unknown`, 20 draws of that pixel shader in both runs), so it goes through the unlit textured statement, `display = t.rgb * (0.75 + 0.25 * facet)`; for a texel of exactly (1, 0, 0) and the flat screen normal of a small near object that is (235.7, 0, 0). So the pixel shader ran its ordinary unlit path and the texture gave pure red: no light input is involved (codes 160 to 162), its t8 / t9 / t10 hold its own positions and are not loaded from (codes 155, 156; case 485), and the same statement draws the hero, who looks the same in both runs (0.07% of his box differs by more than 32 levels, the sun of the two runs being a different one). What differs between the adapters is therefore the texture's content in guest memory, and that fits what the texture is: the dog's 512 x 512 texture (`0x15270000`, DXT1) is not a file image, the game renders the dog's and the hero's skin on the GPU and the emulator reads the result back into guest memory (`plans\hero-dog-texture-readback.md`; without the readback both are black, and a readback of the wrong moment gave "the red / constantly-shifting dog" there, in the emulated picture, long before this renderer). It is the one input of the native picture that is produced by the adapter and not by the game's CPU code. **Inference, not verified**: the run has no emulated shot, so it is not shown that the emulated dog was red too. It would be shown by one more run on the software adapter with a shot in each view (the task's report has the line); nothing in the native pass was changed for it.

*Note of 2026-10-10 (post sub-project, Task 8b; ledger ruling 30).* The fit below, the criteria's table and the region tables after it (the dirt patch at 1.00, the six sunlit regions, "one exposure for the three spots") are of the base map tf3 read as stored, with an ambient 1.8 to 2.5 times the game's on lit ground. They no longer describe the picture since commit `5d0f974`, and the exposure is not fitted again: section 17, "The base map's gamma sign" ("Runs", item 7: the dirt patch at 0.83 with post off).

**The exposure.** `kLitExposure` = 2.22 (`clay_logic.h`), fitted once on the region "dirt patch" at the bridge from run 341's three shots: mean linear luminance (the square of the display value) 0.32914 and 0.33498 in the emulated shots before and after, 0.14926 in the native shot between them, ratio 0.4495, so 2.2248; the two emulated shots are 1.8% apart, and two decimals are kept (`task9\e1_regions_bridge_341.txt`). Taken on red, green or blue alone it would be 2.30, 2.20, 1.97. Measured back with the calibrated binary (run 344): the dirt patch reads 0.997 of the emulated mean. Run 344's native shots are run 341's with every level times `sqrt(2.22)`: 99.9% of the pixels within two levels, mean 1.0001 (`task9\pictures_9.txt`); nothing else changed. In the binary of this section (plan Task 9's) the exposure was the output mapping's factor and therefore also scaled what is not lit: the clear colour, so the undrawn sky of a lit frame showed levels (30, 30, 37) where an unlit frame shows (20, 20, 25); and every unlit draw inside a lit frame, 1.49 times its former display value: clean water of the lake, flat and unlit, read (216, 207, 187) in run 344 where it read (145, 139, 125) in run 341 and with the light off, and the unlit left mountain at the third spot (230, 220, 199) where it read (154, 147, 134) (the whole-branch review's measurements). This was a defect, not a property to be left: fixed in the final fix wave ("After the review: the fix wave" below), since which the exposure multiplies the lit draws' values only. (As first written this paragraph gave the lake as (140, 138, 119) against (94, 92, 80): those figures are wrong, the rectangle they were measured on, `task9\pictures_9.py` line 28, being half rock.) At 2.22 a channel exceeds 1 and is clamped in 0.004% (bridge), 0.05% (third) and 0.15% (trees) of a native picture's pixels (`task9\grass_pole_341.txt`).

- *The grass rectangle was corrected, and why.* The first rectangle, [0.215, 0.515, 0.285, 0.545], straddles the edge of a leaf shadow that moves: in the emulated shots its left half is dark, and its eighths from left to right change by -51%, -25%, -10%, +57%, +29%, +10%, +12%, +17% between 36 s and 44 s, while the native picture is even across it (`task9\grass_pole_341.txt`, crop `tri_bridge_341_grass.png`). Native over emulated is 2.25 over the darker 65% of it and 1.07 over the brighter 35%. The draws there are lit instanced plants over terrain (`task9\which_draws_bridge_341.txt`). The corrected rectangle, [0.252, 0.527, 0.285, 0.548], is the clump in the sun at the first one's lower right, chosen once from the crop before its ratio was computed; the dark part is the new shadowed region "grass in leaf shadow". Its emulated shots still differ by 9.5%, so it is weaker evidence than the other five. A strip of grass left of the dirt patch, not in the file, reads 1.06 with hue -1.1 at exposure 1 times 2.2248.
- *The other sunlit regions.* Third spot: planks 1.015 (hue +0.4, drift +1.4%); grass by the palisade 1.117 (drift -16.6%); green log 1.062 (drift -8.1%); red log 1.268 (hue +1.0, drift +11.2%): not within 25%; it stands under a tree and its emulated shots are not steady. Trees: the cut faces of the left stump, the post and the right stump 0.899, 0.892, 0.829 (hue within 1.3, drift +1.5 to +2.4%): the emulated faces carry a glow the native picture has not (bloom, inference from the picture). Bridge: the rope pole's sunlit side 0.733 with hue -22.0: not within, see next.
- *The rope pole.* Draw `0xFF672A94` of run 341's capture, `0xECD6...` with `0x8D90...`: family `object`, one light, lit; its bool word has neither `b133` nor `b134`, so no emissive or cube-map term is missing; the native form leaves out its normal map and specular term. The pole is thin and stands before the bright haze over the far hills, and the emulated picture is blurred there. A fit of the emulated colour as a x native + b x the emulated background beside the pole (three channels, two unknowns) gives a = 0.85, b = 0.17 with a residual of 0.3% per channel on the sunlit side, a = 0.84, b = 0.03 and under 1% on the averted side, and without the background's share the emulated hue is 51.5 against the native 52.3. Lower on the same pole, before a dark background ([0.302, 0.44, 0.310, 0.50]), run 344 reads 1.004 with hue -1.5 (`task9\regions_bridge_344_first_grass.txt`). So the 0.73 and the 22 degrees are, by inference from the fit and that control, the game's blur mixing the background in (the post chain), not the light.
- *One exposure for the three spots.* The nine sunlit regions on solid surfaces whose emulated shots agree within 5% (five at the bridge, the third spot's planks, three cut faces by the trees) asked for 2.00 to 2.68 each alone at exposure 1 (largest over smallest 1.34); with 2.22 they measure 0.83 to 1.11: bridge 0.95 to 1.11, third spot 1.02, trees 0.83 to 0.90. One number serves them within the criterion; the trees' cut faces sit about 16% under the bridge's regions. By channel no common tint: red, green and blue of the nine are within 0.77 to 1.21 of the emulated, hue within 5.1 degrees.

*Criterion 5, the pairs (emulated ratio a over b, native ratio):* bridge rope pole (sunlit over averted side) 3.60, 3.03; bridge railing post (cap over side) 2.74, 3.09; third spot tall post 3.54, 1.93; small post (cap over side) 1.80, 1.96; trees left stump (top over side) 19.9, 17.1; post 30.2, 20.9; right stump 20.5, 12.6. The same member is brighter in all seven. Steady in the emulated shots: the rope pole and the three by the trees; the railing post and the third spot's two lie under moving leaf shadow (drift 19 to 160%). *The light-off control, and what the criterion is worth* (the whole-branch review; run 347's native shot, light off, against its own emulated shot): with the light OFF both bridge pairs also read "same side brighter": rope pole 1.47, railing post 1.50; the unlit picture has the facet shade and the texture, which is enough for a sign. And the three pairs by the trees compare a cut face of pale wood with bark, so their ratio is mostly albedo (inference: no unlit picture of that view exists to show it). A test of which member is brighter therefore passes with or without the light and cannot fail. What does speak for the light is how large the ratio is: the rope pole reads 3.60 in the game's frame, 3.03 lit and 1.47 unlit. So criterion 5 is recorded as met as written and as weak evidence; the regions of criterion 4 and the replays ("Checked without the game") carry the claim.

*Criterion 6, the shadowed regions (ratio; the acceptance cases of the shadows sub-project):* bridge: grass in leaf shadow 2.29, railing post cap 1.43 (half shaded at 36 s, in the sun at 44 s), planks in leaf shadow 1.32; third spot: dirt by the palisade 2.32, tall post sunlit side 2.01, planks in post shadow 1.44, small post cap 1.22; trees: ferns 1.88, stone slab 1.30, ground between the stumps 1.20, path under the trees 1.10, trunk 0.95. By the trees no shadow edge is seen on the trunk, path or ground in the emulated shots; they are filed as shadowed because they lie under the crowns, and their ratios are near the sunlit ones. Sides turned from the sun (no criterion): bridge railing post side 1.27, pole averted side 0.87; third spot small post side 1.12, tall post averted side 3.69 (under a moving shadow, drift -54%); trees stump and post sides 1.05, 1.29, 1.35.

*Not light: haze and leaves.* Far ground behind the game's haze: far rock 0.41 (bridge) and 0.56 (third spot), far slope 0.70, hue off by 110 to 140 degrees: the native picture has no fog, in-scatter or sky. Leaves: small tree at the bridge 0.95 with hue -24, third spot 1.28 (drift +18%), the crown by the trees 1.16 with hue -2.5; against the open sky the emulated rectangles hold sky and haze between the leaves; relative to the planks the lit leaves stood at about 0.56 of the game's in the review of plan Task 8c. Leaves are not calibration regions.
