**Cost** (criterion 7).
- *Frame rate.* 30.0 fps in every view window of 150 frames after the world has loaded, in all four runs and all four views, with two kinds of exception: the window that holds the `DISC=` capture's one long frame (1.6 to 1.8 s; 15.4 to 16.6 fps), and one walking window by the trees at 29.9. Guest work median per window of 300 frames: bridge 6.9 to 8.9 ms, third spot 8.2 to 9.0, trees 6.7 to 8.6, light off 8.2 to 8.5. The third spot's slower last windows of runs 331 and 343 did not recur (8.99 ms, p90 9.91). The renderer-off run 348 gave no frame-rate figure: the `[frame] guest` lines are written by the native renderer's install and that log has none; the nearest stand-in is the view-off windows of the lit runs (30.0 fps with no clay pass and a capture of 0.05 ms).
- *Capture.* View off: 0.049 to 0.065 ms in the frames logged with records off, and window medians of 0.052 to 0.069 ms in windows that are mostly view off (under 0.5 ms). Records on, bridge: window medians 1.456, 1.466, 1.477, 1.498 ms (p90 1.58 to 1.70); third spot 1.53 to 1.62; trees 1.49 to 1.61. The spec's 1.35 ms was the materials figure of a gated run that began at the menu; no gated run of this code exists. The baseline of the same kind does exist (corrected after the whole-branch review; as first written this said it did not): run 277, the materials sub-project's final bridge run, is master's own code (`07722e6`) in a user-present session started with `-BootSave Hero000` and the same plan, and its records-on windows read 1.474, 1.557, 1.545 and 1.619 ms (p90 1.88 to 1.98; `out\native-evidence\materials\final_bridge_fable_2_277.log`, the `capture:` lines of frames 1200 to 2100). This branch at the same place reads 1.456 to 1.498 (p90 1.51 to 1.70; run 344). So the records-on capture is not above the same-kind baseline, and the 1.35 ms it does not reach is the figure of another kind of run (gated, from the menu), not a regression of this branch: the criterion's second form ("if only user-present runs exist, not above the same-session baseline") is met in the sense of a same-kind baseline; the two runs are a day apart, not one session. Run 285, the binary of plan Task 1 in such a session, read 1.44 to 1.54 ms.
- *Clay pass, CPU* (the logged frame of each 300): hash 0.64 to 1.08 ms, decode 0.25 to 0.49 at the bridge and 1.36 to 1.71 at the other two, record 0.42 to 0.82; largest total over 300 frames 3.5 to 6.6 ms (bridge), 4.9 to 5.5 (third; 19.2 on arrival), 4.9 to 5.1 (trees; 18.5 to 32.1 on arrival), 3.2 to 6.3 with the light off.
- *Memory.* Targets: linear `R11G11B10_FLOAT` 3.1 MB, mapped 3.1 MB, depth 3.1 MB at 1120 x 720 (the log's `targets` line). Geometry resident 45.7 MB (bridge), 53.5 (third), 95.8 (trees: the walk's history; budget 256).

**The target's format** (the ruling deferred from plan Task 6). `R11G11B10_FLOAT` stays. The pass has one format constant behind its pipelines and targets and no switch, so no run of the 64-bit form was made on the display; the two formats' arithmetic is known and was computed instead (`task9\format_levels.py`, `format_levels.txt`: every display level in sixty-fourths, stored toward zero as this GPU does, mapped with the exposure). At 2.22 the 32-bit target shows every level below 96 in all three channels with an error of at most one level, so dark smooth regions (the far hills, shaded planks) cannot band from the format; level by level it loses: blue from level 96 (22% of the levels 96 to 127 never shown, 39% of 128 to 191, 59% of 192 to 255; error up to 3 levels, bands up to 2.9 levels wide), red and green from level 192 (22% never shown, error up to 2). Layers added with a store after each blend, as the terrain's are, come out darker by up to 1, 1, 2 and 4 levels in red and green and 3, 3, 4 and 7 in blue for one, two, three and five layers; a 16-bit float target shows every level, at most one off. In the calibrated bridge shot the far hills and the planks in leaf shadow (levels 26 to 166) show every level of their range in every channel; a small shaded post side lacks 10 red and 5 green levels of its range, which the arithmetic says is not the format (levels 31 to 90) and which was not looked into (`task9\pictures_9.txt`). The 64-bit form would cost 3.1 MB more and a frame time that later runs did not separate from the 32-bit form's (one night's experiment: 2 to 3 ms). The exposure does not widen the format's relative steps; it moves pixels up to levels where they are wider.

- *The target's format, restated.* The paragraph above was computed for an exposure of 2.22 in the mapping. Since the fix the target holds the very value the mapping shows, lit or not, so the arithmetic's rows for a factor of 1 are the ones that apply (`task9\format_levels.txt`, "exposure 1.00"; the missing levels listed by `fix\format_levels_fix.py`): stored toward zero, red and green show every level below 181 with an error of at most one level below 128 and two above, and lack 11 levels from 181 up (5% of the levels 128 to 191, 12% of 192 to 255); blue shows every level below 91, lacks 91 and 95 below 96, 4 of the levels 96 to 127 (12%), 42% of 128 to 191 and 56% of 192 to 255, with an error of up to 2 levels from 64 and 3 from 128; bands up to 2.8 levels wide. Equal layers stored after every blend come out darker by up to 1, 1, 2 and 3 levels in red and green and 3, 3, 4 and 6 in blue for one, two, three and five layers. A 16-bit float target shows every level. The ruling stands (`R11G11B10_FLOAT`): dark smooth regions, below level 91, still show every level in all three channels.
- *What was not run or not looked at.* A change of the light switch in the middle of a run; the debug layer's poll at a failure and at shutdown (the driver ends a run by closing the game's job, so no run reaches the shutdown line); the textures-off wording of the `Light:` line. These rest on their unit tests or on the code alone.

**Checked without the game** (not repeated here): `replay_check.py` (commit `3021b7a`, `task9b\`): the renderer's decode and formula of the probe colour equal the game's vertex microcode in every vertex of every lit probe draw of three captures (2,028 draws, 1,985,744 vertices, largest difference 0), and every other order of the four weights differs by 0.098 to 0.62; one well-seen draw of each lit kind against the lit picture, the texture cancelled by a light-off shot: 0.994 to 1.009 (hero, trunk branch, stream-colour prop, bridge post, plants, the dirt square's light). Whole kinds do not register pixel by pixel (the captures hold the first 512 indices of a draw), and far terrain and the plain `0x79EA...` props have no picture comparison.

**Limitations** (each with its measured size where there is one):
- *No shadows.* Shadowed regions are 1.2 to 2.3 times too bright after calibration (criterion 6); under the trees the picture has no dark ground, and a sunlit and a shaded side of a street would be alike.
- *No further lights.* The two- and four-light shaders (190 of 895 lit draws at the bridge, 278 of 953 at the third spot, 118 of 835 by the trees) are drawn with the sun alone; the lanterns of their light sets give nothing.
- *No normal maps, no specular, no emissive or cube-map terms.* Rock, bark and planks are lit by their vertex normals.
- *No fog, in-scatter, sky or post chain.* Hazed far ground reads 0.4 to 0.7 of the game's and is not blue; leaves stand at about 0.56 of the game's relative to the planks; thin things before the haze differ as the rope pole does; the game's glow on bright faces is missing.
- *One fixed exposure.* It is fitted at one place and one time of day, and on the base map read as stored (note of 2026-10-10 at "The exposure" above: not fitted again after the gamma fix of section 17); the game's own exposure belongs to its post chain. Regions of the three spots agree within 0.83 to 1.11; nothing is known of a scene whose exposure the game sets otherwise (night, interiors: user checks 30 and 31). Since the final fix wave it multiplies the lit draws only. What that leaves: an unlit draw of a lit frame (hair and fur cards, water, a draw whose light inputs could not be read) is shown as with the light off, so against its lit surroundings it is now 1.49 times darker on the display than in plan Task 9's binary; it has no light, and no exposure can stand in for one.
- *Daylight, one area, standing still.* Everything measured is the Bower Lake bridge and two spots near it between about 36 s and 100 s of the save's clock.
- *The plants' shadow side.* Where a plant turns from the sun the picture was brighter than the replay; with the alpha test applied, of the ten largest bright blobs by the trees three are cut-away texture, four fit at a shift of 17 to 20 pixels (the wind the pass does not have) and three, 363 pixels, are unexplained (`task9b\`).
- *The leaf replay's trend.* At the bridge measured over predicted falls from 1.15 to 0.99 across the bins of front light, in two runs alike; the cause is not separated (cards beyond the first 512 indices, cut-away texels, 2 s between shot and capture). By the trees the replay holds for level and colour only (1.19 to 1.21), the unlit picture of the same view being missing; a separate light-off run would not have given it, the view there shifting by 8 to 10 pixels between some runs.
- *Vertex-side identities.* Vertex `c18` = pixel `c21` (exponent times 2.2), `c54` = pixel `c20`, and for leaves vertex `c76` / `c83` = the frame's sun, are used in the place of registers the capture cannot read; they held in every row checked, all of daylight scenes of this one area, and a scene in which one fails is lit wrongly with no message (user check 32).
- *Leaves take the vector to the eye from the unswayed position* (no turn changed in 3,300 bridge leaf vertices; the back term off by more than 0.05 in 0.03%).
- *Discovery rows hold only the first 512 indices of a draw* (`capture.cpp`, `kMaxGeoIndices`): 208 of 309 lit object, trunk and plant rows of a bridge frame are cut short, which limits every picture replay.
- *From plan Task 2, still open:* the game's tangent correction of skinned normals (up to 12.8 degrees at single vertices); the bools `b128`, `b133` to `b135` are never read (terms under them are not drawn); `0x401A...`, fur and water have no formula.
- *The residual of the material path*: the native picture sits about 2% (3% in blue) below the replay with the light on or off (item 13 of section 13's follow-ups).
- *Runs.* All `RUN UNCHECKED`; the light-off comparison by the trees at full size was never made.

**Building on this machine: the antivirus.** Bitdefender flags the shader test's executable (`Gen:Variant.Application.Lazy.7774`, a generic static match on the binary's content: a false positive). The user has excepted the repository's `out` folder, and new binaries there build and run; build test executables only into `out\tests\runtime-unit-tests\`. One file the user restored from the quarantine, `out\tests\runtime-unit-tests\native_shaders.exe`, is locked against overwriting, so `tests\run_native_tests.cmd` stops at the shader test's link until the user deletes that file; until then the suite is run through a generated copy of the script in which only that output name differs (`task9\make_runner.py`, `fix\make_runner.py`). A binary that is removed, locked or refused is reported, never worked around.

**Follow-ups.**
1. *Shadows* (sub-project 8). The research is `.superpowers\sdd\shadows-research.md` (untracked): two 1024 x 1024 sun cascades redrawn every frame, a screen-size mask made by two full-screen draws, every lit family but far terrain multiplying its sun term by the mask (leaves by 0.6 x mask + 0.4: the leaf literals move from code to the table then). The regions of criterion 6 are its acceptance cases.
2. *Fog and the post chain* (haze, sky, the game's own exposure, bloom, depth of field). (The unlit draws of a lit frame and the clear colour under the exposure, listed here at first, were a defect and are fixed: "After the review: the fix wave".)
3. *Anti-aliasing* by a higher internal resolution or multisampling (asked for by the user on 2026-10-08 and marked for later): the pass's targets and the future shadow mask must stay independent of the game's resolution.
4. *Raise the 512-index cap of discovery rows*, so that a replay owns its pixels (the plants' shadow side, the leaf trend, whole kinds).
5. *Surface detail*: normal maps, specular, the further lights; the tangent correction of skinned normals.
6. *Night, town, interior, lanterns*: user checks 29 to 32; a night capture decides what a zero sun means.

From the whole-branch review (2026-10-08), recorded and not done:

7. *The unguarded loads.* The vertex shader loads the positions (t0) and the texture coordinates (t2) outside any branch; what keeps them inside their buffers is the index range checked at both ends before a record is drawn. Put them inside `[branch]` blocks on the range test when the vertex shader is next changed.
8. *The vertex side's identities, per draw.* Vertex `c18` / `c54` (plants) and `c76` / `c83` (the leaves' sun) are taken from the frame's block by identities seen in daylight scenes of one area: carry them per draw (a plant's small slot has 15 unused floats) or count a draw whose own values differ from the frame's.
9. *The leaf literals* (0.4545, 0.6, 0.4) into the generated table, with the shadows sub-project, whose mask they scale; and a log word for leaves left unlit because the frame's eye is not usable (today they are counted `light-unknown` with everything else).
10. *Normals and residuals.* The game's tangent correction of skinned normals (up to 12.8 degrees at single vertices); the 2% (3% in blue) by which the native picture sits below the material replay; the 512-index cap of discovery rows (follow-up 4).
11. *Costs not yet taken out.* The palette hash of a skinned record every frame; the per-frame hashing of colour streams; the light switch's cvar parsed every frame; the 452-byte terrain patch copied per terrain draw.
12. *What is resident.* A breakdown of the geometry cache's resident bytes by kind (positions, normals, colours, probe, bend); a debug assert that every slot bound at b1 lies inside the frame's constant buffer.
13. *A device-backed test of the pass* (the pure parts are tested; `Render`, `PrepareLight` and `FinishTerrain` run only in the game), and whether the debug layer reports a root descriptor that was never set.
14. *The tools.* `pconst_check.py` does not excuse the first rows of a capture begun with the view off; the normal's source is counted by pixel shader only.
15. *Left by the fix wave itself* (its report, `final-fix-wave-report.md` in the sub-project's working folder, has the reasons): a poll of the debug layer's messages at the moment a device is removed (the SDK hands the renderer no such moment: the poll is at a latched failure and at shutdown instead); a pure test of the pass's decision not to build light inputs with the light off beyond `ClayLightInputsBuilt` and the pictures.

## 15. Shadows

Sub-project 8 (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-native-renderer-shadows-design.md`, 2026-10-08). Evidence files of this section are in `out\native-evidence\shadows\` (git-ignored); the names below are files of that folder unless a path is given. What was measured at the end, the criteria and the limitations are in "Validation (plan Task 6)" below. The section begins with the discovery (plan Task 1): how the game makes its sun shadow, as far as captures and the emulated GPU's register file show it. Inference is marked.

### Passes

The order in every captured frame (rows) and every logged GPU frame:

1. A clear (`DrawIndx2:821EF988`, r7 = `0x400`, r8 = the surface word `0x10000410`: pitch 1040, no multisampling), then **the near map**: 110 to 137 decoded draws a frame in the eight captures used here.
2. The same clear, then **the far map**: 121 to 228 draws.
3. Later, in the tiled scene (pitch 1120): the depth pre-pass, then a depth-only rectangle at pitch 560 (surface word `0x08C20230`, depth word `0x00008701`), **the two mask rectangles** at pitch 1120 under bin select `0x2`, a resolve (`RB_MODECONTROL` 6), then the colour draws.

A shadow-pass draw is a draw outside the main scene with surface pitch 1040 and colour mask 0. Its words: depth `0x00708766` (test greater-equal, write) under the reversed range (`2113` = -1, `2114` = 1), `2205` = `0x00219806` (cull back, clockwise front, polygon offset on for both faces) or `0x00219800` (no cull: the leaf cards), `RB_MODECONTROL` 4 or 5 on the GPU. Vertex shaders in frame 1 of the bridge capture, near pass: `0x3A0F9098B839DDBC` 29, `0xF160B4DA459A6D40` 28, `0xFBD39C64463E180B` 21, `0x432563420047C96C` 18, `0x82F6433A69263C75` 12, `0xA8A5B2A89F70336A` 8, `0x5F4416192E87005F` 1 (`task1_bridge_shadow_matrices.txt` lists every pass of every frame).

**Light matrices** (`tools\xdk_sigmatch\shadow_matrices.py <capture>`, test `tests/test_shadow_matrices.py`; outputs `task1_*_shadow_matrices.txt` and, for the three older captures, `task1_shadow_matrices_105316.txt`, `_105659.txt`, `_105833.txt`). In every caster shader but one `oPos = c0..c3 . p` with the world rows in vertex `c4..c6`, so `M = [c0..c3] * inverse([c4..c6; 0 0 0 1])` is the pass's world-to-map matrix. `0xA8A5...` (instanced bushes) builds the world position itself and holds `M` in `c0..c3` (read as world rows its rows are off by 3 to 12; read directly, by under 1e-6). `0x5781...` and `0x87E0...` of the third spot fit the world-row form.

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Passes compared (8 captures, 8 frames each, two passes a frame) | 128; all agree (the tool exits 0 on each capture) |
| Largest deviation of a row's `M` from its pass's median | 2.3e-6 |
| The median against the scene's pixel registers (`c36..c39` near, `c40..c43` far: one value in every scene row of a frame, 886 to 1,059 rows) after `u = 0.5 x + (0.5 + h) w`, `v = -0.5 y + (0.5 + h) w`, depth = z | largest residual 2.8e-7 |
| The half texel `h` | + 0.5 / 1024 in u and in v, in all 128 passes |
| Shape (bridge) | orthographic (`w` row 0 0 0 1); near 30.0 x 30.0 world units (0.0293 a texel), depth span 115; far 70.0 x 70.0 (0.0684 a texel), depth span 155; the depth axis is `-c80.xyz`, the sun |

So the scene's `c36..c43` are world to shadow-map (u, v, depth) with a half texel added, and the pass's own draws give the same matrix: either source can check the other in the capture.

**The origin snaps to whole texels.** The map position of the world origin, `(M.x.w, M.y.w) * 512` texels, is a whole number in every one of the 128 passes (largest distance from one: 0.0016 texel), although the sun, and with it the axes, turns from frame to frame. Standing still it moves by 0 or 1 texel a frame (the sun's turning); in the capture taken while walking (`task1_trees_capture2_shadow_matrices.txt`) by whole numbers of up to 72 texels a frame (near, frame 2 to 3: (-72.000, 67.001); far: (-28.000, 40.000)). The map is not centred on the eye: the eye (pixel `c31` at the second mask draw) sits at clip (-0.34, -0.37) of the near map at the bridge and at (0.52, -0.34) by the trees (`task1_map_centre.txt`). What the maps are fitted to was not established; the native pass takes the game's matrix and need not know.

`c12` = (20, 35, 2, w) and `c13` = `c14` = (1/1024, 1/1024, 0, 0) in every frame of every capture and log; `c12.w` moves with the time of day (0.462 to 0.512 over all of them; later runs go further: 0.5316 in run 378's log, `task5b_trees5_fable_2_378.log`).

### Mask draws

Two rectangle lists of three vertices, clip positions (-1, -1), (-1, 1), (1, -1) (the GPU's bytes of vertex fetch constant 95: the whole target), drawn with `BeginVertices` (`0x822060A0`, r4 = 8, r5 = 3, r6 = 8 bytes a vertex), which now has a decoded discovery row, `"kind":"verts"` (`WriteVertsRow` in `capture.cpp`; discovery only). The surface is `0x11800460` (pitch 1120, one sample; the scene's `0x11810460` has two), `RB_COLOR_INFO` 0; the result is resolved to the `k_8` texture at `0x12B17000` that the lit shaders sample at slot 8.

| | First: `0x1B4B5AE12EF270CA` (vertex shader `0x7A6E981FC4D0A375`) | Second: `0x0F99810F072BF0FC` (vertex shader `0xB1D7F0D4330BBD7D`) |
|---|---|---|
| `RB_DEPTHCONTROL` | `0x00708765`: stencil on, function always, pass replace; depth test off | `0x00700564`: stencil **off** (bit 0 clear; the function field says not-equal), depth test off |
| `RB_STENCILREFMASK` | `0x00FFFFFF`: reference 255, masks `0xFF` | the same word |
| Alpha test (`RB_COLORCONTROL`, `RB_ALPHA_REF`) | `0x0000000C`: on, greater than 0.502 | `0x00000004`: off |
| Blend, colour mask, cull | off, RGBA, none | off, RGBA, none |
| Bin mask | `0x00000002` | `0x00000002` |
| Textures | tf7, tf13 | tf6, tf7, tf13, tf14 |
| Pixel constants read | `c12`, `c31` = (1/1120, 1/720), `c40..c43`, `c46.x`, `c47.x`, `c77.x` | `c12`, `c31` = the eye, `c36..c43`, `c46` = (1/1120, 1/720), `c47` = (0.5, 0.5, 1/32, 1/32), `c77.x` = 2.5/1024, `c116..c119` |

The words are the same in all 40 rows of each shader (5 captures of 8 frames), and equal the GPU's register file in every paired frame (below).

**Which pixels each covers.** The first writes only where its own alpha passes the test: its shader outputs alpha 1 where the pixel is farther than its depth threshold and 0 elsewhere (instr 12, 13, 39), and there it also sets stencil to 255. The second has no test at all in these words: no stencil, no alpha test, no depth test. In the emulated frame it therefore writes every pixel of the target and the first rectangle's output survives nowhere. That costs nothing in the picture, because the second shader holds the far form and the fade itself (instr 87 to 113). Inference: on the console the second is kept off the stencilled pixels by hierarchical stencil (its stencil function field is set although the test is off; `RB_HIZCONTROL`, register `0x2203`, is in no row and was not logged), which makes the first rectangle a cheaper path for distant pixels and nothing more. For the native mask the second shader alone is the game's arithmetic.

**Textures** (the rows' fetch constants, equal to the GPU's fetch constants in every paired row; `task1_*_mask_rows.txt`):

| Slot | Address | Format, size | Filter, addressing | Pixels in guest memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tf6 (near map) | `0x12BE1000` | `k_24_8_FLOAT`, 1024 x 1024, tiled | point (mag and min), clamp | no: the dump's 65,536 bytes are all zero |
| tf7 (far map) | `0x12FE1000` | `k_24_8_FLOAT`, 1024 x 1024, tiled | point, clamp | no (all zero) |
| tf13 (scene depth) | `0x1A02A000` | `k_24_8_FLOAT`, 1120 x 720, tiled | point, clamp | no (all zero) |
| tf14 (rotation) | `0x1A53B000` | `k_8_8`, 32 x 32, linear, pitch 128 (256 bytes a row) | point, repeat | **yes**: 32 rows of 32 two-byte texels; `(2a - 1, 2b - 1)` of every texel has length 0.989 to 1.010 (`task1_bridge_tf14_rotation.txt`), so each texel is a unit vector, the rotation of the tap pattern; 602 distinct texels |

The dumps are `task1_bridge_0F99_tf6_...bin`, `_tf7_`, `_tf13_`, `_tf14_1A53B000_FB036F07EB514FF4.bin`. The same two fetch words are bound at slots 6 and 7 in 94 scene rows of the bridge capture (the research note names their shader: the blended characters' `0x401A...`). The first 8,192 bytes of the tf14 dump are the same in all five captures of the four runs (SHA-256 `9ffab61500cd24a1...`). The rotation texture can be read by the native pass from guest memory; the fallback of the spec (unrotated taps) is not needed.

Byte order of tf14 (added after the review of Task 1): its fetch constant's second word is `0x1A53B04A`, bits 6 and 7 = 1, the 8-in-16 byte swap (`task1_bridge2_mask_rows.txt` line 111 prints "endian 1"). The two bytes of a texel as they lie in guest memory are therefore exchanged before they become the shader's `.x` and `.y`. The length check above cannot tell the two orders apart (both give unit vectors); the wrong order is a mirrored rotation. Which stored byte is `a` and which `b` of the formula `(a, b) = 2 * tf14.xy - 1` must be fixed by the task that reads the texture, from the SDK's `k_8_8` load path, and tested.

**Constants over frames.**

| Register | At `0x1B4B` | At `0x0F99` | Frames |
|---|---|---|---|
| `c12` | (20, 35, 2, w) | the same | every frame of 5 mined logs (212 frames) and 5 captures (40 frames); w between 0.462 and 0.512 (0.532 in the later run 378's log) |
| `c13`, `c14` | (1/1024, 1/1024, 0, 0) | the same | all |
| `c46` | x = 0.995474 (0.99547422 to 0.99547476) | (1/1120, 1/720, 0, 0) | all |
| `c47` | x = 0.997163 (0.99716276 to 0.99716300) | (0.5, 0.5, 1/32, 1/32) | all |
| `c77` | x = 0.000635 (0.00063467 to 0.00063562) | x = 0.00244140625 = 2.5 / 1024 | all |
| `c31` | (1/1120, 1/720, 0, 0) | the eye | all |
| `c36..c43` | screen to map (the world-to-map rows times `c116..c119` of the second draw); `c39` = `c43` = `c119` | the same | change every frame |

Inference from the mined values (`task1_offline.txt`, B): with the view depth `1 / (c39.z z' + c39.w)` of a window depth `z' = 1 - depth`, the first shader's `c46.x`, `c47.x` and `c47.x + c77.x` are the depths of the distances `c12.x + c12.z` = 22, `c12.y` = 35 and `c12.y + 10` = 45 (within 0.003, 0.004 and 0.014 units in all 212 logged draws): it runs beyond 22 units and fades from 35 to 45, the second shader's own numbers.

**Literals** (the GPU's register file at the draws, one value in all 212 logged frames; the rows' `"ps_lit"`, read from the shader object, hold the same values: a table of eight registers from `c248` for `0x0F99...`, and of four from `c252` for `0x1B4B...`, whose `c252` and `c253` are zero and not named by its microcode):

| Shader | Register | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `0x0F99...` | `c248` | (10, 0.0833333358, -1, 2): the far branch ends at `c12.y` + 10; 1/12; texel * 2 - 1 |
| | `c249` | (0, 1, 0.5, 0.1): 0.1 is the slope of the fade |
| | `c250` | (-0.480026007, -0.597710013, -0.194983006, 0.767022014) |
| | `c251` | (0.473434001, -0.791558981, -0.203345001, 0.185461) |
| | `c252` | (-0.0735799968, 0.412458003, -0.69591397, 0.507430971) |
| | `c253` | (-0.405809999, -0.932614982, 0.962339997, 0.519456029) |

`c250..c255` are the twelve offset pairs of the near taps. The files `out\shader_dump\shader_<hash>.ucode.bin.frag` hold no literal table: they are the microcode as the SDK has it (control flow, then three dwords an instruction, three zero dwords at the end; 345 and 123 dwords), so the literals cannot be decoded from them as the plan assumed; they come from the register file and from the shader object.

**Against the GPU** (`task1_mask_rows.py <capture> <GPU log> <frame offset>`; outputs `task1_bridge_mask_rows.txt`, `task1_bridge2_`, `task1_trees_`, `task1_third_`). Each mask row is set against the one `RB_MODECONTROL` 4 draw of its pixel shader in the paired GPU frame: 31 rows of each shader have one (7 + 8 + 8 + 8; frame 8 of the first bridge capture lies outside its log). In all of them the pixel registers the shaders read (`c0`, `c12..c14`, `c31`, `c36..c43`, `c46`, `c47`, `c77`, `c116..c119`) equal the row's `"pfull"`, all twenty state words of `"rs"` equal the register file, and the fetch constants of every sampled slot equal the row's `"tf"`.

### Bias

**Where the registers are.** The polygon offset registers `PA_SU_POLY_OFFSET_FRONT_SCALE`, `_FRONT_OFFSET`, `_BACK_SCALE`, `_BACK_OFFSET` (`0x2380..0x2383`, floats) are the first four of the run of eight the builders flush from device + `0x2A50` (section 13, the table of the eight runs), so their shadows are at + `0x2A50`, + `0x2A54`, + `0x2A58`, + `0x2A5C`. Static: `0x821A8A78` (r3 device, r4 a float's bits) stores its value times 16.0 (the float at `0x820994F8`, read from the image dump `out\xdk\fable2.img`) at + `0x2A50` and + `0x2A58`, the slope scale of both faces; `0x82289648` stores its value at + `0x2A54` and + `0x2A5C`, the offset; both set bits 11 and 12 of the `PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL` shadow (+ `0x2948`) to "scale or offset is not zero". `RB_STENCILREFMASK` (`0x210D`) and its back-face twin (`0x210C`) are in the `0x2100` run, at + `0x2900` and + `0x28FC`; the setters store single bytes (reference `0x822398E8` at + `0x2903`, mask `0x822C08E0` at + `0x2902`, write mask `0x821B1568` at + `0x2901`). Constants and `DeviceRegShadowOffset` in `xdk_layout.h`; the registers of a row's `"rs"` are `kRowStateRegisters` in `render_state.h` (twenty: the fourteen of section 13 and 14, then `210C`, `210D`, `2380..2383`).

`BeginVertices` does not store the device's command write pointer; it keeps the address of the last dword it wrote at device + `0x3484` (`0x82206524`), which is where a `"verts"` row's `"cmd"` is read, so that the row pairs with its packet by the rule of section 13.

**Proof** (`render_state_check.py`, which now compares nineteen registers and takes `"verts"` rows; outputs `task1_*_render_state_check.txt`):

| | bridge | bridge2 | trees | third |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sampled rows (draw, tess, verts), all with `"rs"` | 14,922 | 14,918 | 11,537 | 16,285 |
| Paired with a GPU draw | 13,069 (the 1,853 of frame 8: outside the GPU log) | 14,918 (100%) | 11,537 (100%) | 16,285 (100%) |
| Frame offset; probed rows confirmed; runner-up | +1137; 6,535 of 7,461; 4 | +1132; 7,459 of 7,459; 7 | +1732; 11,537 of 11,537; 703 | +1250; 8,143 of 8,143; 52 |
| Executions compared, colour / pre-pass | 19,051 / 2,968 | 21,752 / 3,391 | 17,503 / 3,465 | 22,403 / 3,948 |
| `210C`, `210D`, `2380..2383`: unequal executions | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| The other thirteen registers | 0 unequal but `RB_COLOR_MASK` in the pre-pass (GPU 0), as in section 13 | the same | the same | the same |
| Shadow-pass executions among them (pitch 1040) | 1,721 | 1,951 | 2,272 | 2,727 |
| Checker exit | 1: rows of frame 8 not paired | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The `"verts"` rows are among the paired rows (203 of the first bridge capture's 232, then 232, 200 and 224; none unpaired where the frame is logged), so the pointer at + `0x3484` is the packet's.

**Values** (`task1_bias_by_pass.py`; outputs `task1_*_bias_by_pass.txt`): the bias belongs to the pass, not to the shader. Every row of a near pass holds one set and every row of a far pass another, in all 40 captured frames (4,757 near rows, 6,423 far rows):

| Pass | `2380` / `2382` (scale) | `2381` / `2383` (offset) | As D3D set it (scale / 16) |
|---|---|---|---|
| near | `0xC2000000` = -32 | `0xBA83126F` = -0.001 | slope scale -2, depth bias -0.001 |
| far | `0xC2A00000` = -80 | `0xBBA3D70A` = -0.005 | slope scale -5, depth bias -0.005 |

Front and back hold the same values and both enables are on. The window depth of the maps is `1 - z` with the test greater-equal, so the negative bias moves a caster away from the light, as a shadow bias must. How the emulator applies the registers (SDK `src/graphics/d3d12/pipeline_cache.cpp`, `include/rex/graphics/util/draw.h`): slope-scaled bias = scale / 16, constant bias = the offset in depth units (as an integer: `ceil(|offset| * 2^21)` steps of 8 for the float depth format). Elsewhere in the frames the offset is on only for one depth-only shader of another pass (`0x87D4404FB36AF71D`: scale 0, offset 0.0001; 3,301 rows of the bridge capture).

Qualification (added after the review of Task 1): the emulator does not apply the offset as an exact depth offset. The SDK turns it into an integer D3D12 bias (`ceil(|offset| * 2^21) << 3`, `include/rex/graphics/util/draw.h` lines 197 to 215), which on a float depth target scales with the exponent of the primitive's largest depth; the factor is chosen for depths in [0.5, 1) (the SDK's comment, lines 166 to 195), and below 0.5 the emulated bias is half or less. A native bias applied as an exact offset therefore differs from the emulated picture for casters with map depth under 0.5. In these captures the eye sits at map depth 0.67 to 0.90 (`task1_map_centre.txt`). Also: the polygon offset registers keep stale near or far values at other draws with the enables off; only bits 11 and 12 of `0x2205` say whether a draw is biased. The upper bound 0.512 of `c12.w` quoted in this section comes from the older capture `native_discovery_20261008_105659` (0.51186); the mined logs and Task 1's captures reach 0.5014.

**What a later task can rely on.** The two bias sets can be read per pass from the first shadow draw's `"rs"` words (the proof above covers every shadow-pass draw of four captures); as constants they are the table above.

### Native shadow maps

Plan Task 4 (2026-10-09). The clay pass draws the game's two maps itself, from the frame's shadow records (`FrameScene::shadow_draws`; the capture of plan Task 3), into two depth targets of its own. The rules are in `src/native/render/clay_logic.h`, "Native shadow maps"; `test_clay_logic.cpp` cases 540 to 555 and `test_native_shaders.cpp` 170 to 188 hold them.

| | Native map |
|---|---|
| Size | 1024 x 1024 `D32_FLOAT` each, a constant (`kShadowMapSize`); 8.0 MB together; made on the first frame that draws them (lazily, with the mask target: "Native shadows") and destroyed with the pass's other targets; their size does not follow the window |
| When | a frame whose mask is drawn: drawn with light and the shadows' switch, with a valid shadow block, a light block, an eye and one view (`DecideClayMask`, `ClayMapsDrawn`; since the final fix wave: before it the maps were also drawn in a frame with a valid block and no mask, for nothing); otherwise neither map is touched and nothing may read them (`ClayPass::shadow_maps_drawn`) |
| Geometry | each record with its own rows (the game's matrix of that draw) through the clay vertex shader: static, bone-skinned and instanced casters by the scene's paths; no sway (as the scene's trees) |
| Depth | the game: window depth `1 - z`, cleared to 0, greater-equal. Native: depth = `z`, cleared to 1, less-equal (the RHI has no greater-equal): the same caster stays. A record with another depth state is not drawn (`state`) |
| Cull | the record's (`ClayCull`): none for the leaf cards, back for the rest in every capture; three depth-only pipelines, one a mode, outside the pass's cache |
| Bias | the record's polygon offset, in the pixel shader through the output depth: `depth = saturate(z - (scale / 16) * max(abs(ddx z), abs(ddy z)) - offset)`; near +2 slope and +0.001, far +5 and +0.005: away from the light |
| Alpha | alpha-test casters: the texture's alpha (times `c15.w` for the leaf cards) against the captured function and reference; the leaf cards then alpha-to-mask as on one sample, `alpha >= 1 - offset / 4` with the offsets of `0x2202`'s top byte (`0xAA00001C`: 0.5 at every pixel; SDK `src/graphics/pipeline/shader/dxbc_translator_om.cpp` lines 1681 to 1685, 1740 to 1746, 1790). A caster whose texture is not ready is left out that frame, never drawn solid. The bushes' distance dissolve is not drawn |
| Texels | drawn with a viewport origin of (0.5, 0.5): a native texel's centre (i + 0.5, j + 0.5) is where `c36..c43` (with their half texel) put the same point, so `ShadowBlock::world_to_map` addresses the native maps as it stands and a lookup compares with its depth row. Inference: the registers' half texel is the console's pixel centre at whole window coordinates (`PA_SU_VTX_CNTL` is in no row) |

**The bias against the emulator's, corrected.** "Bias" above says the emulated bias is right for depths in [0.5, 1) and half or less below, and that the eye sits at map depth 0.67 to 0.90. That figure (`task1_map_centre.txt`, "depth") is the clip `z`, the native map's depth; the game's window depth there is `1 - z`, 0.10 to 0.33. The shadow-view shots agree: the casters' stored depth is 0.49 to 0.88 at all three spots (medians 0.73 to 0.79 near, 0.63 to 0.68 far; grey levels of the shots below, taken as the stored value). So nearly every caster of these scenes lies where the emulator's constant bias is below its nominal value (inference from the SDK's comment: a half for window depths in [0.25, 0.5), a quarter in [0.125, 0.25)), while the native one is the exact 0.001 and 0.005. The native casters are therefore pushed back further than the emulated ones, by up to about 0.00075 of the depth range near (0.09 world units of the 115) and 0.00375 far (0.58 of the 155). Whether that shows as a detached shadow at a contact is for the comparison with the emulated frame to say (plan Tasks 5 and 6); nothing was tuned for it.

### Native shadows

*Note of 2026-10-10 (post sub-project, Task 8b; ledger ruling 30).* The terrain figures of this subsection, the shadowed ground regions above all (dirt by the palisade, grass in leaf shadow), are of the base map tf3 read as stored, with an ambient 1.8 to 2.5 times the game's; ground in shadow is ambient alone and is what that reading moved most. Since commit `5d0f974` they no longer describe the picture, and the native shadow's strength has not been judged again on the right ambient: section 17, "The base map's gamma sign" ("Runs", item 4).

Plan Task 5 (2026-10-09). With the shadows on, the clay pass keeps the game's order: depth pre-pass, mask, colour. The rules are in `src/native/render/clay_logic.h`, "Native shadows"; `test_clay_logic.cpp` cases 560 to 570, `test_native_shaders.cpp` 190 to 199 and `test_texture_decode.cpp` 120 to 129 hold them; `tests/test_light_check.py`, `MaskPinnedForTheRenderer`, has the reference's side of the pinned numbers. The runs are at the end of this part.

| | Native |
|---|---|
| Pre-pass | every scene record whose colour pipeline tests and writes depth, drawn once more before the colour draws, depth only: the record's vertex path, and its colour shader compiled with `CLAY_DEPTH_ONLY` (the same alpha, the same discards: alpha test, alpha-to-mask, a layer's hole and weight; then a return: no light, no mask). Its pipelines are a cache of their own (kind x depth function x cull: 36 keys at most, so it cannot overflow). Since plan Task 5b a record that lies wholly beyond the mask's reach is left out and counted, and a record whose pixels are all kept is drawn with the flat kind's pipeline ("The pre-pass's reach", below) |
| Mask | one full-screen step into an `R8_UNORM` target of the clay target's size (0.8 MB), `shaders::kClayMaskPs`: `mask_0f99` of `light_formulas.py` in the native form, for every pixel. `0x1B4B...` is not ported (in the emulated frame `0x0F99...` writes every pixel: "Mask draws") |
| Clear depth, far pixels | no special case: a pixel at the clear depth is a pixel beyond `c12.y + 10` and gets `c12.w` (0.46 to 0.53), as the game's does. (The spec's Design 5 said 1 there; superseded by the ruling after plan Task 2) |
| Colour pass | drawn as without shadows, from a depth that is cleared again after the mask step, each record with its captured depth function. The pre-pass's depth is the mask's alone, so no record can lose a pixel to its own pre-pass depth (review focus 3 by construction; the cost is that the colour pass gets no early rejection from the pre-pass) |
| Use | each lit pixel reads the mask at its corner over the target's size (linear, clamped: the mean of the four texels (px - 1, px) x (py - 1, py), as the game's lit shaders fetch tf8; plan Task 5b, below; it was the pixel's centre, one texel, in the runs of plan Task 5) and multiplies its sun term: `SunGateSingle(mask, facing)` for the layers, `SunGateSingle(mask, 1)` for objects, trunks and both plant families, `LeafMask(mask, 0.6, 0.4)` for the leaves; the far terrain has none. An unlit pixel does not sample it (per `light_mode`, on the compiled programs) |
| Binding table | the albedo's parameter is a pair, albedo `t3` and mask `t4` (`SetTexturePair` at every draw); the terrain table is `t5..t8`, the light's four vertex buffers `t9..t12`; still twelve parameters and 56 root words |
| Without a mask | the 1 x 1 white texture at `t4`: with the shadows off, the light off, no light block, no valid shadow block (any reason, a frame without shadow records included: counted `shadow-block`), no constant buffer for the frame, or no view (`shadow-view`). Then neither the pre-pass nor the mask step is drawn, nor (since the final fix wave) the two maps |

**Compare directions.** The game's maps hold `g = 1 - z` of the nearest caster and its shader tests `1 - z > g` (near, strict) and `1 - z >= g` (far). The native maps hold `n = z` (1 where no caster is), so the native tests are `z < n` for the near map and `z <= n` for the far map: lit where the receiver is not farther from the light than the stored caster, strictly nearer for the near map. Case 563 draws one world point through the pass's light matrix and the bias (`ShadowMapWindow`, `ShadowMapDepth`, checked against `ShadowBias` on the game's window depth) and looks it up through the registers' rows (`ShadowMapLookup`, `MaskProject`): the same texel and depth; lit by both rules with the bias, shadowed by the near rule and lit by the far rule without one, shadowed 0.01 behind, lit 0.01 in front; and the verdicts equal the game's on the game's values. A receiver beyond a map's far plane (`z` above 1) is in shadow by both rules, as in the game (`1 - z > 0` fails).

**The frame's view-projection.** The mask step needs the world position of a pixel: the pre-pass depth through the inverse of one view-projection. The clay vertex shader makes each clip position from the record's own rows (the game's `c0..c3` of that draw), so there is no frame matrix as such. What the captures say (`task5_frame_vp.py`; outputs `task5_frame_vp_*.txt`; four captures of 8 frames at the bridge, by the trees, at the third spot and while walking):

- The terrain rows (layer and far) and the instanced plants' rows hold the same `c0..c3`, bit for bit, in every frame (bridge: 492 + 75 terrain and 135 plant rows a frame): for them the pass builds world positions, so their rows are the frame's world-to-clip matrix.
- For the meshes with world rows (`c4..c6`: objects, trunks, leaves and others) `c0..c3 * inverse(c4..c6)` is that matrix to 2.5e-7 of its largest entry (bridge: about 230 rows a frame; leaves 4.8e-8 to 1.9e-7 in all four captures). No per-tile or per-draw difference was found: every in-scene row of a shader whose `c4..c6` are world rows agrees.
- The inverse of that matrix is the mask shader's own `c116..c119` up to a common factor (1.00000 +- 0.00004, which the division by `w` removes) with a largest relative difference of 3.5e-8 to 1.1e-7, in all 32 frames; and the mask shader's `c31` is the scene's pixel `c19` (the eye) in every one of them.

`FrameInverseViewProj` takes the rows of the terrain records and of the instanced records as they are, and for a tree leaf `rows * inverse(world rows)` (`PassMatrix`; a leaf's light inputs carry its whole world matrix, the other meshes' only the rotation), takes the matrix that more than half of them agree on within 1e-4 (of the larger of the entry and its row's largest direction entry), counts the others, and inverts it in double (the majority is the fix round's, "Oracle and fix round" below: as first built every record had to agree with the first). No record, no majority, a matrix that is not finite or cannot be inverted, or a frame without a usable eye: no mask for the frame, counted `shadow-view` with the reason. A scene without ground, plants and leaves (an interior) has no view by this rule: its frames are counted, not shadowed.

**The rotation texture.** tf14 of the mask draw is in no product record (the mask draws are not captured), so its address is the constant of "Mask draws", `0x1A53B000`, read every frame through the bounded physical read (`TextureCache::ReadRotationTile`: 32 rows of 256 bytes) and checked: every texel `(2a - 1, 2b - 1)` a unit vector within 0.05 (the game's: 0.989 to 1.010), else the taps are drawn unrotated, `(a, b) = (1, 0)`, and the frame is counted (`unrotated`). Another address in another session shows there. Channel order, from the SDK's load path: the fetch constant's endian is the 8-in-16 swap and the 16-bit load shader exchanges the two bytes (`src/graphics/shaders/bytecode/d3d12_5_1/texture_load_16bpb_cs.h` lines 121 to 126) into `DXGI_FORMAT_R8G8_UNORM` (`src/graphics/d3d12/texture_cache.cpp` lines 127 to 130: `k_8_8`, host swizzle RGGG); the fetch constant's swizzle (dword 3 = `0x01001690`: x from 0, y from 1) goes through `GuestToHostSwizzle` (`src/graphics/pipeline/texture/cache.cpp` lines 352 to 366) unchanged. So **tf14.x is the second byte of a texel as it lies in guest memory and tf14.y the first** (`DecodeRotationTile`; test 121 holds it on a hand-made texel, and the game's dump passes the check). The tile is addressed as the game addresses it, texel = pixel mod 32 in the game's 1120 x 720 pixel units, the native pixel's centre scaled into them first.

**Numbers the mirrors are pinned to** (`task5_mask_pins.py`, output `task5_mask_pins.txt`): frame 1 of `task4_bridge_capture1_native_discovery_20261009_015622.jsonl` gives the view-projection, `c12`, `c19` and `c36..c43`; synthetic maps and tile; twelve pixels in the five regimes (near only, blend, far only, fade, beyond) and at the clear depth, with and without the tile; four world points for the two terms alone; seven values of the combination. The C++ mirrors (in double on the shader's single-precision inputs) agree with `mask_0f99`, `mask_near`, `mask_far`, `mask_combine` to 1e-9 or better.

**The patch in the near map** (review of plan Task 4: a smooth grey-to-white patch right of the deck in `task4_bridge4_shot_48s.png`, and a similar one in the far map). It is one draw, in both passes: vertex shader `0xF160B4DA459A6D40` (opaque, static), 23,321 indices, a vertex buffer of 299,820 bytes (`task5_patch_draw.py`, output `task5_patch_draw.txt`: rows 96 and 176 of frame 1). Its sampled vertices span u 0.38 to 0.95 of the near map with depth 0.954 to 1.093: a large mesh that leaves the near map's depth range through its far plane, where it is clipped, so its stored depth runs up to the clear value: the fade to white. In the far map the same mesh lies at depth 0.77 to 0.88. It is not the slope bias saturating a caster: its depth changes by about 2.4e-4 a texel, a slope term of 5e-4. What it shadows in the near map can only be what lies farther from the light than it and still inside the range.

**Cost, as expected before the runs** (an estimate; the measured figures are under "Runs"). The pre-pass submits each depth-writing record a second time: at the bridge the scene has about 950 rows a frame, and if most of them write depth that is up to about 900 more draws a frame with the same seven buffer binds each and no new geometry or texture work (the buffers and textures are the colour draws'); the mask is one full-screen draw of 16 map loads a pixel at most. The lit pixel paths gain one texture read.

### Oracle and fix round (plan Task 5b)

*Note of 2026-10-10 (post sub-project, Task 8b; ledger ruling 30).* The terrain figures of this subsection, the shadowed ground regions above all (dirt by the palisade, grass in leaf shadow), are of the base map tf3 read as stored, with an ambient 1.8 to 2.5 times the game's; ground in shadow is ambient alone and is what that reading moved most. Since commit `5d0f974` they no longer describe the picture, and the native shadow's strength has not been judged again on the right ambient: section 17, "The base map's gamma sign" ("Runs", item 4).

Plan Task 5b (2026-10-09), after the runs above: the canopy's shadow that read as too dense, the third spot's frame rate, the two adapters' masks, and the fix round of the review of plan Task 5. Evidence files are `task5b_*`.

**The oracle.** No SDK change was needed. The emulator's `--readback_resolve=full` copies every resolve back into guest memory, so the two maps (`0x12BE1000`, `0x12FE1000`: `k_24_8_FLOAT`, tiled, big-endian, the 20e4 depth float in the upper 24 bits, holding `1 - z`) and the scene depth (`0x1A02A000`) can be read there at the frame's end. A temporary diagnostic in `clay_pass.cpp` (`task5b_diag_clay_pass.patch`; behind `FABLE2_NATIVE_SHADOW_DUMP`; removed again, not in any commit) wrote, for consecutive frames, those guest ranges and the native maps, pre-pass depth and mask read back from the GPU, with the mask's constants and the tile. `task5b_oracle.py` compares them. Runs 372 (`task5b_bridge_oracle_*`: the bridge plan of plan Task 5) and 373 (`task5b_bridge_split_*`: `38:VIEW=split`), both `RUN CLEAN`; with the read-back the game runs at about 2.5 fps, which does not matter for a comparison of one frame's textures. Limits: the mask's memory (`0x12B17000`) and a band of rows of the near map are reused by later resolves of the frame (76% of the mask's bytes are zero at the frame's end; the band shows in `task5b_bridge_oracle_cmp_01_near_emulated.png`), so the emulated mask itself was **not** read; comparisons of the near map use the rows below the band.

**The two adapters' masks** (the crisp mask of the software adapter against the soft one of the real GPU). The same check that holds the GPU's mask to the CPU arithmetic within one level in 99.2% of the pixels rules out a shader that behaves differently on the real GPU. The soft wide edges near the camera are the kernel: 2.5 texels of 0.0293 units is a penumbra of 0.15 units, tens of pixels wide a few units from the eye, and the formula on the emulated maps shows the same soft blots. The software adapter's shot is another moment of another run (about eighty frames after the load, another position of the maps). Not done: the same dump on the software adapter.

**The third spot's frame rate.** Run 374 (`task5b_third_timing_*`, the third spot's plan with the emulator's `--native_render_collect_stats=true` and the diagnostic's stage timers; `RUN CLEAN`; its frames are 42 to 43 ms, which was first put down to the statistics' cost and is not: run 379 below, without them, has the same frames. Runs made through the idle gate on this machine are slower throughout than the controller's runs with the user present, view off included; why was not established, so their frame rates are compared only with one another). Per frame in the native view: the command processor is busy 31.5 to 33.6 ms (14.2 to 14.6 ms of it in 3,900 to 3,960 emulated draws, 4.2 to 4.4 ms in 86 resolves) and spends 9.8 to 10.0 ms in the swap, where the clay pass runs; of that the pass's own recording is 4.2 ms: 3.5 ms preparing the records (hash, decode, cache), 0.2 ms preparing the shadow records, 0.13 ms recording the 972 pre-pass draws, 0.13 ms the 977 colour draws, 0.04 ms the 270 to 330 shadow draws, 0.001 ms the mask step. The rest of the swap is the emulator's submission of the frame's command list. So the thread that emulates the GPU has no idle time at this spot: the game's frame is paced by that thread's `WAIT_REG_MEM` on the vertical blank counter, and a frame whose emulation and swap together exceed 33.3 ms is late by the excess. Without the statistics (run 370) the frame is 33.4 ms in the median with a tenth of the frames at 37.7 ms and more: the sum sits at the limit, and the pre-pass's 972 further draws (about nine recorded calls each) were what moved it over (run 365 without them: 30.0). The pre-pass's recording itself is 3% of the pass's time; its replay by the emulator's deferred command list is not measured (no timer of the SDK separates it). What was changed (fix round, item 4): a pre-pass draw whose pixels are all kept binds three buffers and no texture and is drawn with the flat kind's pipeline, and the light's four registers are bound once in the pre-pass and once for the two maps (about four of nine calls a pre-pass draw and four of nine a shadow draw less). Its effect, run 376 (the controller's, a quiet machine, the user present; `task5b_third5_*`): none to speak of: shadow window 27.1 fps, native windows 27.5, 28.4, 29.2, 28.3 fps, view off 30.0; bridge (377) and trees (378) 30.0.

**The pre-pass's reach.** Beyond `split.y` + 10 = 45 units from the eye the mask is `split.w` whatever the depth: `mask_combine`'s fade `sat(0.1 * (d - split.y))` is 1 there, the far term is read only below that distance and the near term below `split.x + split.z`, so `m` = 0 and the value is `split.w` exactly (case 573 holds it at 45, 45.001, 60 and 5,000 units); a pixel at the clear depth is such a pixel. A depth-writing record that lies wholly beyond that distance therefore changes no pixel of the mask, and the pass leaves it out of the pre-pass: where it was the nearest surface the depth is now the clear value or that of a surface farther still, `split.w` either way, and nearer surfaces are drawn as before. Conditions (`PrepassBeyondReach`, `clay_logic.h`): the record's depth function keeps the nearer surface (less, less-equal; a far record drawn with another function could overwrite a near one's depth and is kept); its bound is known and finite. The bound: the box of the record's position buffer (all four components, computed once when the geometry cache builds the buffer: after the bones, after the copies of an instanced record were laid out, so it holds for those too) under the record's own matrix gives the smallest clip `w`; `(w - w(eye)) / |V[3].xyz|` with the frame's view-projection `V` is the distance along the view axis, never more than the distance from the eye; it must reach 45.05 (a margin for the mask's own rounding of the distance). Anything unknown: kept. The `Shadow:` line counts both: `pre-pass P draws, C beyond reach`. No shader text, binding or target changes.

**Fix round (review of plan Task 5).** (1) The lit shaders read the mask as the game's fetch does: `0x26052DEFBA688AF2` instr 4 and 5 (and `0xA7E45D07F5CF6627` instr 7) fetch tf8 at `|r4.xy| * c0.zw + c0.xy`, `r4` the pixel position register (whole pixel coordinates: the SDK's translator rounds the position down, `dxbc_translator.cpp` line 659), `c0` = (0, 0, 1/1120, 1/720), and tf8's fetch constant (`0x88C24802 0x12B17002 0x0059E45F 0x00281400 ...`: 1120 x 720, `k_8`, magnification and minification linear, clamped): the pixel's corner, the mean of four texels. Native: `(pos.xy - 0.5) * (1 / width, 1 / height)` with the linear clamped sampler; mirrors `MaskReadCoordinate`, `MaskRead`, `MaskReadValue` (case 571). (2) Frames with the switch and the light on that are drawn with the white mask for want of the light block or of the shadows' objects are counted: `no-light L, no-objects O` at the end of the `Shadow:` line. (3) `FrameInverseViewProj` takes the matrix of the majority of the records that give one (more than half agree within the tolerance), counts the others (`mask drawn (K records with another view)`) and fails closed without a majority (case 568). (4) The pre-pass's lighter draw, above (`PrepassDiscards`, `PrepassKey` with the record's alpha: case 572). (5) Comments. This changes shader text and the binding pattern: it needs the software-adapter run before any run on the real GPU.

(`task6_edges_bridge_368.txt`, `_377.txt`, `_380.txt`, `task6_edges_bridge_on_383.txt`; shot by shot `task6_edges_table.txt`. The segments run at 16 degrees to the horizontal, so a shot pixel along them is 0.885 game pixels.)

- *The control.* A shadow's edge that lies along a gap between two planks cannot be told from the gap. So each segment was also measured on the native shots of run 382, shadows off, where a shadow's edge must give no step: the left edge's step is gone (the tool finds a weak rising step elsewhere and refuses the triple: `the step is not of one direction`), the right edge's too (`no step above contrast 1.25`; `task6_edges_bridge_off_382.txt`). Both counted edges pass.
- *The rope pole's shadow does not pass it.* Its band runs along the planks and its lower edge sits on a gap: at three places the native edge is 0.6 to 1.5 pixels above the emulated one in runs 368, 377 and 380, but the shadows-off shot has a step at the same place (11.0 against 10.5 with shadows), so those numbers measure the planks as much as the shadow. Kept in the file, not counted.
- *What is missing.* The criterion names three edges: a rail post on the planks (measured), a trunk's shadow on the ground, the bridge's edge. No trunk's shadow falls on open ground in any of the three views (under the trees the ground is ferns in leaf shadow), and the bridge's own shadow falls where no view looks. So the criterion is met for one caster of three, by 0.4 pixels of 6, and not shown for the others. The 6 pixels were meant to catch the bias's detachment and a shifted map: at this post neither shows.

*Criterion 6, shadows off.* (a) The programs: `task5_old_new_programs.txt` (commit `068c84c` against `b8bf181`): the vertex, flat, far terrain and shadow-map shaders are the same program at all 128 values of `light_mode`, the textured and layer shaders at the 64 values without the lit bit; the 64 lit ones differ by the mask's read and its product alone. With the shadows off the mask is a white texel. The two later commits: `3ab5833` changed that read to the pixel's corner with the linear sampler, and a 1 x 1 white texel read anywhere with a clamped linear sampler is 1 exactly (case 571 of `test_clay_logic.cpp` holds the mirror: a mask of 1 reads 1), so the product is `x * 1`; `3484927` changed no shader. (b) Regions of a shadows-off run of the final binary, run 382, against the lighting validation's run 350: dirt patch 0.999 (0.999), grass 1.035 (1.036), planks 1.033 (1.031), rock face 1.107 (1.108), trunk 1.113 (1.112), shirt 0.945 (0.946): each within 0.002 (run 367 of `068c84c`: within 0.01). Its log reads `Shadow: off` on every line and has no maps or mask line: nothing of the shadows is made.

**The walk** (run 384, `task6_walk_fable_2_384.log`): twenty-four shots: native at 34 to 46 s, one a second, then 48, 52, 56 s; split view at 60 to 68 s while the hero walks back (`task6_walk_shot_<t>s.png`; contact sheets `task6_view_walk_a.png`, `_b.png`, `_d.png`, looked at; `_c.png` not). **What the series cannot show is shimmer:** the hero runs and the camera swings, so two shots a second apart share no ground, and after he stops the camera is still turning (the shots at 43 to 56 s differ from one another in 30 to 92% of their pixels by more than 8 levels: `task6_walk_steady.txt`; that is the camera, and says nothing of the shadows). What it does show: in every one of the nine native shots of the walk (34 to 42 s) the shadows are there and where their casters stand: the rails' and planks' shadows on the deck (34, 35 s), a soft-edged shadow across the dirt path and the dog's own shadow under the dog (36, 37 s), the fence posts and the trunks with their shaded sides (38 to 41 s), the dim ground under the canopy from 42 s; no shot has a frame without shadows, a straight line where the shadow stops (a map's edge), stripes or dots on the sunlit path, or a shadow away from the foot of its post. The log over the run's 900 clay frames, the walk among them: `shadow-block 0, shadow-view 0, unrotated 0, no-light 0, no-objects 0`, every shadow record drawn (`near 142 of 142`, `135 of 135`, `115 of 115`; far 157, 150, 184), the capture's `shadow-block in 0 of 300 frames`. In the split shots (60 to 68 s) the emulated strip at the left and the native picture meet without a step in brightness on the hero, whom the seam crosses at 65 and 66 s, or on the path. Why the native shadow should not crawl any more than the game's while walking is an argument, not an observation: the game's map origin moves in whole texels ("Passes": up to 72 texels a frame while walking, always a whole number), and the native maps are drawn with the game's matrices of the same frame, so their texels lie where the game's do. Whether that holds to the eye is user check 34. The frame rate while walking was not measured in a run with the user present: run 384 is a gated run, and its native windows read 19.8 (the one with the first native frames), 26.1, 28.3 and 28.0 fps (gated runs are slower in every window).

In the normal runs he is not in shadow in the native mask: the mask panel of run 377 at 54 s is white over him (254.9 of 255 over the shirt's rectangle; read off `task5b_bridge5_shot_54s.png`, no output file) with a thin shadow at his feet, and his shirt reads 0.948 of the emulated value with the shadows and 0.945 without. So what the read-back runs showed did not recur; it was a moment of another run at another frame rate, and was not explained.

**Limitations** (each with its measured size where there is one).
- *No sway.* The casters are drawn in their rest pose, as the scene's trees are. In the six frames compared one crown of the near map lay 8 to 18 texels (0.2 to 0.5 units) from the game's, as a whole, the rest within 0 to 4 texels (`task6_sway_displacement.txt`); a region under a crown's edge reads 0.49 to 1.05 of the emulated value depending on the moment when the emulated shots are 4 to 6 s from the native one, and 0.93 to 1.15 over the two large rectangles when they are 3 s away (run 387). Whether the game's crown swings about the rest pose or leans steadily is open. "Rest pose" and "stand still" mean no sway: the native shadows still move with the sun, as the game's do (`final_native_over_time.txt`).
- *The bushes' distance dissolve* is not drawn: a far bush keeps its whole cut-out shadow until the game drops it.
- *The exact bias.* Native casters lie further from the light than the emulated ones by a median of 0.03 to 0.08 units in the near map and 0.40 to 0.45 in the far one (plan Task 5b's oracle), because the emulator reduces the bias with the depth's exponent. At the one contact measured (the railing post) no gap shows (edges within 0.4 pixels).
- *An empty cascade removes both.* A frame in which either map has no recorded draw has no valid block and no shadows at all (`shadow-block: no-pass`), also where the other map would have been right.
- *A caster whose texture is pending* is left out of the maps for those frames (never drawn solid): its shadow is missing for the frames after a load.
- *`0x0F99...` alone.* The first mask rectangle (`0x1B4B...`) is not ported; on a console it may cover distant pixels by another path (hierarchical stencil, inference).
- *Blended characters and water.* The hair and fur cards (`0x401A...`), which take the two maps by taps of their own, and water are unlit and unshadowed.
- *The per-light map* (slot 9: one lantern's or fire's shadows) is not drawn. *Daylight only:* nothing is known of night, town or interiors (user checks 35 to 38).
- *No view, no shadows.* The mask needs the frame's view-projection, which comes from ground, instanced plants or leaves: a scene with none of them (an interior, by inference) is drawn without shadows and counted `shadow-view`.
- *The pre-pass's reach* is exact only for records drawn with the frame's projection: a depth-writing mesh drawn with another projection could be left out wrongly, and records with another view are counted only among ground, plant and leaf records. None in evidence (review of plan Task 5b: the mask panels of runs 381 and 376 at 62 s, `task5c_third5_shot_62s.png` and `task5b_third5_shot_62s.png`, are 99.67% identical: 1,758 of 544,640 pixels differ, every one in the box where the hero stands; recomputed by the documents review, no output file).
- *The rotation texture's address* (`0x1A53B000`) is a constant of these runs' boot path; elsewhere the read fails its check and the taps are unrotated (counted; banded penumbras).
- *The mask's HLSL is not executed by a test.* It is held by text pins, by the pinned numbers of its C++ mirrors and by plan Task 5b's comparison of the GPU's mask with the same arithmetic on the CPU (99.2% of the pixels within one level, bridge, six frames). *The emulated mask itself was never read* (its memory is reused within the frame): that it equals the formula on the emulated maps rests on the microcode check.
- *The half-resolution depth pass* on surface `0x09000230` (the leaf cards again, in the camera's view) is not understood and not recorded.
- *Criterion 5* is shown for one caster. *Criterion 4* is not met as written: it is shown on two small regions with an emulated drift of 11 to 25% (one of them outside 25% in two of run 387's three triples) and, uncounted, on two large leaf-shadow regions within 16% in one run; one sunlit region is outside 0.05 in two of that run's triples and the rock face in all. Two regions at the third spot are darker natively for a reason not established. *Criterion 6* is shown by a substituted measure, not pixel for pixel.
- *Runs.* Frame rates and the 2.2 ms are from runs with the user at the machine (`RUN UNCHECKED`: 377, 378, 381, and for the 2.2 ms also 385 and 386), one run a spot for the frame rate; gated runs are slower for a reason not established.

**Follow-ups.**
1. *Sway*, with the scene's own trees (the animation work): casters and scene together, and with it the question whether the game's crowns lean.
2. *Early rejection from the pre-pass depth*: keep it for the colour pass (equal-or-less tests) instead of clearing it.
3. *Record preparation cost*: 3.5 ms of the clay pass's 4.2 ms at the third spot is hashing, decoding and cache lookups of the scene's records, every frame (28 buffers rebuilt a frame).
4. *The third spot's frame budget*: the emulated GPU's thread is busy for the whole frame there; a timer for the replay of the native draws in the emulator's deferred list before the draw count is touched again.
5. *A unit-level execution of the mask's HLSL* (a software rasteriser or the software adapter in a test), and a device-backed test of the pass.
6. *Night, town, interior, lanterns* (user checks 35 to 38): the per-light map, a view for scenes without ground, the rotation texture's address in another session.
7. *A static edge test that does not depend on what happens to be in view*: a place with a trunk's shadow on open ground and the bridge's shadow, for criterion 5's other two edges; the two undecided regions of the third spot with an oracle there.
8. *The blended characters' own taps and water*, with their lighting; *the bushes' dissolve*; *the half-resolution depth pass*.
9. *The `no-caster` path seen in a run* (the scratch build above), or a town capture that brings a caster without an entry.

### After the reviews: the fix wave

Written 2026-10-09 after the two whole-branch reviews of commit `3aff85f` (code: ten minor findings; documents: six important and ten minor). The binary is that day's of 06:40 (`fable_2.exe`, 109,750,784 bytes, sha256 `9E1FB0C7...015A4D7F`, `final_fix_build_game.txt`). **No shader text, binding or target changed** (`src/native/fable2_native_shaders.h` is byte-identical to `3aff85f`'s), so no run on the software adapter was needed. Evidence files are `final_*` and `task6_ab_*`.

**Code.**
- *The mask is decided first, and the maps are drawn only with it.* One pure chain, `DecideClayMask` (`clay_logic.h`; case 574 of `test_clay_logic.cpp`), in which the first thing missing decides: the shadows' switch (`off`), the light's switch (`no light`), the shadows' objects (failed), the shadow block (`shadow-block`), the light block (`no light`), the frame's constant buffer (`maps not drawn`), the eye, the one view, the mask's constants (`shadow-view: eye | no-record | disagree | singular`). Before, the two maps were prepared and drawn in every lit frame with a valid block, also when the frame then had no mask (no light block, no view): about 230 draws that nothing read. The pass's frame counts follow from the verdict (`CountClayMaskFrame`). The failed objects come before the block in the chain because of the next item: without that order the line would read `shadow-block` in every frame after the failure and never name its cause.
- *After the shadows' objects have failed the capture records no shadow passes* (`ShadowRecordsWanted`, `native_render_state.h`). The failure is cleared where the pass is rebuilt (another device; the F6 retry after a failure of the renderer). A failure of the shadows' objects alone does not latch the renderer, so F6 does not retry it: the log line and the `Shadow:` line say `off until the pass is rebuilt or the game restarted`. The failure has not occurred in any run; the path is held by the pure functions' tests alone.
- *The switches' words.* `--fable2_native_shadows` and `--fable2_native_light` take `on`, `true`, `1`, `off`, `false`, `0` (case 575); before, `true` was silently off. The warning names the words.
- *The `Shadow:` line* reads `frames since start N: shadow-block B, ...`: the pass's totals over the frames drawn with both switches on, which is another count than the capture line's `shadow-block in F of W frames` (one log window, frames with shadow records). Logs of earlier binaries read `frames N:`.
- *The capture's read of the block's registers* checks under the lock that its frame is still the one being built, as the shadow draws, passes and extra draws did already.
- Removed: `ShadowPassTracker::Frame` (never called outside its test), an unreachable branch and an alias in `ClayPass::Render`. Comments that still said the mask is 1 everywhere, named `t10` / `t11` for the buffers now at `t11` / `t12`, or gave two figures for one residual without saying which is which, are corrected (9.95e-7: the largest of a single shadow row's own matrix over 6,612 rows; 2.8e-7: the largest of a pass's median matrix over 128 passes).
- *A test of the literals.* `tests\test_mask_literals.py` reads `kMaskNearTaps`, `kMaskTapWeight`, `kMaskFarReach`, `kMaskFadeSlope` and `kMaskNearRadiusTexels` out of `clay_logic.h` and the taps, the weight, the reach and the slope out of the mask's pixel shader's text, and holds them against `light_formulas.MASK_NEAR_TAPS`, `mask_0f99`'s defaults and the generator of the pinned numbers, now checked in as `tools\xdk_sigmatch\mask_pins.py` (its output is line for line that of plan Task 5's scratch copy).
- Tests: native suite 29 `PASS` lines, exit 0 (`final_fix_native_suite.txt`; through the scratch runner, the shader test as `native_shaders_fix8.exe`); Python 754 tests, 3 skipped; nine mutations of the new pure functions each fail a case (`final_fix_mutations.txt`).

**The quiet A/B of the records-on capture** (the controller's runs 385 and 386; "Cost"): 1.427, 1.442, 1.455 ms without the shadow records, 1.865, 1.874, 1.865 ms with them: 0.41 to 0.44 ms for the two passes' records, under the criterion's 2.2 ms.

**Emulated shots 3 s either side** (the controller's run 387, a quiet machine, `RUN UNCHECKED`, the binary of `3484927`; shots `final_tight_shot_<t>s.png`: emulated at 36, 42, 48, 54 s, native at 39, 45, 51, 57 s; `final_tight_regions_39s.txt`, `_45s.txt`, `_51s.txt`; the 57 s shot has no emulated shot after it and makes no triple). What it shows, and its limits:
- The two large rectangles under the canopy's shadow are within 16% of the game in all three triples, where the 6 s brackets gave 0.626 and 0.849 (run 377) and 0.804 and 0.938 (run 383). So "the canopy is too dark" (plan Task 5: 0.613) was in good part the time between the shots. It is one run at one spot; sway and the sun are still not separated; and the emulated shots themselves change by -54% to +161% over the planks' rectangle within 6 s, so a mean of two of them is a rough stand-in for the moment between.
- The small rectangles move with shadow edges. The post cap says nothing (0.545, 1.755, 0.610 while the emulated shots change by +78, -48 and +226%). The two props' shadows are leaving their rectangles in both pictures ("these shadows move too", above): the native rectangle is the lighter one in every triple, the rope pole's by 36 and 29% in the second and third, **outside the criterion's 25%**. Whether the native shadow leaves sooner, is lighter, or the 3 s still matter was not established.
- **The grass beside the dirt, a sunlit region, is 0.052 and 0.062 below its lighting ratio (1.035) in the second and third triple**, outside 0.05. Not explained (the emulated rectangle brightens faster than the native one over those seconds).
- Later seconds, native only (`final_native_over_time.txt`, runs 377, 380, 383, 386; no emulated shot exists there): the planks' leaf-shadow rectangle, at the shadows-off value at 60 to 62 s (0.098), is dark again at 78 to 84 s (0.044 to 0.067), and the sunlit dirt patch reads 0.29 to 0.30 at 78 to 84 s against 0.35 with the shadows off (runs 382, 385). Something shadows them natively then; whether the game's picture does the same is not shown.

**Ruling** (the controller's; spec ruling 36): validation of moving shadows uses emulated shots 3 s or less from the native one. The figures with 6 s between the shots stay in the record as they were measured.

## 16. Fog and sky

Sub-project 9 (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-native-renderer-fog-design.md`, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-09-native-renderer-fog.md`). Evidence files of this section are in `out\native-evidence\fog\` (git-ignored); captures and their dump folders are in `out\build\win-amd64-release\logs\` and are named by their stamp (`092459` is `native_discovery_20261009_092459.jsonl` with `native_tex_20261009_092459\`). The formulas are in `lighting-formulas.md`, part "Fog and sky".

### Discovery

Plan Task 1: a capture-only change (commit d7af364 and the commit of this section) and three runs. Nothing the pass draws changed.

**What the capture writes now** (`capture.cpp`; all of it only while a discovery capture is armed):

- *1D textures are dumped*, their texels in one row (`render::Fetch1DDumpBytes`). Textures the game rewrites in place are kept once per **content**, not once per address (`render::DumpKeyedByContent`: every 1D texture, and 2D textures of formats 29, 22 and 23, which are dumped in full now): the first content at an address as `<BASE>_<IDENTITY>.bin`, every other as `<BASE>_<IDENTITY>_<XXH3>.bin`, each with a `"texture"` row carrying `"frame"`, `"content"` and, for a 1D texture, `"dim":1`. Bounds: 512 files; 512 MB for the 2D targets (the tables do not count against the bytes).
- *`"tf"` of draw, verts and indx rows holds the vertex shader's slots too* (listed in `"vs_tex_slots"`), and every decoded row has `"tfc"`: slot -> content hash of the texture as it was when the row was written. A row is paired with a dump by that hash, never by address or order.
- *`DrawIndx:82217EE8` has a decoded `"indx"` row.* The builder is `BeginVertices` with an index list (read from the recompiled function, `xdk_layout.h`: r4 primitive, r5 base vertex, r6 vertices, r7 indices, r8 index format, r9 vertex bytes; the two storages at device +0x3488 and +0x348C). The game fills the storage after the builder returns, so its bytes come in an `"indxdata"` row written when the thread enters its next hooked draw. In the four captures every sky row's data row holds the eight corners of the unit cube ((0, 0, 0, 1) to (1, 1, 1, 1), 16 bytes a vertex) and 36 indices below 8 (`task1_<stamp>_sky.txt`): the storage is filled by then.
- A `"texture"` row's `"frame"` is the frame of the draw that sampled the texture, not the frame that rendered it; see "The oracle" for what that means for targets.

`tools/xdk_sigmatch/fog_tables.py` decodes and reports (`tables`, `trees`, `sky`, `scene`, `replay`); its outputs for the four captures are `task1_<stamp>_tables.txt`, `_trees.txt`, `_sky.txt`, and for the oracle `task1_092959_scene.txt` and `task1_092959_replay_frame<N>.txt`.

**Runs** (made by the controller with the user present: all three `RUN UNCHECKED`, exit 0, no `d3d ERROR` line in a log; through `tools\drive_game.ps1 -BootSave Hero000`). No window has the freeze signature: in the world the work medians are 6.9 to 12.6 ms (runs 1 and 2 at 30.0 fps but for the windows that hold a capture or the end; run 3, with read-back, at 23 to 28 fps, 18.7 in its last window, with swap medians of 26 to 37 ms); the two windows of 27 to 28 fps with work medians of 34 ms at each start are the loading.
