**The two tables** (28 frames of the four captures; `task1_<stamp>_tables.txt`).

| | tf4, in-scatter by angle | tf5, transmittance by distance |
|---|---|---|
| Fetch constant (frame 1 of `092459`) | `00804956 1FAB505D 0000003F 00280D11 00000003 00000018` | `02004802 1FAB4086 000000FF 00280C14 00000003 00000018` |
| Reading | 1D, 64 texels, format 29, endian 8-in-16, swizzle `0x688` (identity), sign fields 1 1 1 1, exponent adjust 0, clamp to edge, linear, no mip | 1D, 256 texels, format 6, endian 8-in-32, swizzle `0x60A`, sign fields 0, exponent adjust 0, clamp to edge, linear, no mip |
| Bytes | 512: a texel is four half floats, each stored high byte first, in the order r, g, b, a | 1,024: a texel is four bytes stored a, r, g, b |
| Values | all finite; r 0.308 to 0.952, g 0.384 to 0.517, b 0.306 to 0.555 over the four captures, a = 0 everywhere. Not above 1: not an HDR table in these scenes. Texel 0 (looking away from the axis) is blue-grey ((0.308, 0.384, 0.465) in `092459`), the last texel (towards the axis) orange ((0.933, 0.467, 0.306)) | texel 0 is (1, 1, 1), a = 1 everywhere; falling with distance, blue fastest: (0.745, 0.714, 0.565) at 254 units, (0.361, 0.310, 0.133) at 1,004, (0.149, 0.114, 0.024) at the last texel (1,996 units) in frame 1 of `092459` |

- *The decode is proven on real texels as far as these scenes can:* the tables are smooth and in range only in this reading (tf5 monotone from exactly 1, alpha exactly 255; tf4's alpha exactly 0), and the sky function with tf4's texel 0 in the order r, g, b reproduces the oracle's sky to 0.7%, 0.2% and 1.6% in red, green and blue (below); with red and blue exchanged it would be off by a factor 1.5.
- *One table per frame, complete at the first fogged draw.* In every frame of every capture all main-scene rows that sample slot 4 name one (address, content) pair, and likewise slot 5: 56 of 56 table-frames (896 rows a frame at the bridge), from the frame's first fogged row (the water `F6D9...`, in the opaque group) to its last. The content hash is taken at each row, so the bytes did not change between the first and the last sampling draw of a frame. The sky rows of the same frame name the same tf4.
- *The ring of three addresses* is as the research has it (tf4 at `0x1FAB1000`, `0x1FAB5000`, `0x1FAB3000`; tf5 at `0x1FAB0000`, `0x1FAB4000`, `0x1FAB2000`). The content does not change every frame: of the 24 steps between consecutive frames 4 have both tables byte-identical at another address; the others change tf4 by at most 0.002 and tf5 by one step (1 / 255) in a few texels.
- *With the clock* (run 2, the same place 120 s apart, frame 1 of each): `c66` (-0.8272, 0.0134, 0.5618) to (-0.6848, -0.4149, 0.5991); `c67.x` 20.44 to 28.49; `c68` (0.2671, 0.4012, 0.4667) to (0.2734, 0.4201, 0.4667); tf4's texel 0 (0.311, 0.388, 0.471) to (0.352, 0.448, 0.552), its last (0.934, 0.471, 0.313) to (0.952, 0.517, 0.386); tf5's best single exponent in red 0.001011 to 0.000897.
- *tf5 is not `exp(-k d)` of `c64` or `c65`.* The best single exponential per channel (`fit_exponential`) is off by 0.028 to 0.038 of full scale (7 to 10 steps of the table), with k = (0.00102, 0.00117, 0.00209) in `092459` against `c64` = (0.000305, 0.000394, 0.001071) and `c65` = (0.00525, 0.00596, 0.00983). The optical depth per unit of distance falls with distance (red: 0.00135 at 12 units, 0.00116 at 254, 0.00095 at 1,996), and no single second path length makes it `c64 d + c65 l` in all three channels (the implied l differs by channel: 41, 40, 31 units at 254). Spec ruling 3 (read the tables, never compute them) stands.

**The trees' tables** (`task1_<stamp>_trees.txt`, all 28 frames: 52 tree rows a frame at the bridge, 84 at the third spot). Slot 16 holds **tf5 itself** and slot 17 holds **tf4 itself**: the same fetch constants, the same address, the same content hash as the frame's tf5 and tf4, texel difference 0, in 28 of 28 frames each. tf17 is therefore a **1D** texture fetched with a 2D fetch: the second coordinate (the near blend `t`) addresses nothing, `tf17(a, t)` = `tf4(a)` for every `t`. The trees have no blend from `c68`. Against the pixel form `c68 + t * (tf4(a) - c68)` the difference is `(1 - t) * (tf4(a) - c68)`, which exists only within one unit past the fog start (`c67.z` = 1) and is multiplied by `1 - T`, where T is tf5's first texel, (1, 1, 1): nothing in the picture.

*Ruling B (controller, 2026-10-09; the evidence above supports it: 28 of 28 frames).* Trees are fogged with the game's own form: `T = tf5(c67.w * dD)`, `add = (1 - T) * tf4(angle) * c8.x`, `colour * T * c49 + add`: no blend from `c68` and no amount `c28.x`, evaluated per pixel. Spec ruling 4 is amended accordingly in plan Task 6.

**The sky draw** (`task1_<stamp>_sky.txt`). Five `"indx"` rows a frame have pixel shader `F7601FBE485936FD` with vertex shader `8262E1111C273B50`: four outside the main scene (the reflection passes; vertex `c9`.z = -9.97, 30.8, -9.97, 29.8 at the bridge) and **one inside it**, 28 of 28 frames. So the product recognises the sky draw as: a call of `0x82217EE8` inside the main-scene bracket whose pixel shader hashes to `F760...`. At that row:

- triangle list, 8 vertices, 36 indices, 16 bytes a vertex (one float4 fetch, slot 95); depth word `0x00708762`, blend `0x00010001`, cull `0x00218000`, colour mask `0xF` (as the GPU log has them);
- vertex `c0..c3` equal the terrain rows' view-projection of the same frame, vertex `c9` is the eye ((82.072, 157.339, 50.171) at the bridge, equal to pixel `c19`); the vertex shader's `c255` is its literal, not in the bank;
- pixel `c31.x` = 150, `c46.x` = 100, `c47.x` = 0 in all 140 sky rows; `c64..c67` the frame's; `c28` = (1, 1);
- tf4 is the frame's table (the same content hash);
- **tf13 and tf14 are one texture**: 2D, 16 x 16, format 6 (`k_8_8_8_8`, which the texture cache decodes), linear (not tiled), endian 8-in-32, swizzle `0x60A`, wrap in both axes, linear filter, no mip address, at `0x1A544000`; fetch constant identical in all 140 rows. Its 256 texels are all (0, 0, 0, 0) in all four captures. With alpha 0 the shader's blend leaves the clear-sky term alone: **the sky of these scenes is `(1 - E) * tf4(angle)`**, no cloud texture. tf11 and tf12 (the `b129` volume's) are a 1 x 1 black texture.

**The oracle** (run 3; `task1_092959_scene.txt`, `task1_run3_oracle_scene_frame1.png`). With `--readback_resolve=full` the texture the post chain samples at `0x199E0000` (1120 x 720, format 29, tiled, 6,594,560 bytes dumped, 6,592,512 needed) is the scene before post. Untiled (`untile_scene`: half floats high byte first, r, g, b, a) and viewed: the whole bridge picture, planks and railing, the hero and the dog, the tree at the left, hazy blue hills, the lake, a blue-grey sky; no tearing. All 806,400 texels finite; medians (0.570, 0.652, 0.282), maxima about 4.

- *Whose frame.* Each of the four frames' downsample (`87E8...`) and composite (`37B1...`) rows name one content of the scene, another in every frame. But a target's bytes at a row are not that frame's render: the depth content first seen at frame 1's last sampling row is the one frame 2's mask rectangles name, and so on (the emulator's GPU thread runs behind the guest thread that writes the rows). So a dump is some earlier frame's resolve, by about one frame (inference from the contents' order). With the camera standing still and the registers drifting by 1e-4 a frame, this changes no number below; a moving camera would need the pairing settled first. A half-written target could also be hashed and kept as a content; none of the four pictures viewed or replayed shows one.
- *The scale is not 16.* `c20.w` is 8.44137 in every main-scene row of run 3 and 16.0 (15.9999914) in every one of runs 1 and 2. The scene's values are the shader output with that run's `c20.w` in it: the sky replay below fits with 8.44 and would be off by 1.9 with 16. `c20.w` is thus the game's exposure and it moves when the read-back gives the game its luminance (inference for the cause; the two values are measured). The picture file was written with the tool's default divisor 16.
- *The clear colour* was not found (the clear rectangle is another builder, `DrawIndx2:821EF988`, without a decoded row). It does not show: the pixels whose depth is clear follow the sky function (below).

**Replay against the oracle** (`fog_tables.py replay`, every 4th pixel in x and y, 50,400 pixels a frame; `light_formulas.sky` and `light_formulas.fog` with the frame's tables through `table_1d`; the world position from the read-back depth `0x1A02A000` through the inverse of the sky row's `c0..c3`; `task1_092959_replay_frame1.txt` to `_frame4.txt`).

- *Sky* (10,135 pixels whose stored depth is 0, frame 1): observed / (`sky()` * `c20.w`), median per channel **1.007, 0.998, 0.984**; frames 2 to 4: 1.006 to 1.007, 0.998, 0.983 to 0.984. Median absolute difference in linear values 0.0019, 0.0013, 0.0070. The red ratio's 10th and 90th percentiles are 0.997 and 1.141: the upper tail is what is drawn over the sky without depth (the glare and the sun's quad; inference, not separated). Spec criterion 3 (median within 10% per channel) holds on this picture.
- *Ground*: the colour before fog is unknown, so the test is a bound. With T and the in-scatter floor `(1 - T) * F` of each pixel, the colour the pixel implies is (observed / `c20.w` - floor) / T:

| 300 to 600 | 2,133 | (0.664, 0.625, 0.448) | (0.145, 0.188, 0.283) | (0.104, 0.145, 0.258) | (0.060, 0.063, 0.036) | 1.3% |

  The far picture is the in-scatter: beyond 600 units the floor alone is 94 to 99% of what is observed, and the implied ground colour stays a plausible dark green-brown (0.02 to 0.08) at every distance instead of going negative or growing with distance, as a wrong table, a wrong distance scale or a wrong channel order would make it. The pixels below the floor (water, the lake `2B09...` with its own form, edges where the depth and the colour are of different surfaces: inference) are 0 to 5%.
- *What the replay does not test.* tf4 beyond its first texel and the texel addressing: at the bridge every sampled sky pixel and every fogged ground pixel looks away from the axis `c66` (tf4's coordinate is 0 in 10,135 of 10,135 and 14,633 of 14,633), where the clamp reads texel 0 under any convention; reading tf4 half a texel to either side changes no median. For tf5 half a texel is 3.9 units of distance, far inside the bound above. A view towards the sun is needed for both (no such capture exists).

**The research's open questions.**

1. *Texels of tf4 and tf5:* above. In range 0 to 1, per frame, slowly changing with the clock, tf5 not an exponential of `c64` / `c65`.
2. *tf16, tf17:* tf5 and tf4 themselves; no `c68` blend in the trees (ruling B).
3. *The sky draw:* one in-scene row a frame; tf13 = tf14 = a 16 x 16 `k_8_8_8_8` texture of zeros; `c47.x` = 0 in all 28 frames (two clocks 120 s apart included); vertex `c0..c3` the scene's view-projection, `c9` the eye. Whether the cube is clipped: its half-size is 2,850 around the eye and the depth-clear pixels all follow the sky function, so nothing of it is missing at these two views (inference from the replay, not from the cube's clip positions).
4. *The scene at `0x199E0000`:* the pre-post scene, r, g, b, a in that order, with the run's `c20.w` (8.44, not 16) in it; an earlier frame's by about one (above).
5. *The clear colour:* not found; not visible.

**What plan Task 3 can rely on.**

- Read 512 bytes at `fetch[4].base` and 1,024 at `fetch[5].base` (dword 1 & `0xFFFFF000`), at the first fogged main-scene draw; decode as in the table above (`decode_tf4`, `decode_tf5`; `tests/test_fog_tables.py` pins both on literal bytes, and the bytes of frame 1 of `092459` are `native_tex_20261009_092459\1FAB5000_*.bin` and `1FAB4000_*.bin`, a fixture for `MakeFogBlock`).
- Pin in `MakeFogBlock`, besides width, format and endian: 1D, the swizzles `0x688` and `0x60A`, sign fields (1 1 1 1 and 0), exponent adjust 0, clamp to edge, linear filter. All are constant over the 28 frames.
- The tables are whole at that draw (one content per frame over all sampling rows). The capture reads on the guest thread at the draw, as the discovery dump did.
- The sky block: at the in-scene `0x82217EE8` call with pixel shader `F760...`. Its textures decode in the texture cache (format 6, 16 x 16, linear layout, wrap); here they are all zero and `c47.x` is 0, so the clear-sky term is the whole sky of the captured scenes.
- `c20.w` is not a constant of the game (16.0 and 8.44 in these runs): what the native exposure stands in for moves with the game's own adaptation when that works.

**Older tools on the new rows.** `albedo_finder.py` on `092459` against the same place before the change (`native_discovery_20261009_065904.jsonl`): the same 16 pixel-shader and 5 vertex-shader proposals, equal but for the evidence text and three draw counts. `terrain_replay.py --frame 1 --check-dumps`: the same 125 lines but for addresses of streamed textures and the two fog tables, which now have rows.

**Limits.** Daylight, two places less than 1 unit apart looking two ways, both away from the fog axis. The three runs are `RUN UNCHECKED`. The capture's last small changes (the tables outside the byte budget; a content marked as dumped only after its file is written) were built and not run in the game.

### Fog block

Plan Task 3 (commit 5cd4f47 and the commit of this subsection): the capture builds a fog block and a sky block for each frame. Nothing is drawn with them yet; the switch `--fable2_native_fog` is off by default until plan Task 6.

**What is read, and when** (`fog_block.h`, pure; `capture.cpp` `ReadFogBlock`, `ReadSkyBlock`). Only in a frame with records and with the fog wanted (a composite view, textures, the light and the fog's switch on; latched at the frame boundary with the records, as the shadows are). With the switch or the view off nothing is read.

- *Fog block*, once a frame, at the frame's first main-scene draw that is not depth-only and whose pixel shader is one of the 40 of `fog_shader_table.inc` (generated from `light_formulas.FOG_SHADERS` by `gen_fog_table.py`): pixel `c28`, `c64` to `c68` through `ReadPixelConstant` (none is a register a constant-buffer load can name: a static assert), the fetch constants of slots 4 and 5 from the device, and 512 + 1,024 bytes at the constants' base addresses. The constants are judged before any table byte is read; the bytes are copied, and the copy is what is hashed and decoded.
- *Sky block*, once a frame, at the main-scene call of `DrawIndx:82217EE8` that draws the sky. The draw is told from the builder's other calls (sparkles, particles) without decoding its geometry: the device holds the pixel shader object at any hooked call, and the call whose shader's microcode hash is `F7601FBE485936FD` is the sky's (the reflection passes' four sky draws are outside the main-scene bracket and are never looked at). Read there: pixel `c31`, `c46`, `c47` and the fetch constants of slots 13 and 14.
- Both with the shadow paths' recheck: under the scene mutex the frame is checked again, and a read that finished after its frame ended is dropped and counted. A read that gives no block is counted with its reason and tried again at the next such draw, at most eight times a frame.

**Rules of `MakeFogBlock`** (the first that fails names the reason; an invalid block is all zero):

| Reason | Rule |
|---|---|
| `unread` | a register, a fetch constant or a table's memory could not be read |
| `register` | every component of the six registers is finite |
| `amount` | `c28.x`, `c28.y` in [0, 4] |
| `axis` | the length of `c66.xyz` is 1 within 1e-3 |
| `magnitude` | beyond the spec (review of plan Task 3, M2): none of the components the fog reads (`c67.x`, `.z`, `.w`, `c68.rgb`; `c28.xy` and the axis have their own bounds) beyond 1e6 in magnitude (`kFogRegisterLimit`), so that no product downstream can overflow. Narrowed by the review of plan Task 4 (M2): as first built every component of the six registers was bound, the sky's `c64`, `c65`, `c67.y` and the unread ones among them; the sky's magnitudes are judged where the sky is decided (`SkyRules`) |
| `range` | `c67.x` >= 0, `c67.z` >= 0, `c67.w` > 0 |
| `tf4-<property>`, `tf5-<property>` | the table's fetch constant: `dimension` (a texture constant, 1D), `base` (an address; beyond the spec), `width` (64 / 256), `format` (29 / 6, and the number format bit of dword 3: 1 / 0), `endian` (8-in-16 / 8-in-32), `swizzle` (`0x688` / `0x60A`), `sign` (1 1 1 1 / 0), `exp-adjust` (0), `clamp` (clamp to edge along the table), `filter` (magnification and minification linear), `mip` (highest mip level 0); `bytes`: exactly 512 / 1,024 |
| `tf4-texel` | every half float of tf4 is finite, the alpha too (tf5's are bytes) |

The sky block: `c31.x`, `c46.x`, `c47.x` finite (`register`); beyond the spec, `c31.x` >= 0, `c46.x` >= 0 and `c47.x` in [0, 1] (`range`). Only the x of each register is judged; the two fetch constants are carried as they are (a texture the pass cannot decode is plan Task 5's `sky-texture`).

*Rules beyond the spec* (spec design 3 lists the others): the magnitude bound, a base address that is not 0, the number format bit and the mip level of the tables' constants, and the sky block's three ranges. They hold in every captured frame; **they are untested at night and indoors**, where a frame they refuse would be drawn without fog or sky and counted with the reason. Not pinned: the clamp of the two axes a 1D texture does not have, and the lowest mip level.

*Changed by the review of plan Task 3* (the fix round at the head of plan Task 4; the run below was made with the rules as first built). As first built the fog block also refused `c67.y` < 0 (the sky's path height) and a negative component of `c64` or `c65` (reason `extinction`), because they make the sky's `exp(-(l1 c64 + l2 c65))` grow. The fog reads none of the three, so those two rules are gone: a night or an interior in which the game leaves a sky register negative keeps its fog. The three values are held finite and bounded like every component, and their signs are judged where the sky is decided (plan Task 5: no sky, counted `sky-block`). Added in the same round: `magnitude`, the number format bit, `mip`. `ReadFogBlock` now gets its reason from `MakeFogBlock` alone (called first without table bytes), so a frame with two faults is named in the one documented order. A builder call in the main scene whose pixel shader cannot be told is counted as a sky try with `unread` (at most eight a frame, without using up the eight reads), so such a frame does not read `no-draw`.

A frame's reason when it has no block: `off` (not wanted), `no-draw` (no fogged draw, or no sky draw: a menu, a loading screen, an interior), else the last failed read's.

**Evidence of the table read.** `FrameScene::fog_source` holds, per table, the address read and the XXH3 hash of the decoded bytes: the hash a discovery capture writes as a table's `"content"` and in the rows' `"tfc"`. It goes to the log and to the frame row, to no shader. The periodic line (every 300 frames, with records): `[native] capture: frame N fog: block valid, tries T, c28 (..) c66 (..) c67 (..) c68 (..) tf4 0x<address> <hash> tf5 0x<address> <hash> | sky valid, tries T, c31.x a c46.x b c47.x c tf13 0x<dword> tf14 0x<dword> | fog-block in F of W frames {reason: n} | sky-block in S of W frames {reason: n} | dropped at a frame's end D`. A discovery frame row carries `"fog"`: the registers, both sources, the decoded tables (192 + 768 numbers) and the sky block.

**For plan Task 4** (ruling B). The trees' form needs nothing more in the block: its tables are the block's (tf16 is tf5, tf17 is tf4), its axis and range are the block's (vertex `c110`, `c111`), its eye is the light block's (vertex `c9`). *The water's vertex shader is not a tree.* `BEAD84BD72072E0E` (the water's by the research's table, pairs `BEAD` / `F6D9` and `BEAD` / `A17D`; with `F6D9...` in the rows read here; 22 to 24 main-scene rows a frame) samples slot 16 alone: its microcode (`out/shader_dump`, instructions 3 to 19) fetches one component of a 2D texture at the vertex's own coordinates (instruction 9; in the rows a 64 x 64 `k_8` texture, tiled, at `0x1BD03000` / `0x1BD05000`: not tf5) and passes it on in `o3`; it reads `c9` for a term of the view vector in `o0.w` and neither `c110`, `c111` nor a second table. It has no fog block and does not belong in `FOG_VERTEX_SHADERS`; the water is fogged in its pixel shader. `fog_tables.py` took a frame's "first tree row" as the first row sampling slot 16, which was this shader's; it now needs slots 16 and 17. No report used that row (the trees report counts tables by their kept content, and the water's texture is not kept by content), so no number of "Discovery" changes.

### Native fog

Plan Task 4 (2026-10-09; commits `bc7d404`, `2487da6` and the commit of this subsection). With `--fable2_native_fog=on` (the default since plan Task 6; `off` when this was measured) every lit pixel of the clay pass is fogged (since the fix wave: but for the one lit shader without fog; "After the reviews: the fix wave") with the game's arithmetic and the frame's own tables. The rules are in `src/native/render/clay_logic.h`, "Native fog"; `test_clay_logic.cpp` cases 580 to 587, `test_native_shaders.cpp` 200 to 204, `test_material.cpp` 398 to 404 and `tests/test_fog_literals.py` hold them; `tools/xdk_sigmatch/fog_pins.py` made the pinned numbers from `light_formulas.py`. The sky was not drawn when this was measured (plan Task 5, "Native sky" below): above the ridge the native picture of these runs shows its clear colour.

| | Native |
|---|---|
| Ground form | terrain layers, far terrain, objects, instanced plants: `light_formulas.fog` term for term (`FogMirror`): beyond the start `c67.x`, `C * T + (1 - T) * c28.y * (c68 + sat(c67.z * dD) * (tf4(angle) - c68))`, applied by the amount `c28.x` |
| Trees' form | trunks and leaves (ruling B): `C * T + (1 - T) * tf4(angle) * c8.x` for `dD > 0`, no blend from `c68`, no `c28.x` (`TreeFogMirror`), evaluated per pixel. `c8.x` is the draw's own vertex register, read with its light inputs (`LightInputs::tree_fog`); a draw without a usable one (unread, not a number, outside 0 to 4) keeps its light and is drawn without fog, counted |
| Place | after the family's lit colour (an object's and a tree's `c49` included), before `c26` and the exposure that stands in for `c20.w`; each terrain layer before its blend; the far terrain before its cross-fade. As measured in this subsection only lit pixels were fogged; an unlit draw of a fogged frame is fogged since plan Task 6 ("Unlit draws and the reviews' fixes" below) |
| Tables | arrays in the frame's constant block, read by hand as `table_1d`: `clamp(sat(u) * N - 0.5, 0, N - 1)`, the texels `i` and `min(i + 1, N - 1)`, a linear blend (`FogTableRead`) |
| World position | rebuilt per pixel from its own `SV_Position` through the frame's inverse view-projection (`FogPixelWorld`; the mask step's view, `FrameInverseViewProj`, asked once for both) |
| Without fog | the fog's tail of the frame's constants is all zero and one flag (`f_fog_on`) keeps every table unread: the switch off, no light, no valid fog block, a value the pass will not hand a shader, no usable eye, no single view. Counted by reason under `fog-block` (`DecideClayFog`, `CountClayFogFrame`) |

**Built differently from the spec** (the controller's two rulings of 2026-10-09; for plan Task 6's "Built differently").

- *The tables are not textures* (spec Design 4: "two small textures"). The clay layout uses 12 of the RHI's 12 binding parameters and no SDK change is allowed, so the two tables travel as `float4 f_scatter[64]` and `float4 f_transmit[256]` in cbuffer Frame. There is no texture, upload, barrier or neutral object; the read is the reference's exactly (a sampler's filter weight has 8 fractional bits). Cost: the frame's block grew from 112 to 5,344 bytes and is written whole each frame; a table read is two dynamically indexed loads and a blend. The binding layout itself did not change (12 parameters, 56 root words, the same registers, b2 bound at offset 0 for the whole frame); the block is now the head of the frame's constant buffer, 21 small slots (`kClayFrameSlots`), and the terrain, plant and mask slots follow it. The buffer's size stays a multiple of 64 KB (the block's 20 more slots can move a frame that was near a step to the next one). The tail is declared by the three lit pixel shaders' colour programs alone (`CLAY_FOG`); the vertex shader, the flat shader and the depth-only programs declare the 112 bytes they declared before. The in-scatter table lies at byte 224 (register 14), where the sky step can read it.
- *The world position is not an interpolator.* The game's fogged shaders get the pixel's world position from the vertex shader. The native vertex shader hands on a mesh's position as stored (model space for objects, trunks and skinned meshes), so one source serves every family: `S = (2 x / W - 1, 1 - 2 y / H, z, 1)`, `P = inverse . S / w`, with `(x, y, z)` the pixel's own `SV_Position`. In the clay pass `z` is the clip `z / w` of the draw's own vertex shader for every family: one vertex shader writes `o.pos = c`, the viewport's depth range is 0 to 1, no clay pipeline has a depth bias, and it is the value the pre-pass writes and the mask reads (read from the code; the far regions below are the measurement). Blended draws use their own depth. A frame without a single view (a scene without ground, plants and leaves, such as an interior) is drawn without fog and counted. **The error of the rebuilt position**, computed on the CPU at exact points with the bridge frame's captured matrices in single precision (case 587; 1,990 points from 1 to 2,020 units; the rasteriser's interpolated depth adds an error that nobody measured, and the stretched crop under "Banding" is the only evidence of it from the GPU): its distance from the eye is off by up to 2.19 units within 1,000 units and 6.13 units at 2,007 (0.79 of a texel of the transmittance table, 7.8 units), and by under 0.01 units within 40 units, where a pixel changes from unfogged to fogged. The near plane is at about 0.1 units and the inverse's rows cancel; an estimate of 0.25 units at 1,000 made before the measurement was wrong.
- *The trees* take ruling B's form, not the shared function of spec ruling 4 (frame map, "Discovery").

**Guards** (plan, Review Focus 2). A pixel keeps its colour when the frame's flag is clear, when `w` is zero or not below 3e38, when its squared distance from the eye is not above 0 and below 1e30 (`kFogDistance2Max`: one comparison that is also false for a position that is no number), or when it is not past the start; the tables are read inside a branch. The distance is `d2 * rsqrt(d2)` (the pixel shaders call no square root). The constants come from `MakeClayFogConstants` and `SetClayFrameFog`: every register a number inside the block's own bounds, every entry of the matrix and every texel a number, or the whole tail zero; `SetClayFrameFog` makes every byte of the tail zero before it writes anything, so a frame without fog holds nothing of an earlier frame (case 584). Two differences from the reference, neither reachable with a valid block: the distance bound, and a start below 0 with the pixel at the eye (the reference fogs with angle 0; the mirror and the shader leave the pixel).

**Fog off is the picture of sub-project 8, by the programs** (`task4_old_new_programs.txt`, tool `task4_old_new_programs.cpp`: every clay shader of commit `bc7d404`, whose shader text is sub-project 8's, and of the working tree compiled with `light_mode` fixed at each of its 128 values and compared line for line). The vertex, flat, shadow-map and the three depth-only programs: 128 of 128 the old program. The textured, layer and far shaders: the 64 programs without the lit bit the old program; the 64 lit ones longer by 62 to 68 lines; and with the fog's flag a constant 0 in the place of the block's word, **all 64 lit programs of each shader are the old lit program line for line**. So what a frame without fog runs differs from sub-project 8 only by the fog's coordinates being formed from a zero matrix and thrown away. Case 201 of `test_native_shaders.cpp` holds the same inside the suite, with two controls.

### Native sky

Plan Task 5 (2026-10-09; commit `6b4a0ea` and the commit of this subsection). With `--fable2_native_fog=on` (the default since plan Task 6; `off` when this was measured) a fogged frame also gets the game's sky, drawn by one step of the clay pass in the place of the game's sky draw. The rules are in `src/native/render/clay_logic.h`, "Native sky"; `test_clay_logic.cpp` cases 588 to 594, `test_native_shaders.cpp` 205 to 209 and `tests/test_sky_literals.py` hold them; `tools/xdk_sigmatch/sky_pins.py` made the pinned numbers from `light_formulas.py`. Evidence files: `task5_*` and `task5b_*`.

| | Native |
|---|---|
| Geometry | one full-screen triangle (`kSkyVs`) instead of the game's cube, which only supplies a direction (spec ruling 5) |
| Depth | the pass keeps the game's clip z (0 near, 1 far) and clears the depth to 1.0; the triangle is at `z = w = 1`, exactly the clear value, tested **less-or-equal** (the mirror of the game's greater-or-equal on its reversed depth), no depth write, no blend, no cull. It lands exactly where the depth is still the clear value |
| Place | before the first drawn record that blends and is no terrain record, after the last record when there is none (`SkyPlace`). The pass draws its records in the game's order: the opaque group, the terrain layers (blended, **with** depth write), the game's sky, the blended group with opaque draws in it (main-scene rows of captures `120428` and `121150` by depth and blend word) |
| Arithmetic | `light_formulas.sky` term for term (`SkyMirror`): the in-scatter table at `sat(n . c66)` times `1 - exp2(-1.4426950 * (l1 * c64 + l2 * c65))`, the paths from `|n.z|^0.2`, `c67.y`, `c31.x`, `c46.x`; with the textures `lerp(that, lerp(tf13^2, tf14^2, c47.x), alpha)`; the lat-long coordinate by the game's own polynomials and literals (`SkyLatLong`), not `atan2` / `asin`; through the lit draws' exposure |
| View ray | `ray0 + X * rayx + Y * rayy`, three vectors made on the CPU in double from the rows of the frame's view-projection (`SkyRayBasis`: `r0 x r1 + X (r1 x r3) + Y (r3 x r0)`); it reads no depth, no depth row and no eye |
| Bindings | a layout of its own, like the mask step: the frame's block at b2 (the in-scatter table at byte 224, the axis, the exposure, 1 / the target's size), 112 bytes of constants in one small slot of the frame's constant buffer at b0, the two sky textures at t0 and t1, four static samplers. The clay layout keeps its 12 parameters |
| Textures | from the texture cache by the sky block's two fetch constants (the cache judges a constant before it follows its address and bounds the read); the second only when `c47.x` > 0; `SampleLevel(..., 0)`; wrap or clamp by the fetch constant. A texture that cannot be had: the clear-sky term alone, counted `sky-texture` (also when the missing texture's content would not have mattered: the pass does not read the guest's texels to find out, so the count is of what was not drawn, not of what would have shown) |
| Without a sky | nothing is drawn for it and the clear colour stays: the fog's switch off, no light, no fog (no fog block, refused values, no eye, no single view), no valid sky block, a value the sky's own rules refuse (`SkyRules`), no ray, the step's objects failed. Counted by reason on the `Sky:` line (`DecideClaySky`, `CountClaySkyFrame`) |

**The sky's own rules** (`SkyRules`; the review of plan Task 3 took them out of the fog block, the review of plan Task 4 their magnitudes too). No sky, counted `sky-block` with the rule, when `c67.y` < 0 (`height`), a component of `c64` or `c65` < 0 (`extinction`), `c31.x` or `c46.x` < 0 (`path`), `c47.x` outside 0 to 1 (`blend`), or any of them or the axis is no number or beyond 1e6 (`value`; the sky block has no upper bound on its paths). Inside the rules both paths are not negative and E lies in 0 to 1. None of these has occurred in a run: they are held by case 590 alone.

**Built differently from the spec and the brief** (for plan Task 6's "Built differently").

- *The view ray is formed from the view-projection's rows, not from its inverse* (spec Design 5: "from the frame's inverse view-projection (the shadow mask's)"). It is the same line. Measured on the bridge frame's matrices at the picture's centre, edges and corners (case 593, 49 pixels): 0.000063 pixel this way; 0.139 pixel (1.2e-4 radian) for the ray through the single-precision inverse at two depths, whose rows cancel.
- *The native sky is at the far plane, the game's is a cube of half-size 2,850 around the eye.* The far plane of the bridge frame lies at about 5,000 units (the inverse's w row at depth 1: 2.0e-4). Ground farther than the cube's face is covered by the sky in the game and is drawn natively (hazed to the table's last texel). Measured from the read-back depth (`task6_far_ground.txt`, every second pixel; plan Task 6, the review's M6): the farthest ground is 1,183 units from the eye at the bridge (capture `132250`) and 212 units in the pitched view towards the sun (capture `134312`); no pixel lies beyond 2,850. The third spot has no read-back capture; its far ranges are the bridge's, seen from 1 unit away.
- *A frame without fog has no sky*: the step reads the fog's tail of the frame's block and the lit exposure. Besides the plan's list this takes the sky away from a frame whose fog values are refused or whose eye is not usable.
- *Records before the sky that write no depth* are covered by it where nothing else wrote depth under them, as the game's sky covers the game's own draws; the `Sky:` line counts them (`before it R records, D without depth write`). D is 0 in every line of every run.

**Guards** (plan, Review Focus 2). A ray without a length or beyond 3e38 squared counts as (0, 0, 0): the table's first texel and the horizon's paths; the power of a zero `|n.z|` is 0; the arctangent's ratio is 0 at the poles (the console's zero product); the textures are read inside a branch on the block's flag; the output is `clay_lit`: 0 for a value that is no number, at most 64. Case 207 holds the compares, the table's float and integer clamps and the branch on the compiled program, with three controls; case 589 feeds the mirror every constant, sample and texel as NaN, infinity and 3e38.

### Unlit draws and the reviews' fixes

Plan Task 6, Part A (2026-10-09; the commit "Native fog: unlit draws ..."), built before the validation runs. Rulings of the controller after the reviews of plan Tasks 4 and 5.

**Unlit draws are fogged** (`clay_logic.h`, "Unlit draws"; `UnlitFogOf`, which the fix wave replaced by `DrawFogOf` ("After the reviews: the fix wave": an unlit trunk or leaf, the alpha factor's draws and the bound are changed there), `UnlitFogMirror`; cases 595 and 596 of `test_clay_logic.cpp`, 210 to 212 of `test_native_shaders.cpp`; `tests/test_fog_literals.py`). The game fogs every draw whose pixel shader has the fog block. A draw the pass does not light (a family it has no function for: the water `F6D9...`, the fur, the blended characters; or a draw whose light inputs could not be read) is drawn as flat clay or with its texture alone, and until here it stood unhazed against hazed ground (the flat brown water of the lake's near part, the two beige hills at the third spot).

| | Native |
|---|---|
| Which draws | a drawn record without light, in a frame whose fog is drawn, whose pixel shader is one of the 40 of `fog_shader_table.inc` (the record's `material.ps_hash`: no record field was added). A record whose shader is not in the table stays unfogged and is counted |
| Form | `light_formulas.fog` (the ground form) on the draw's **unlit colour**, with the in-scatter term times the frame's exposure: `G = U * T + (1 - T) * c28.y * exposure * F`. A lit value is multiplied by the exposure after its fog and an unlit value is not, so this gives an unlit pixel the in-scatter a lit pixel at the same place gets. The colour under the haze stays the placeholder it was (flat clay, or the texture with the facet shade): at 1,000 units, where T is about 0.3, the haze is most of the pixel; near the start the placeholder shows as before |
| The blended form | for the ten shaders the table marks `alpha` (the game multiplies their in-scatter by the pixel's alpha and draws them blended one / inverse source alpha) the in-scatter is also multiplied by the textured draw's own alpha, saturated. **An approximation**: the game's factor is its output alpha before `c26.w`, the native one is the material's alpha (the texture's alpha times the draw's scale constant) |
| Place | the flat shader's return, the textured shader's two unlit returns and the terrain shaders' unlit return, each on the value it writes. For an unlit far-terrain draw that fades in this is after its cross-fade, not before it as in the lit path and the game (no such draw has occurred in a run: every terrain record of every run was lit) |
| How a draw is told | two bits of the draw's `light_mode` above the light's seven: 128 (`kLightModeUnlitFog`) and 256 (`kLightModeUnlitFogAlpha`). Only the pixel stage reads them, and only in a draw without the lit bit. The flat shader `kClayPs` now declares cbuffer Frame with the fog's tail (b2 is bound for the whole frame in every drawn frame; no binding changed) |

*Fog off: equal.* Restated from "Native fog", whose statement was "the 64 programs without the lit bit are the old programs": with the unlit fog's bits clear, every program of the four shaders is line for line the program it was (case 166 for the flat shader at all 128 modes, case 201 for the three others; `task6_old_new_programs.txt`: 22 programs of this tree against commit `c8fb1db`, lit and unlit, all the same listing). With the bits set and the frame's flag a constant 0, the program is line for line the unlit program of the mode without them (case 210: 4 shaders x 64 unlit modes x 2 bit patterns). So a frame without fog draws every unlit draw with the instructions it had. The lit programs did not change at all (the unlit form is a function of its own, `FogUnlit`).

*The lake.* What the pictures show as the lake is two things. The water near the shore is `F6D9...` (11 draws at the third spot; in the table, of the plain form): drawn flat, fogged since this task. The far surface out to the horizon is `2B091BD0C45A7454` (`FOG_NOT_OF_THE_FORM`): one draw a frame through the indexed builder `DrawIndx:82217EE8` (8 vertices, 30 indices: the sky cube's box without its top, with the cube's literal 2,850; row 433 of frame 1 of capture `134312`), and **the pass makes no record of that builder's draws, so it is not drawn at all** and nothing was decided for it: where the game has pale far water the native picture has whatever lies behind (ground, or sky). It goes to the follow-ups with the water.

**The Fog line** gained `unlit F fogged (A by their alpha), X without a fog block` (the text of binary `7242edb`; the final line is in "After the reviews: the fix wave") and `O records with another view` (review of plan Task 4, M3): the frame's records whose matrix is not the frame's one view-projection (`FrameView::outliers`; the Shadow line has the same number). Their pixels are fogged with the majority's inverse, so with a wrong position; object, trunk and skinned records do not vote at all. No log of any run has an outlier.

**From the review of plan Task 5.** M2: case 207 of the shader test holds the arctangent's ratio guard where it stands (the comparison of the divisor with 0 on the line before the one division, its result and-ed onto the ratio within two lines), with a control; the other guards of that case are found anywhere in the listing, and that each feeds what it guards is shown by reading the listing (the two reviews), not by the test. M3: a frame without its constant buffer is `no objects`, not `sky-block: value`. M4: the `sky changed` line is also written when a drawn sky gains or loses its textures, so that a software-adapter run shows the textured step under the debug layer. M1: the Sky line names the pixel shader of the record the sky is drawn before and counts the frames whose sky came before a terrain record (`early`). M5: case 592's exhaustive part (137,257 lists) tests the place rule's arithmetic against a model that shares its premises: the counts, the bound, "no blended record that is no terrain record before the place" and "a covered record implies no depth writer before it" are real checks, "nothing at or after the place is under the sky" follows from the model's own line; it says nothing about whether the game's order is what the rule assumes, which rests on two captures and has run 411's line as an exception.

**The clouds, and what else the game draws after its sky** (review of plan Task 5, I1; `task6_134312_after_sky.txt`, `task6_after_sky.py`: the in-scene rows of frame 1 of capture `134312` from the sky row on; `task6_after_sky_tex\sheet.png`: the textures of those rows through `texture_thumb.py`, viewed). The sky row is row 426 of 461. After it, through the same indexed builder `DrawIndx:82217EE8`, none of them a record of the native pass:

| Rows | Pixel / vertex shader | Geometry, blend word, depth word | Texture (viewed) | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 427 | `18D39DCEBEE4C2FC` / `81BADE63A169E3DC` | 1 quad; `0x07060706`; `0x00708762` | tf13 at `0x16E60000`, 1024 x 128, DXT4/5: eight phases of the moon in a strip | the moon (inference from the texture) |
| 428 to 430 | `61976295517D7015` / `C304C6A1AF18B46F` | 3 quads; `0x07060706` (source alpha, inverse source alpha by the register's fields: my decode); `0x00708766` | tf13 at `0x163E0000` (two rows) and `0x15CC0000` (one), 512 x 512, DXT4/5: grey-brown cloud colour with a cloud-shaped alpha | **the clouds** (inference from the textures, the blend and the place right after the sky; three layers) |
| 431, 432 | `7F65142C12BEB353` / `43ED37430887A46C` | 144 vertices, 768 indices each; `0x00080008`; `0x00708762` | tf13 is the scene's depth at `0x1A02A000` | not identified: a mesh that reads the depth and multiplies the picture (the sun's shafts or the `b129` volume are guesses) |
| 433 | `2B091BD0C45A7454` / `5763211D63BBFA3D` | 8 vertices, 30 indices; `0x00010001` | the two fog tables, tf2 | the lake's far surface (above) |
| 455, 456 (the scene's end) | `04985A0F7296E130` / `81BADE63A169E3DC` | 2 quads; `0x01010101` (one, one: additive) | tf13 at `0x14E60000`, 256 x 256: a soft white disc | the sun's disc and glow (inference) |

So the clouds are three blended quads of one shader pair drawn right after the sky, each with a 512 x 512 colour-and-alpha texture; they are in the picture before the post chain (the oracle shows them) and are not made in the sky shader, whose two textures are zeros. How they are placed and scrolled (the vertex shader's constants) was not read. **Ruling (controller): clouds are not drawn in this sub-project** — why: they are separate draws, not part of the sky shader — cost if wrong: the sky is plain where the game's has clouds; sky regions against the oracle hold only between clouds.

### After the reviews: the fix wave

2026-10-09, after the two whole-branch reviews of `f764cc9` (code: one Important, twelve Minor; documents: six Important, ten Minor). Commit `71f7f4e` ("Fog, final review fixes: ..."), and this subsection with the corrections in "Validation", "Limits" and "Follow-ups". **The binary of `71f7f4e` (109,885,952 bytes, sha256 `DB08588E...FFF8D5E4`) is the final binary of the sub-project and has been run** (runs 432 to 435, below); "Validation" above is of binary `7242edb` and is not repeated here.

**What changed in the code.** One rule now decides the fog of every drawn record, by the game's own pixel shader (`DrawFogOf` / `RecordDrawFog` in `clay_logic.h`; the shader's light family from the generated table through `capture::PsLightFamily`, its entry of the fog table; test cases 596 and 597 of `test_clay_logic.cpp`, 210 to 213 of `test_native_shaders.cpp`):

| The draw's pixel shader | Lit by the pass | Not lit |
|---|---|---|
| in the fog table (the 40 of the game's fog block) | its family's form, as before | the unlit form, as before; the blended form's alpha factor only where the draw's program writes an alpha of its own (a textured mesh draw), so the count `by their alpha` no longer includes flat draws |
| a trunk's or a leaf's (not in the table: a tree's fog is its vertex shader's) | the trees' form through its object block, or none without a usable scale, as before | **new:** the trees' form on the unlit colour, the in-scatter times the draw's scale `c8.x` and the frame's exposure (`light_mode` bit 1024; the product travels as the float bits of the draw's last constant word), when the record's light inputs carry a usable scale; otherwise unfogged and counted `trees without a scale` |
| any other | **new: not fogged** (`light_mode` bit 512, read by the lit path of the textured shader). This is the one lit shader without a fog block, the plant form `26052DEFBA688AF2` (22 instructions, no fog register; the controller's ruling on the code review's I1: the game does not fog it, so neither does the pass). Counted `lit N not fogged` | not fogged, counted `not in the fog table` (was `without a fog block`) |

A lit terrain record is always fogged: every terrain shader of the light table is in the fog table (case 597 holds the two tables against each other: 21 light entries, 16 in the fog table, 4 trees, the one bare plant). With bit 512 the lit program is, line for line, the lit program compiled from the text without the fog, at all 64 lit modes (case 213). The unlit fogged value is bounded like a lit one (not negative, at most 64), inside the fog's branch: with `c28.x` above 1, which the block allows up to 4, the blend could otherwise go below 0 (unreachable with the captured `c28` = (1, 1)). The CPU mirrors are not bounded.

Also: a frame drawn without light with the fog's switch on is counted `no-light` (Fog line) and `no-fog` (Sky line), and "frames since start" counts every frame with the fog's switch on (run 421's lines, of binary `7242edb`, read `no-light 0` beside `not drawn (no light)`); a frame without a constant buffer because nothing of it is drawn reads `not drawn (no light)`, not `drawn`; `PollFrame` stores the shadows' and the fog's switches before the records' when the view comes on (the records' word with release, read with acquire at the frame's boundary before the other two), so no frame is recorded without its fog block for the order of the stores; the slot plan of the frame's constant buffer is a pure function under test (`PlanClayFrameSlots`, `ClayFrameSmallSlots`; case 598); `FogShaderEntry` lost a field nothing read; the three line buffers are larger. The Fog line now reads

`Fog: on, block valid, drawn | trees T with a scale, U without | unlit F fogged (A by their alpha, R trees by their scale), S trees without a scale, X not in the fog table | lit N not fogged (no fog in their pixel shader) | O records with another view | frames since start ...`

so `task4_logs_summary.py`, `task5_logs_summary.py` and `task6_logs_summary.py` do not parse the new logs; `fix_logs_summary.py` (output `fix_logs_summary.txt`) is this wave's.

*The capture gained two things, both only with the fog wanted.* (1) A frame whose fog block was read and refused gets a line of its own (the first eight): `capture: frame N fog block refused: T reads at the frame's fogged draws gave none, the last: <reason> ...`. (2) For every frame with a block the two tables are read once more when the frame is over and their hashes held against the block's (1,536 bytes hashed a frame); the fog line ends `tables changed by the frame's end in N of M frames`. Nothing is done about a difference.

**Tests.** Written before the code (red as a compile failure on the new names; the literals test 2 failures), then: native suite 30 `PASS` lines through the scratch runner, Python `Ran 902 tests`, `OK (skipped=3)`, 18 of 18 mutants of the new pure rules killed by `test_clay_logic.cpp` (`out\tests\fogfix\`: untracked). No HLSL is executed by any of them.

*The picture* (`fix_regions_summary.txt`; shots viewed: 433 at 45 s, 434 at 47 s, 435 at 45 s, 432 at 225 s). Bridge, run 433 against run 417 (same plan, binary `7242edb`), native shot at 45 s: all 24 regions' native means agree within 0.0005 but three under moving leaf shadows (railing post cap -0.0066, planks in leaf shadow -0.0016, railing post side -0.0012); the ratios to the emulated shots are run 417's to the third decimal (far mountains 1.217, 1.027, 0.927; far peak 0.761; island 0.966 with hue -22.5; far slope 1.014 with hue -32.7; sky 0.804, 0.795). So the fix of the bare plant shows in none of the measured regions: how far its instances stand from the eye against the fog's start was not measured (the game uses the shader for more batches as the start grows: above) (the code review's estimate: under 1% at 40 units). Third spot, run 434 at 47 s: far mountains left and centre 1.062 and 0.910 (run 430: 1.091, 0.922), far rock 0.952 (0.990), sky 0.820 and 0.801 and the unlit hill 0.885 against the emulated shot at 44 s alone (the 50 s shot has the quest banner over these three regions; the table's 0.900, 0.980, 0.942 are against the mean of the two; no criterion rests on these numbers), the water 0.764; the near regions are not comparable with run 430's (the walk ended at another place again: the emulated near regions differ by factors). The native shots look as "Shots viewed" describes them.

*Criterion 2 on this binary.* `fix_165011_block.txt`: the fog block and the sky block equal the rows in 8 of 8 frames.

*Criterion 7 on this binary* (the logs' `[native] frames: view native (window): 150 frames` and `capture: ... records on` lines; `fix_logs_summary.txt` has them):

| | Bridge, fog on (433) | Third spot, fog on (434) | Bridge, fog off (435) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frame rate, steady native windows of 150 frames | 30.0 or 30.1 in all seven after the capture's window | 30.0 or 30.1 in seven of nine, **29.2 in one** and 29.8 in one | 30.0 or 30.1 in all ten |
| Guest work median | 10.9 to 12.0 ms | 12.0 to 14.5 ms | 11.6 to 14.7 ms |

| Capture, records off, in the world | 0.070, 0.087 ms | 0.065, 0.073 ms | 0.070 ms |

The verdict of criterion 7 stands, **not met as written**, on this binary too: at the third spot one window of nine at 29.2 fps, and the records-on capture median 2.64 to 2.92 ms against 2.3. At the bridge the fog-off run's medians are higher than the fog-on run's, so the fog's own part does not show in them either. View off is met.

*Run 435, the fog off.* `[native] fog: off`, `Fog: off`, `Sky: off`, `capture ... fog: off` in every line. The shot at 45 s (viewed): unhazed ranges under the dark clear colour, the water flat: sub-project 8's picture. **It cannot be held against run 418 by region**: its camera stands elsewhere in every shot, emulated ones included (the dirt patch's emulated mean 0.207 against 0.328, the rock face's 0.14 against 0.34; the view is wider), from the run's start and without any input in the plan; why the bridge's camera settled differently in this one run is not established. Criterion 6 therefore rests on what it rested on (the program comparisons, now with cases 210 and 213 on the final text, and Task 6's regions of binary `7242edb`): a substituted measure, not repeated by region on this binary.

**Run 416's refused fog block (`tf4-texel`).** The capture line of run 416 counts `fog-block in 3 of 51 frames {no-draw: 2, tf4-texel: 1}`. What the log and the code tell:
- The rule: a component of a texel of tf4 (64 texels of four half floats) was not finite, a half with all exponent bits set. The read is tried again at each next fogged draw of the frame, up to eight times, and a frame's reason is its last read's: so every read of that frame failed, the last for such a half. How many there were is not in the log.
- The frame was one of the first three with records, 250 to 252. The pass drew 250 (no record), one more frame counted `no-light`, then 253 with a valid block; its counts at 253 are `fog-block 0, no-light 2` and no later `fog changed` line exists: **no frame was drawn natively as "fog-block"**; the refused frame was not rendered, or was the second `no-light` frame (inference from `light-block in 2 of 51`).
- Those are the first frames in which the world is drawn on that adapter (the save was still loading 17 s before; the view came on at plan second 32). The best fit is a table of the world's first frame that the game had not filled yet (inference; the content was not kept). The brief's other candidate, a table read while the game writes it, is what the frame-end comparison would show: 0 of 2,682 frames in runs 432 to 434.
- Frequency: software adapter, 1 `tf4-texel` and 2 `no-draw` in 145 frames of four logs (397, 405, 416, 432), all three in run 416's first three frames; real GPU, **0 frames without a fog block in 25,409** (22,777 in 82 capture lines of the 22 logs of runs 396 to 431, and 2,632 in runs 433 and 434).
- **Ruling (controller): no retry across frames and no fallback to an earlier frame's tables** — why: a stale table must never reach a shader; one unfogged frame at the world's start is invisible — cost if wrong: a rare single unfogged frame. (Spec ruling 22; ruling 21 is the lit draw without fog, above.)

**Warning 1008** (`ResourceBarrier: Called on the same subresource(s) ... in separate Barrier Descs`): once in run 416 and once in run 432, in no other run. **Whose barrier it is is still not established; no code was changed for it.** Two patterns fit the five software-adapter runs, and they cannot be told apart from these logs:
- *By build and switch:* present in the two fog-on runs of builds from Task 6 on (416: `7242edb`; 432: `71f7f4e`), absent with the fog off (415, `7242edb`) and in the fog-on runs of earlier builds (397, 405).
- *By the guest's frames:* present in exactly the two runs whose native view covered the world's first frames (first native scene frames 250 and 251), absent in the three whose first native frame was 268, 273 or 285; and in both runs the message was polled at the start of the overlay callback that then drew **scene frame 253**.
- What speaks against the pass's fog in run 416: the layer's messages are polled before each callback's Render, so the message is older than frame 253's Render, and before it the pass had drawn only frame 250 (no record) and one frame without light: no fogged draw, no sky step (its objects were made after the poll), no unlit bit, no texture upload (the first burst line is frame 253's). In run 432 the window before the poll does hold the first fogged frame (251: the sky without textures, 1,208 unlit fogged draws, 90 uploads, the first shadow mask). What the two windows share is the guest's frames 251 to 253, which the emulator's own command stream draws in both (inference).
- The run that would tell them apart: software adapter, fog off, the view on at plan second 32 or earlier, so that the native view covers frames 250 to 253 with the fog off (run 415's came on at frame 268). Not asked for in this wave.

**Stated, not changed** (the code review's M9, M10, M12): flat clay's debug colours are hazed in a fogged frame (`--fable2_native_fog=off` gives the plain colours; the colour switch's help says so). `KeyOf`, a linear search over the pass's pipelines, runs a third time per record a frame for the sky's place: with 919 to 979 drawn records and 13 or 14 pipelines (runs 431 to 434) about 41,000 pointer comparisons a frame, 188,000 at the cache's limit of 64; not measured as time. The sky's texture coordinate is scaled by the cache's `uv_fix` (guest extent over host extent, the host extent being the guest's rounded up to the format's block: `texture_cache.cpp`) and then wrapped: the factor is 1 for an uncompressed texture and for a block-compressed one whose sides are multiples of 4, and the captured sky texture is 16 x 16 of format 6 (`tf13 0x1A544086`), so its wrap is exact; only a block-compressed sky texture with a side that is no multiple of 4 would wrap at the padded extent. When the view goes off, a frame boundary that read the records' switch just before it changed can still latch one last frame with records and without fog; the view is off by then and that frame is not drawn (by reading; not seen).

### Limits

- **No test executes the HLSL.** The shaders' fog and sky are held by reading (three reviews, with the compiled listings), by text pins, by a CPU mirror that is a second writing of the same sentences, by the compiled-program checks of the shader test (which find an instruction in a listing, and in one case where it stands) and by the pictures: the oracle's far peak within 1.4%, the sky within 2% just above the ridge with its red down to 0.85 at the top of the picture (clouds).
- **One daylight save**, one region, standing still; every run `RUN UNCHECKED`. Night, a town, an interior, weather, dawn and dusk: never seen (user checks 40 to 47).
- **One fog block has been read and refused in a run** (`tf4-texel`, run 416, software adapter, among the world's first frames; cause not established, and that frame was not drawn natively as a frame without fog); no other `fog-block`, `sky-block`, `view`, `values`, `rules` or `no-objects` path has occurred in a run with the light on, and they and the rules beyond the spec (the magnitude bound, the sky's ranges) are held by tests alone. No failure path of `ReadFogBlock` or `ReadSkyBlock` but that one has ever executed.
- **The moment of the table read** (the design's risk 2): the tables are read at the frame's first fogged draw and, if refused, at up to seven more. A refused block is never replaced by an earlier frame's (spec ruling 22): that frame is drawn without fog. That a table changes while its frame is drawn has not been seen: the bytes were the same at the frame's end in 2,682 of 2,682 frames of runs 432 to 434. An interior has no single view and so no fog and no sky (counted `view`); whether the game fogs interiors is not known.
- **The sky's texture term has never been seen with content**: both textures are zeros and `c47.x` is 0 in every capture. `sky-texture` counts a missing texture also when its content would not have mattered.
- **Clouds, the sun's disc and glow, the moon** are draws of their own after the sky and are not drawn; sky regions hold against the oracle only between and away from them.
- **The sky is at the far plane, the game's is a cube of half-size 2,850 units** around the eye: ground beyond the cube's face is under the sky in the game and drawn natively. The farthest ground measured is 1,183 units (bridge; `task6_far_ground.txt`); the third spot has no read-back capture.
- **The rebuilt position** is off by up to 6 units at 2,000 by CPU arithmetic at exact points (case 587); the rasteriser's interpolated depth adds an error nobody measured.
- **Records of another view** than the frame's majority are fogged with the majority's inverse, a wrong position; object, trunk and skinned records do not vote. Counted on the Fog line; 0 in every run.
- **The texel addressing of the two tables** is the reference's by construction and bounded against the game to a few texels (tf4, run 413) and to several texels (tf5, the far peak), not to half a texel.
- **Unlit draws** are fogged over a placeholder colour; the blended form's alpha factor is the material's alpha, not the game's; an unlit far-terrain draw would be fogged after its cross-fade; an unlit trunk or leaf has the trees' form only when its light inputs carry the scale (otherwise unfogged, counted). The lake's far surface `2B09...` is not drawn. Flat clay's debug colours are hazed in a fogged frame.
- **Which lit draws the game fogs** is decided by two generated tables (the pixel shaders with a light family, those with the fog block); the one lit shader outside the fog table, `26052DEF...`, is left unfogged. How far its instances stand from the eye was not measured, and its count on the Fog line follows the fog's start (3 to 14 at the bridge), because the game itself moves plant batches to this shader as the start passes them; that those batches lie wholly inside the start, so that nothing visible depends on the ruling, is an inference.
- **`c20.w`**, the game's own exposure, is 7.4 to 8.6 under read-back and 16 in normal runs; the native exposure is one fixed number. The display clips the sky's red towards the axis and its blue near the horizon under it.
- **The dirt patch and the rock face are 21 to 24% brighter than the oracle** (not fog: both are at or inside the start).
- **The sky's place** assumes the game's order (opaque, terrain layers, sky, blended): two captures show it, run 411 has one line with the sky early; case 592's exhaustive part tests the rule against a model that shares its premises. The finiteness rule of the fog block judges the sky's registers too: a register that is no number is a bad read of the block, and costs the frame its fog.
- **Costs** are from a machine in use; nothing times the fog or the sky on the GPU. **The records-on capture median is over its limit of 2.3 ms at the third spot with the fog off as well** (2.43 to 2.64 ms on Task 6's afternoon, where run 412 at midday read 2.14 to 2.23; 2.64 to 2.92 with the fog on in run 434): not explained beyond "the machine's state" (inference), and the fog's own part has never shown outside the runs' spread.
- **The final binary's fog-off run (435) could not be compared by region** (its camera stood elsewhere); fog off equal to sub-project 8's picture rests on the compiled programs and on binary `7242edb`'s regions.

### Follow-ups

1. **The post chain** (sub-project 10): the exposure table at `0x1FAA0000` and `c20.w`, bloom, the half-resolution quads, grading. It is what remains between the native picture and the game's final one where both draw the same things (the sky at 0.80, the hue of the far grass).
2. **Tree billboards** on the far hills: the largest remaining difference of the far picture (the two ranges at 1.28 and 1.45 of the oracle).
3. **Water and the lake**: the water `F6D9...` / `A17D...` is a fogged placeholder; the far surface `2B09...` (not of the fog's form; through the indexed builder) is not drawn.
4. **Clouds**: three blended quads of `61976295517D7015` / `C304C6A1AF18B46F` through `DrawIndx:82217EE8` right after the sky, 512 x 512 colour-and-alpha textures; placement and scrolling not read ("Unlit draws and the reviews' fixes"). **The moon** (`18D39DCEBEE4C2FC` / `81BADE63A169E3DC`, a strip of eight phases) and **the sun's disc and glow** (`04985A0F7296E130` / `81BADE63A169E3DC`, additive, at the scene's end), by inference from their textures; the depth-reading mesh `7F65142C12BEB353` is not identified. All need records of the indexed builder first.
5. **The `b129` volume** (ground fog; never set in a capture; unchecked in the formulas).
6. **Night, town, interior, weather**: user checks 40 to 47; the counters say what happened.
7. **The red dog on the software adapter**: red with the fog off too (run 415), in four of four software-adapter runs of this sub-project and in none of sub-project 8's three; never on the real GPU. An albedo with no green or blue, lit and clamped; the dog's texture is one the emulator reads back from its own GPU (`0x12704000`, forced every frame). Upstream of the fog; not followed.
8. **The freeze-like state of run 424**: guest work 42 to 45 ms without a wait at the swap, 22 fps, from before the native view; once in this task's eighteen runs; cause not established.
9. **Warning 1008 on the software adapter** (runs 416 and 432, once each): whose barrier is not established. Tried: reading every barrier call of the pass, the texture cache and the composite (no resource twice in one flush on a path that ran); placing the message by its poll in both logs (before scene frame 253's Render in both; in run 416 before any fogged draw, sky step or upload of the pass). Two patterns fit and are not separated: fog on with a build from Task 6 on, or a native view that covers the world's first frames (250 to 253). The run that separates them: software adapter, fog off, the view on by plan second 32 so that it covers those frames. The shared barrier queue of the native RHI and the emulator is still the first place to look.
10. **The window's size**: the game opens 1280 x 720 logical pixels on whichever monitor Windows gives it; runs 405 to 408 were 1296 x 759 (another monitor or scaling, inference) and one of them read 25 fps at the third spot. Not repeated: every run of this task was 1942 x 1136.
11. **The sky early** in one line of run 411: the Sky line now names the record and counts such frames.
12. **Anti-aliasing** (the horizon's silhouettes are stair-stepped), later, as its own sub-project.
13. **The `tf4-texel` frame of run 416**: a table that was not whole at the read, among the world's first frames on the software adapter. The capture now writes a line for such a frame (frame, reads, reason) and counts tables that change within their frame; a run in which it recurs will say more. No retry across frames (spec ruling 22).
14. **The capture median with the records on**, over 2.3 ms at the third spot with the fog off too: a repeat on a machine known to be quiet, fog off and on, against run 412's 2.14 to 2.23.
15. **The dirt patch and the rock face**, 21 to 24% brighter than the oracle inside the fog's start: not fog; the light's or the exposure's.
16. **HLSL executed in a test** (a software rasteriser or a compute path): the y flip and rows of `FogCoords`, the unlit forms, the sky; and the failure paths of `ReadFogBlock` / `ReadSkyBlock` exercised in a run.
17. **The bare plant `26052DEF...`**: the distance of its instances against the fog's start.
18. **Run 435's camera**: the bridge's emulated picture stood elsewhere in one run of four with the same plan; cause not established.
19. **A tally by pixel shader on the Fog line** (the fix wave's review, C1; not built): `lit N not fogged {shader: N}`, as the Light line has it for unlit draws. The reason: the count of lit draws not fogged moves by itself, as the game swaps plant batches to `26052DEF...` with the fog's start, so a second, wrongly excluded shader would not stand out in the bare number (ruling 21's cost).

## 17. The post chain

Sub-project 10 (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-native-renderer-post-design.md`, plan
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-09-native-renderer-post.md`): the game's exposure, composite,
bloom, sun layer and sky furniture. This section grows task by task.

### Discovery

Plan Task 1, capture only: nothing the pass draws changed. Evidence in
`out/native-evidence/post/` (`t1_*`); captures in `out/build/win-amd64-release/logs/`. All five
runs were made by the controller with `-UserPresent` (`RUN UNCHECKED`, the last line of each
`t1_<run>_driver.txt`), under `--readback_resolve=full`; their frame rates are no timing
evidence (a capture at every draw runs at 2 to 20 fps). What is used of them is what the
captures hold; the captures show the game advancing (the eye moves, the exposure moves). The
shots were not looked at for this section.

| Run | Log | Capture(s) | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 436 | `native_discovery_20261009_205049.jsonl`, 40 frames | bridge, standing |
| 2 | 437 | `..._205229` (4 frames, 36 s), `..._205303` (4 frames, 70 s) | the 60-frame capture was lost (its token came while the first capture was still writing) |
| 2b | 440 | `..._205802` (4 frames, 34 s), `..._205815` (60 frames from 47 s) | two turns of the camera, the second inside the long capture |
| 5a | 438 | `..._205445`, 8 frames | third spot |
| 5b | 439 | `..._205645`, 8 frames | under the trees |

**What a capture holds since this task** (commits `01caf6a`, `0ca7dc7`):

- `"resolve"` rows: every outermost call of `DrawIndx2:821EF988` (the clear routine) with the
  dwords it wrote to the command buffer (`"cmd"`, hex in guest order, at most 512 dwords;
  `"cmd_ok"`). Run 1: 2,640 rows, all with dwords (66 a frame).
- `"cmdgap"` rows: the command stream between two consecutive outermost hooked draws of a
  thread, written when it names a copy register (`0x2318..0x231B`; `NamesCopyRegisters`,
  `discovery_format.h`; at most 2,048 dwords). They exist because **the post chain's resolves do
  not pass through any hooked routine**: between the `"verts"` rows of two post rectangles no
  hooked call lies (seen first in `native_discovery_20261009_092959.jsonl`, frame 1, between the
  luminance pass's row and the bright pass's). Run 1: 54,825 rows (the copy registers are
  written with most draws' state, so most rows hold no resolve; the reader decides). **A
  stretch that is not looked at** (longer than the 2,048 dwords, the write pointer gone back at
  a change of the command buffer's segment or its wrap, no whole dwords, unreadable) is, since
  the review fixes, a `"cmdgap"` row without `"cmd"` and with `"skipped":"long"|"back"|
  "unaligned"|"unreadable"`, `"from"`, `"to"` and the distance in `"dwords"`
  (`ClassifyStream`, `SkippedGapRow`); `resolves` counts them. The captures of runs 1 to 5b
  were made before that and do not record their skipped stretches ("Review fixes" below).
- The post buffers by content: a 2D texture whose base is the front buffer `0x1ECFF000` or lies
  in [`0x12A00000`, `0x12E00000`) (`render::PostBufferBase`) is dumped once per content, formats
  7 and 54 in full; at most 1,024 content files and 512 MB of targets a capture (run 1 reached
  the bytes after frame 17: later frames have their tables only).
- Under `--readback_resolve` the block [`0x12A00000`, `0x12E00000`) whole at the end of a
  capture's frames 1 and 2 (`mem_12A00000_f<N>.bin`, a `"memdump"` row).
- In the game log, with a composite view: `[native] ramp: read at clay frame N: valid V, <2,304
  hex digits>` at the first read and at the changes after it (256 entries of nine digits
  `rrrgggbbb`, each channel the 10-bit value as three hex digits; at most 16 such lines a run
  since the review fixes, `kRampFullLogs`: a ramp that changes every frame is then only
  counted), and `[native] ramp: changes C (reads R, without a table F)` with the 300-frame lines.

`tools/xdk_sigmatch/post_tables.py` reads them: `resolves` (walks the PM4 packets of both row
kinds; a resolve is a draw packet under `RB_MODECONTROL` 6; several bases after the luminance
pass are an outcome only when they come in turn with a period, each seen at least twice:
`ring_period`), `table`, `ramp`, `find-luminance`, `downsample`.

**Question 1: where the luminance is resolved to** (`t1_run1_resolves.txt`). Outcome (i), with
a finding the plan did not expect: **two addresses in turn**. In each of run 1's 40 frames
exactly one resolve follows the `"verts"` row of the luminance pass `5821366EE8FDE893`; its
destination is `0x1A385000` in the capture's odd frames and `0x1A34F000` in its even ones (20
each; they lie `0x36000` = 221,184 bytes apart, which is the tiled size of the buffer: 280 x 180
texels of 4 bytes at pitch 288). **The same two addresses, in turn, in all seven captures of the
five runs** (`resolves` on each, outputs `t2_review_resolves_<stamp>.txt`: 2 + 2 frames in
`205229`, `205303` and `205802`, 4 + 4 in `205445` and `205645`, 30 + 30 in `205815`; which of
the two a capture's first frame has differs, `0x1A34F000` in `205229`). The limit of that: five
boots of one save at one place. The addresses are the game's allocations; another region or
another way into the game may put the buffers elsewhere, and a fixed list of addresses (Task 2)
would not follow. Both resolves are the same but for the base:

```
RB_COPY_DEST_BASE 0x1A34F000 | 0x1A385000   RB_COPY_DEST_PITCH: pitch 288, height 180
RB_COPY_DEST_INFO: format 36 (k_32_FLOAT), endian 2 (8-in-32)
RB_COPY_CONTROL 0x00100000 (copy command 1, convert; source 0; no clear)   RB_MODECONTROL 6
PM4_DRAW_INDX_2, initiator 0x00030088: rectangle list, 3 indices
```

The SDK's rule for a forced read-back (`PM4_DRAW_INDX_2`, a rectangle list, 3 indices) matches
both in all 40 frames. No other resolve has its base in [A, A + 64 KiB) for either A **among
the stretches of the command stream the capture holds** (85 to 88 resolves a frame in those).
That is not all of the stream: a stretch between two hooked draws that is longer than 2,048
dwords, or across which the write pointer went back, was not written and, in these captures,
not counted; the review counted them from the rows' own pointers (review-task-1.md, item 1):
274 stretches over the cap and 9 backward steps in run 1's 40 frames, about 7 a frame, the one
across each frame's end some 37,000 dwords. A resolve issued inside one of them is in no row.
So "nothing else in the window" is shown for the captured stretches only; the SDK's own log of the resolves it forces (the first 24 of a
run) was meant as the proof for a whole frame, but all 24 lines are of the front end ("Exposure
read-back" below): for a frame in the world it is shown for the captured stretches only. The two bases are farther apart than the SDK's 64 KiB window, so a forced list needs both
entries. The pitch is 288, not the 320 of the surface; neither address
is in the block the research and the plan looked in (`0x12A00000` on), so the memory dump could
not have held it: `find-luminance` found no plane (`t1_run1_find_luminance.txt`), which says
nothing more than that. That the CPU reads these two buffers is still the research's inference;
Task 2's run (only these addresses forced) is its proof. By the alternation the CPU can read
one buffer while the GPU fills the other (inference).

The other post resolves, as the same rows give them (frame 1): radial blurs to `0x12CFD000`
(format 7), the downsample to `0x12D33000` (format 32, `k_16_16_16_16_FLOAT`, endian 1), bright
pass and both blurs to `0x12D9F000` (format 7), all at pitch 288, height 180, all
`PM4_DRAW_INDX_2` rectangle lists of 3 indices. After each resolve the game writes the copy
control and info back to 0 and draws the next rectangle in colour mode (`RB_MODECONTROL` 4).

**Question 2: the adaptation** (`t1_run2b_series_205815.txt`, `t1_run2b_eye_205815.txt`,
`t1_run2b_table_205815.txt`; run 2b's 60 consecutive guest frames). `c20.w` falls from 9.271 to
7.738, in every frame, by at most 0.0712 a frame (0.8% of its value; frames 3 and 4), the steps
shrinking to 0.002 at the end (by about 6% a frame: 0.071 at frame 3, 0.0020 at frame 59); the
steps come in pairs of nearly equal size (-0.0706, -0.0666, -0.0662, -0.0674, -0.0669, -0.0587,
-0.0583, ..): the rate is renewed every second frame, as the two luminance buffers would have it
(inference). The table moves with it in every frame (largest change of a texel 0.0031 a frame;
T at scene luminance 1 from 0.2176 to 0.2707, `T(3) / T(0.1)` from 1.448 to 1.551). **The
bright pass's `c77.y * c20.w` is 1 within 5.7e-08 in all 60 frames** (and within 4.4e-08 in the
other 68 frames of the five runs): the pairing rule of spec ruling 11 holds while the exposure
moves; no frame would fall back.

What this capture does not show: the lag between a turn and the exposure's first move. The
camera's eye moves in frames 3 to 6 (the second turn), but the scale was already falling in
frames 1 to 3. After the turn the steps shrink pair by pair with one exception: the pair of
frames 7 and 8 (-0.0674, -0.0669) is larger than the pair before it (-0.0666, -0.0662), by 1%,
the only rise after frame 3 in the 60 frames. It may be the turn arriving, one or two frames
after the eye stopped; one bump of 1% on a settling curve proves nothing either way. The exposure was not at rest in any capture of run 2b: 12 s earlier
(`..._205802`, 34 s after the start) `c20.w` was 11.70 falling by 0.14 a frame, on its way down
from the blind 16 of the game's start; run 2's two captures show 8.845 (36 s, before its turns)
and 7.606 (70 s, after them, constant over 4 frames), the research's "8.4 to 7.4" seen as 8.85
to 7.61. So: speed measured (a step of at most 0.8% a frame, an approach by about 6% a frame),
scale and table of one frame belong together (the pairing), lag not measured.

entries, **the same 2,304 digits in all five runs**, and `changes 0` wherever a 300-frame line
was written (602, 902 and 303 reads in runs 1, 2 and 5a). Entries 0, 64, 128, 192, 255: 0, 193,
462, 741, 1023. Against the pairs of spec criterion 4 (front-buffer level to shot level,
measured on run 395's shot):

| Level | 23 | 47 | 63 | 124 | 156 | 204 | 236 | 252 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| measured on the shot | 10 | 32 | 47 | 110 | 144 | 197 | 232 | 250 |
| the table (entry * 255 / 1023) | 9.7 | 31.2 | 47.1 | 110.9 | 145.3 | 197.9 | 233.6 | 251.3 |

**Criterion 4 as written (within 1 level) is not met**: five pairs are within 1, three are off

`out/tests/post-research/ramp_092959.txt` the largest difference is 1.74 and the median 1.05,
the table the brighter from level 63 up. The table is the SDK's own, so what differs is either the
measurement (medians of a window shot scaled to the front buffer's size) or something the
presenter does after the blit (dithering or rounding to 8 bits); which, is not known. The
differences are systematic, not noise: from level 124 up all have one sign (+0.9 to +1.6), and
rounding the table to 8 bits gives at most 0.5. The table, not the eight numbers, is what Task 5

picture with the emulated picture of the same frame, not with the shot pairs.
