**Question 6: the downsample's form** (`t1_run1_downsample.txt`). Not settled. In the 17
frames of run 1 whose buffer was dumped, the content of `0x12D33000` at the luminance pass's
row is no downsample of the scene the downsample pass's row names: the nearest form in the
nearest frame differs by a median of 2.25 against a median level of 0.71. The buffer's memory
holds neither form when the capture reads it (the guest runs ahead of the GPU, and the sun
layer's 560 x 360 resolves into `0x12CFD000` reach over this address: inference from the sizes).
The four-texel form stands on the microcode reading and on variant B's fit alone, as the spec's
table of open questions provides.

**Row order** (`t1_run1_table.txt` and the others): the composite's row precedes the frame row
of the same frame in 40 of 40 frames of run 1, and in all 128 frames of the five runs: a block
read at the composite's call is in the frame's own scene (spec "Frame pairing", ruling 10).

**The ramp's source** (controller ruling 20): `src/core/sdk_gamma_ramp.h` reads the SDK's
256-entry table through `CommandProcessor::gamma_ramp_256_entry_table()`, which is a protected
member (the spec's "public accessors" was wrong for this one): named through a derived class's
using-declaration, no SDK change. The table is written on the command-processor thread (packet
execution) and read in the post-processor callback on that thread; a public accessor upstream
replaces the file. It reads the 256-entry table whatever the front buffer is; the SDK applies
that table to an 8-bit front buffer only and the piecewise-linear ramp to a `k_2_10_10_10` one.
The game's front buffer is 8-bit (format 6), and nothing checks it yet: Task 5 fails the ramp
(`post-ramp`) for any other front buffer (said in the header).

**Contradictions with the spec and the plan, in one place**: the luminance resolve has two
addresses, not one, outside the expected block, at pitch 288 (Task 2's `kLuminanceResolveBase`
and its four-case list need two addresses); the resolve rows of the plan's hook cannot see a
post resolve (`"cmdgap"` rows do); the ramp accessor is protected; criterion 4's tolerance is
not met by the table itself; the adaptation's lag was not measurable; question 6 stays open.

### Exposure read-back

Plan Task 2 (commits `d6108dc` and the one this text came with; the review fixes of Task 1 are
`3f1b57b`). The switch **`--fable2_exposure_readback`** (on, true, 1 / off, false, 0; **default off until Task 7's valid runs**, see "Cost") adds the game's two luminance buffers to the SDK's forced read-back list, so
that the game measures its own picture and its exposure adapts in a normal run (no
`--readback_resolve`).

**How it works.** `src/core/readback_force_list.h` (pure; `tests/native/
test_readback_force_list.cpp`): `ForceReadbackList(hero_dog, exposure)` gives `""`,
`"0x12704000"`, `"0x1A385000,0x1A34F000"` or `"0x12704000,0x1A385000,0x1A34F000"`: both
luminance addresses of question 1, since they lie farther apart than one window; the hero and
dog texture's entry is the same text whatever the switch says. `Fable2App::OnPostSetup` writes
the list into the SDK's `readback_resolve_force_addresses` once, only while that switch is at
its default source (a list given by hand wins), and logs `[fable2-config] seeded
readback_resolve_force_addresses '<list>' (... hero_dog_texture_readback=B,
fable2_exposure_readback=B)`. The switch is read with the native renderer on or off.

The SDK's side, unchanged (`thirdparty/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/command_processor.cpp`,
`ShouldForceReadbackResolve`, lines 203 to 274; `d3d12/command_processor.cpp`, `IssueCopy`,
lines 3056 to 3293): the list is read and parsed at every resolve (a hot-reload switch, no
cached parse), only while `readback_resolve` is `none`; an entry matches a resolve issued as
`PM4_DRAW_INDX_2`, a rectangle list of 3 indices, with its base in [entry, entry + 64 KiB) (the
switch's help text says 1 MiB; the code says 64 KiB). A forced resolve is read back at once:
the command processor ends its submission, **waits for the GPU to finish everything queued**
(`AwaitAllQueueOperationsCompletion`), and copies the bytes (here 207,360 to 221,184) into
guest memory. The first 24 forced resolves of a process are logged (`Forced readback-resolve
for RB_COPY_DEST_BASE=... (matched force address ...)`), never more.

binary of 21:21:47; other programs used 0 to 1% of the graphics card by the controller's word;
evidence `out/native-evidence/post/t2_*`; no `--readback_resolve` in any):

| D, on, renderer off | 444 | `-Total 70 -Shots "36,66" -GameArgs --fable2_native_render=false,--fable2_exposure_readback=on` | none possible |

### Post block

Plan Task 4 (commit `f24588b` and the one this text came with). Capture only: nothing is drawn
with the block yet, and no shader, binding or target changed. The switch
**`--fable2_native_post`** (on, true, 1 / off, false, 0; **default off**) makes the capture read
the frame's post block; it is read only in a frame with records, with the light and the textures
on (`PostRecordsWanted`), latched at the frame's boundary with the records' word.

**The block** (`src/native/capture/post_block.h`, pure; `capture::PostBlock`, 2,168 bytes, in
`FrameScene::post`):

| Field | From | |
|---|---|---|
| `composite[6]` | `37B186F4BD3288F7` | `c31.x` (bloom scale), `c46.x` (table scale), `c47.x` (grey fade), `c77.x` (saturation), `c77.y` (gain), `c78.x` (exponent) |
| `bright[5]` | `EE922CFB4426EA83` | `c31.x`, `c46.x`, `c47.x` (a divisor), `c77.x`, `c77.y` (= 1 / `c20.w`) |
| `blur[2][7]` | `EA83C7E7E24EC4C8`, `28DBE18F313350BF` | the centre tap's weight and those of the taps 1 to 6 texels away: `c46.xyzw`, `c47.xyz` |
| `radial[4]` | `4BE4344C27016E04` | zero until plan Task 12 |
| `table[512]` | fetch slot 1 of the composite | the 2,048 bytes at the constant's base, one float a texel, high byte first |
| `parts`, `valid` | | `kPostPartBlur` when the fourteen weights are there |

**Where it is read** (`capture.cpp`, `ObservePostDraw`, beside `ObserveShadowDraw` in
`OnXdkReturn`): at the return of an outermost `D3DDevice_BeginVertices` hook outside the main
scene, on the guest's drawing thread. Which step a rectangle is, is told by the pixel shader's
microcode hash (`ChoosePs`, `LookupPs`, as the sky draw is told). The bright pass's and the
blurs' registers wait in a thread-local of the frame; at the composite its registers and the
fetch constant are read and judged first (`MakePostBlock` without bytes), the address is
followed only for a constant that is the pin, the 2,048 bytes are read whole or not at all,
copied, and the copy is hashed (`PostSource`: the content a capture's `"tfc"` names the table by)
and decoded. The block goes to the builder under the scene's mutex after the frame's recheck. At
most 8 reads a frame at a composite that give none (and 8 counts more for rectangles whose
shader could not be told); after the frame's block nothing more is looked at that frame.

**`MakePostBlock`'s rules, in order** (the first that fails is the reason; an invalid block is
all zero): `unread` (the composite's or the bright pass's registers, or the fetch constant);
`register` (one of the eleven components is not finite); `range` (composite `c31.x` in [0, 64],
`c46.x` in (0, 64], `c47.x` in [0, 1e6], `|c77.x|` <= 4, `c77.y` in (0, 64], `c78.x` in (0, 1];
bright `c31.x` in [0, 64], `c46.x` in [0, 64], `c47.x` in [1e-3, 64], `|c77.x|` <= 4, `c77.y` in
(0, 64]); `table-dimension`, `-base`, `-width`, `-format`, `-endian`, `-swizzle`, `-sign`,
`-exp-adjust`, `-clamp`, `-filter`, `-mip` (the pin: 1D, an address, 512 texels, format 36 with
number format bit 1, endian 2, swizzle `0xB68`, sign fields `0x55`, exponent adjust 0, clamp to
edge, point filter, one level; the captured constant is `04000956 1FAA00A4 000001FF 010016D1
00000000 00000018`); `table-bytes`; `table-texel` (every texel finite and in [0, 4)). The blur
part needs both blurs read, every weight in [0, 1] and each set's `w0 + 2 (w1 + .. + w6)` within
1e-3 of 1; a block without it is valid. The table is carried as stored; which texel a luminance
reads is the reader's rule, the nearest, `floor(u * 512 + 0.5)` (controller ruling 19).

**The frame's decision** (`ChoosePostBlock`, called by `FrameBuilder::Finish`): the frame's own
block if it pairs with the frame's light block (`PostBlockPairs`: bright `c77.y` times
`out_scale` is 1 within 1e-3); else the last valid block of an earlier frame if it is at most
`kPostBlockMaxAge` = 4 frames old and pairs (`post_age` 1 to 4); else none, with `pairing` (a
block was at hand and none paired; also every frame without a valid light block that had a
block at hand), the frame's last failed read's reason, `stale` (said once, for the frame that
finds the kept block too old; the block is dropped then) or `no-draw`. The builder keeps the
last block that passed `MakePostBlock`, whether or not it paired in its own frame, and drops it
when the switch is off at a frame's end. **The kept block serves almost only a still or blind
exposure** (review of Task 4, Minor 3): with the pairing at 1e-3 and `c20.w` falling by 6.4e-4 a
frame (T4-1: 8.58923, 8.58371, ...) a kept block pairs at age 1 only, and at the 2.9e-3 a frame
of Task 1's turn towards the sun at no age. The bound of 4 frames is then in effect 1 or 0: a
frame whose own read fails while the exposure moves has no block (`pairing`) and is drawn with
the fixed mapping. That is ruling 11 as written; the rule is not loosened.

**Limits.** (1) One place, a standing camera, daylight: no frame without a block, no kept
block, no failed read has occurred in a game; those paths are held by tests only. In a frame
without a composite (a menu, a loading screen) every `BeginVertices` call outside the scene pays
the device snapshot and the shader lookup for the whole frame (the tries bound only the reads at
a composite); with 12 such calls a frame at the bridge that was at most 0.25 ms of the work
median here, and a menu or a cutscene with many quads has not been run (review, Minor 7). (2) The 240 or
so frames after the last periodic line of a native stretch are not counted in any line. (3) The
block is read at the composite's call, before the frame's swap, in 12 of 12 captured frames;
a read that came after its frame's end would be dropped and counted (`dropped at a frame's end`:

one: nothing in the block says whether the game measures its picture; the log line's `c20.w`

when it is read** (review, Minor 2). It lies at one address, `0x1FAA0000`, in every frame and the
CPU rewrites it every frame; which guest thread writes it, and when, is not known. The block's
equality with the capture's dump does not show it (the dump is read in the same hook's return),
and the rules cannot see a table written half by one frame and half by the next: both halves
pass [0, 4). What a tear would cost is bounded by the data: the largest change of a texel between
consecutive frames is 2.4e-4 to 9.6e-4 (`t4_table_222843.txt`), so a torn table is off by under
1e-3, of a gain of about 0.3, for one frame. (7) Spec Design 4 says a block without the blurs'
weights is counted; the periodic line prints `parts P` of the one frame it names and has no count
over its window. The count is left to the bloom's task (plan Task 8), which is the first to draw
with the weights (review, Minor 8).

### Native composite

Plan Task 5 (commits `f8ec8f7` and the one this text came with). With **`--fable2_native_post=on`**
(still **default off**) the native picture of a frame that has a post block goes through the
game's own composite and the scan-out ramp; every other frame is drawn as before.

**A frame is a post frame or today's frame** (`DecideClayPost`, `clay_logic.h`, "Native post";
one chain, the first thing missing decides; decided in `ClayPass::Render` before the frame's two
words are written and once more when the frame's constant buffer is known):

| Verdict | When | Counted as |
|---|---|---|
| `kOff` | the switch is off | not counted |
| `kNoLight` | the light's switch or the textures off, no usable light block, or the constant buffer could not be made | `no-light` |
| `kBlock` | no post block in the scene; one older than 4 frames; one that does not pair with the frame's `c20.w`; one whose registers or texels the pass refuses (`MakeClayPostConstants`: the block's own bounds, judged again) | `post-block` |
| `kRamp` | no scan-out ramp, or one with an entry outside [0, 1] or a channel that decreases | `post-ramp` |
| `kObjects` | the post steps' GPU objects could not be made (off until the pass is rebuilt; the renderer goes on) | `post-objects` |
| `kBuffer` | the frame has no constant buffer because nothing of it is drawn | `no-buffer` |
| `kDrawn` | none of the above | `drawn` |

**A post frame.** (1) The frame's exposure word (`f_exposure`) is the light block's `c20.w`, the
game's own output scale, in place of the fixed 2.22: lit draws, the sky and the unlit fog's
in-scatter write the game's scene values. (2) The word at byte 60 of cbuffer Frame, a padding word
until now, is `f_post`, which every unlit colour is multiplied by before its fog: in a post frame
the **unlit scale** `U = 1 / (c77.y * T[128])`, at most 64 (spec ruling 9: the reciprocal of the
composite's gain at scene luminance 1), in every other frame 1. (3) Two full-screen steps with a
layout of their own replace the output mapping:

- **composite** (`kClayPostCompositePs`): the arithmetic of the game's `37B186F4BD3288F7`
  (`light_formulas.post_composite`) with the frame's registers and table, from the linear target,
  texel for texel, into the **front target** (1120 x 720 `R8G8B8A8_UNORM`, 3.1 MB: the game's
  front buffer before the ramp). The table is read at the **nearest texel**,
  `min(511, uint(512 * saturate(c46.x * L) + 0.5))` (controller ruling 19), not at the floor. The
  bloom is (0, 0, 0) until plan Task 8.
- **ramp** (`kClayPostRampPs`): each channel of the front target through the guest's 256-entry
  gamma ramp into the mapped target the views sample. The application reads the SDK's table at
  every composite frame, now before the clay pass renders, so it is the table the emulated picture
  of that frame went through.

The post layout (3 parameters, pixel stage): b0 the steps' constants (`ClayPostConstants`, 6,288
bytes: the composite's six registers, the scene's clamp 31.875, the bright pass's registers, the
blurs' weights and the radial blur's registers for later tasks, the table as `float4[128]`, the
ramp as `float4[256]`), which lie in 25 small slots of the frame's constant buffer
(`PlanClayFrameSlots`' `post`, between the sky's slot and the objects'); b1 8 words of a step's
own (read by no shader yet); t0 a table of 4 textures (entry 0 the step's source); static samplers
s0 point clamp and s1 linear clamp (not used yet). The table and the ramp are read by index: no
texture, no upload, the game's point fetch exactly (spec ruling 12).

**Values that are no numbers.** Every reader of the linear target takes a channel that is not
above 0 as 0 (a NaN, a negative value) and one above 31.875 as 31.875 (an infinity). With the
block's registers and texels inside their bounds every later term is a number, the table's index
is bounded at 511 after a saturate and the ramp's at 255 by one; the front target is 8-bit. Held
by the mirror on 43,008 combinations of such inputs (test case 607) and in the compiled programs
(shader test cases 234 to 236).

**Today's frame is today's picture.** With the switch off: the verdict is `kOff` for all 64
combinations of the other inputs (test case 600); the exposure is 2.22 and the mapping is
`kOutputMapPs`, text and program unchanged. What differs from the build before: each unlit colour
is multiplied by a word that is 1. With the word the literal 1 every compiled program of the four
scene pixel shaders is the program before, instruction for instruction; the vertex shader, the
sky's shader and the terrain shaders' lit programs are the programs before as they stand, the
textured shader's lit programs once `textured` is fixed too (its branch of a draw without an
albedo, which no lit draw takes, reads the word); an unlit program gained one `mul` by
`cb2[3].w` for each colour it can return (shader test cases 230, 231: 111 lit programs equal, 101
unlit programs with the multiply alone).

**Tests before any run**: the mirrors (`PostTableTexel`, `PostUnlitScale`, `PostCompositeMirror`,
`PostRampIndex`) against the reference's generated numbers (`post_pins.py`; 41 texel pins, among
them `(k + 0.5) / 512 -+ 1e-6` and `k / 512`; 24 composite points, worst difference 0); a
mutation check, 15 of 15 wrong headers caught (`out/native-evidence/post/t5_mutations.txt`);
`tests/test_post_literals.py`.

**Limits.** (1) The clear colour of a post frame is not black as spec Design 6 first said: its

against the game's own front buffer, pixel for pixel, is plan Task 6 (the oracle feed). (7) One
place, daylight, a standing camera; night, towns, interiors, menus and cutscenes have not run.

step in the darks was seen, none was looked for beyond the shots.

### Oracle feed

Plan Task 6 of the post sub-project (spec ruling 17, Design 17, criterion 6): a diagnostic that
runs the pass's post steps, on the GPU, on a scene whose right answer is known. No test executes
the HLSL ("Native composite", limit 6); the mirrors of `clay_logic.h` are a second writing of
the same sentences. The post steps are full-screen steps over one input, so with the game's own
scene colour as that input their result can be held against the reference's picture and against
the game's front buffer pixel for pixel, apart from every error of the native scene. For
"Native composite"'s one-sided offset (the far and sunlit regions 0.02 to 0.05 above the
prediction) it can exclude one cause and no more: fed the game's scene, the composite's and the
ramp's compiled shaders either reproduce the reference (then the offset is not theirs) or they
do not (then it is). The feed does not run, and so cannot clear, the scene-side words of a post
frame (the exposure `c20.w` in the lit draws, the unlit scale), the live block's path from the
capture, the prediction's own model of today's mapping, or the measuring of regions in window
shots. (Review of plan Task 6, Important 1: the first writing said "then the offset is the
native scene's".)

**The switch**: `--fable2_native_post_oracle=<prefix>` (empty by default), with
`--fable2_native_post=on`. Read once at startup (`fable2_native_render.cpp`, `LoadOracle`, before
the callbacks are registered): `<prefix>.scene` and `<prefix>.block`, parsed by
`src/native/render/post_oracle.h` (pure; `tests/native/test_post_oracle.cpp`). A file that is
missing or refused gives one log line with the fault's word and nothing else changes. Without
the switch nothing of the feed is reached: the pass's pointer to it stays null.

**The files**, little-endian, written by `tools/xdk_sigmatch/post_replay.py export <capture>
<frame> <prefix>` from a capture made under `--readback_resolve=full`:

| File | Content | Refused when (`OracleFault`) |
|---|---|---|
| `<prefix>.scene` | `"F2OS"`, u32 width, u32 height, width x height x 3 float32: the scene colour the game's composite read (`0x199E0000`, by content), in the game's scale | `short`; `magic`; `size` (not 1120 x 720, the pass's logical size, or a length that is not the header's); `value` (a NaN or an infinity anywhere) |
| `<prefix>.block` | `"F2OB"`, u32 1, float32 `c20.w`, `PostBlock`'s 541 floats in the struct's order, u32 parts | `short`; `magic`; `version`; `size` (not 2,180 bytes); `scale` (`c20.w` no number or not above 0); `parts` (an unknown bit, or the blur's bit with weights that fail their rule); `value` (a radial float that is no number); `block` (a rule of `MakePostBlock`, named: `register`, `range`, `table-texel`); `pairing` (`c77.y` of the bright pass times `c20.w` not 1 within 1e-3) |
| `logs/native_post_dump_<stamp>.rgba` | `"F2OD"`, u32 width, u32 height, width x height x 4 bytes: the mapped target | (written by the pass) |

The block is made through the capture's own `MakePostBlock` (with the table's fetch constant as
every capture holds it, and the table as the bytes the guest holds), so a file can hand the
pass nothing a guest frame could not; it is then the file's floats bit for bit. The radial part
(plan Task 12) is accepted and not carried. A scene value that is no number refuses the file:
the steps would read it as 0 or as the clamp, but the exporter writes none (0 in each of the
four exports below), so one is a damaged file.

**In the pass** (`clay_pass.cpp`; `ClayPass::SetPostOracle`, `TakePostOracleDump`). The feed
acts only in a frame that is a post frame by its own verdict (`DecideClayPost`: nothing of
"a frame without post" changes, and a menu or a frame without a block is today's with the feed
set as without). In such a frame: the steps' constants are made of the file's block and the
frame's own ramp by the frame's own rule (`MakeClayPostConstants`); on the first such frame the
scene is uploaded once as a 1120 x 720 `R16G16B16A16_FLOAT` texture (alpha 1; each value
bounded to the largest half, 65504, so that no infinity is uploaded; `HalfFromFloat`, the
nearest half, a tie to the even one, tested against `HalfToFloat` on every half and every tie);
the composite reads that texture by `Load` in place of the linear target, and the ramp step
follows as always. The scene's own draws are drawn as in any post frame and nothing reads
them; the frame's exposure and unlit words stay the live block's. The native view therefore
shows one still picture, the game's scene through the native steps, while the feed is on. In
the frame 30 fed frames after the upload's the mapped target, resting in
`kPixelShaderResource`, is taken to `kCopySource`, copied to a read-back buffer (rows of 4,608
bytes, the RHI's row pitch above 4,480) and returned to its resting state; when that
submission has completed the buffer is read once and the file written, once in a run. The
mapped target has `kTextureUsageCopySource` for this (no effect on Direct3D 12, where the
SDK's texture creation does not read the flag). A failure of the texture, the staging buffer
or the read-back buffer turns the feed off until the pass is rebuilt, with one log line, and
the steps read the pass's own scene again. The texture and a pending buffer are destroyed with
the pass's other objects; a rebuilt pass uploads again and makes the copy again if none was
taken.

Log lines: `[native] post oracle: <prefix>: scene W x H (N values a half-float texture changes),
block c20.w S, parts P; ...` at startup; `[native] clay: post oracle: scene uploaded ...` with
the block's registers at the first fed frame; `... the mapped target copied for the dump at fed
frame 31 (submission N)`; `[native] post oracle: wrote <path> (3225612 bytes ...) at clay frame
N`.

**The exports** (`out/native-evidence/post/oracle/<stamp>_f1.scene` / `.block`; frame 1 of the
three bridge oracle captures of section 16 and of the trees capture `134312`; each parsed by the
C++ parser through `out/tests/runtime-unit-tests/post_oracle.exe <prefix>`, output in
`out/native-evidence/post/t6_oracle_files.txt`):

| Capture | `c20.w` | Largest scene value | Values no number | Values a half changes | Parsed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `092959` | 8.44137 | 4.359375 | 0 | 0 | scene valid, block valid, parts 1 |
| `121331` | 8.42832 | 4.359375 | 0 | 0 | scene valid, block valid, parts 1 |
| `132250` | 8.45966 | 3.9375 | 0 | 0 | scene valid, block valid, parts 1 |
| `134312` | 7.40595 | 4.5625 | 0 | 0 | scene valid, block valid, parts 1 |

No value is changed by the half-float texture (the game's scene target has 7 bits of mantissa
and at most 31.875), so the GPU reads exactly the numbers the reference computes from. The
exporter writes parts 3 for these frames (they have a radial row); the parser takes the blur's
part alone.

**The comparison** (`post_replay.py`, for a capture `<c>` and the log of the run that made the
dump): `replay <c> 1 --variant A --ramp <log> --write <ref>` writes the reference's variant A
picture and the game's front buffer, both through that run's own ramp, as `<ref>_A.rgba` and
`<ref>_final.rgba`; `compare <dump> <ref>_A.rgba` is spec criterion 6 (the command prints the
whole picture's largest difference, the mean signed difference by channel and whether the
criterion's bounds hold: at least 99.9% of the pixels within 1 level, all within 2);
`compare <dump> <ref>_final.rgba` is criterion 5's figures from the GPU (the front buffer holds
the HUD and the bloom: the line "outside the HUD" and the regions are the ones to read).

**Runs** (the controller's, `-UserPresent`, `RUN UNCHECKED`; all exit 0; the window on the
100%-scaled monitor, shot width 1296: no timing is taken from them; evidence
`out/native-evidence/post/t6_*`, each run's dump copied there as `<name>_dump.rgba`):

*The feed ran as written* in all five: the startup line (scene 1120 x 720, 0 values a
half-float texture changes), `scene uploaded` with the file's registers, `the mapped target

live frames were post frames throughout (`drawn 600` of 600 in each real-GPU run, blind:
`c20.w 16.0000`). The ramp line of all five logs is the table of log 455 (the same text;
`changes 0`), so the references are those written through log 455's ramp
(`oracle/ref455_<stamp>_f1_A.rgba`, `_final.rgba`).

*Software adapter, debug layer* (log 457; spec criterion 10 for this build): no `d3d ERROR`
line; warning id 1328 only, as in log 450. The half-float texture, the copy-source state and
the read-back buffer raised nothing.

*Spec criterion 6, the shaders against the reference's variant A after the ramp*
(`t6_compare_reference.txt`; `post_replay.py compare`, 806,400 pixels):

| Dump | Within 1 level | Within 2 | Largest | Mean signed (dump less reference), r g b | The criterion's bounds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| software adapter, `092959` | 100.000% | 100% | 2 | -0.000, +0.000, +0.000 | **held** |
| real GPU, `092959` | 99.333% | 100% | 2 | -0.060, -0.060, -0.041 | not held (99.9% within 1) |
| real GPU, `121331` | 99.495% | 100% | 2 | -0.055, -0.066, -0.042 | not held |
| real GPU, `132250` | 99.354% | 100% | 2 | -0.053, -0.059, -0.040 | not held |
| real GPU, `134312` | 99.476% | 100% | 2 | -0.048, -0.055, -0.036 | not held |

**Criterion 6 is met on the software adapter and not met as written on the real GPU**: every
pixel is within 2 levels there, but 0.5 to 0.7% of the pixels are 2 levels off where the
criterion allows 0.1%. The plan asks which is at fault, the shader or the reference's
addressing. Neither: it is how this graphics card stores a float in an 8-bit target.

- *On the software adapter the steps are the reference* (`t6_analyse_092959.txt`): taken back
  through the ramp, 2,419,192 of 2,419,200 channels hold the reference's front level; the 8
  others (5 one level down, 3 up) are pixels whose unrounded reference value lies within
  0.00001 of a level of a rounding boundary. So the table's nearest-texel addressing (ruling
  19), the fade, the power and the ramp's index are, as compiled HLSL, what
  `light_formulas.post_composite` and `post_ramp` say, on the game's own scene and block.
- *The real GPU differs only downward, and only at rounding boundaries*
  (`t6_ramp_levels_092959.txt`, `t6_boundary_<stamp>.txt`; scripts beside them). Two writes
  into 8-bit targets are involved. (1) The ramp step's: a ramp entry whose value times 255 has
  a fraction of 0.5015 to 0.5337 is stored one level low at every pixel of its front level (25
  channel-levels of capture `092959`, for example front level 96: entry 81.51, reference 82,
  dump 81; 0.86% of the channels); entries with a fraction of 0.5513 and above are stored as
  the reference rounds them (146 of them between 0.55 and 0.75). (2) The composite's: with the
  ramp step's results taken as this card's, the dump holds the entry of the front level below
  the reference's in 2.66 to 3.10% of the channels, and in every one of them the reference's
  unrounded level lies 0 to 0.062 of a level above the boundary (median 0.015 to 0.020, 99%
  0.053 to 0.057); **no other difference remains, in any of the four captures (0 channels)**.
  The rule that fits is the reviewer's (review of plan Task 6, question 4 and Minor 1; found
  with the reviewer's own scripts, which are not in the repository, on three of the four
  captures, and not rerun here): **the card (an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080, log 458 line 11)
  truncates the float to 12 fractional bits and then takes the nearest level**,
  `floor(floor(v * 4096) / 4096 * 255 + 0.5)`, at both writes, where the reference and the
  software adapter take the nearest level of the float itself. Applied to the reference's float
  at the composite's write and to the ramp's entry at the ramp's write, it gives the real GPU's
  dump in 2,418,698 of 2,419,200 channels of `092959` (99.9792%), in 99.9780% of `121331` and
  99.9915% of `134312`; the nearest level alone gives 94.843% of `092959`, truncation to 11
  bits 94.243%, to 13 bits 98.279%, rounding to 12 bits 96.051%. Of the 502, 533 and 205
  channels the rule misses, 493, 526 and 199 are one case: front level 128, where the truncated
  value is exactly 0.5 and 0.5 x 255 is the tie 127.5, which the card takes down (dump 114
  where the ramp's entry of level 128 gives 115); the other 6 to 9 channels of 2.4 million are
  the single-against-double noise the software adapter also shows (its 8). The rule's largest
  shortfall is 255 / 4096 = 0.0623 of a level: the 0 to 0.062 above. So the dump is one
  function of the reference's own output value, the same at both writes, one of them a write
  with no arithmetic before it (the ramp step stores a constant): a wrong table texel or a
  different power cannot be that function, and no shader difference hides in the pattern.
  Direct3D allows a float-to-UNORM conversion a tolerance of 0.6 of a level, so this is a
  conforming conversion, not an error of the card or the pass. (The first writing said "this
  card stores `floor(v * 255 + 0.5 - d)` with d near 0.04 to 0.06 ... the conversion's
  threshold is not one number": an inference from `t6_rounding_model_092959.txt`, in which a
  single offset d for both writes fits 98.5% of the channels at best, d = 0.035, against 94.8%
  for d = 0. The truncation is why no offset fits.) The two effects can meet in one pixel, and
  the ramp has 18 steps of 2 levels a channel, hence the pixels 2 levels off.
- *The two implementations against each other* (the software adapter's dump against the real
  GPU's, the same file): 99.333% of the pixels within 1 level, all within 2, the real GPU lower
  by 0.060, 0.060, 0.041 on average: the same figures as the real GPU against the reference,
  as they must be when the software adapter equals the reference.
- *What would make the real GPU exact*: writing the level itself, `floor(v * 255 + 0.5) / 255`,
  as the last statement of both pixel shaders, so that the stored value has no fraction for the
  conversion to round. Not done here: it changes shader text (the shader test's cases 232 to
  236 and a software-adapter run with it), and whether the criterion is to be met that way or
  restated is the controller's ruling. (Since ruled, controller ruling 25 in the ledger: both
  writes write the rounded level themselves, in plan Task 8, whose shader-text change needs the
  software-adapter run anyway; criterion 6's real-GPU half is measured again there with one
  feed run. A stored `m / 255` loses less than 0.0623 of a level under this card's rule and
  returns to m; the tie cannot occur, since 128 / 255 is not 0.5. The expectation for that run
  is sharp: the real GPU's dump equal to the software adapter's but for a handful of channels.
  The ruling covers these two writes only: the same rule will show at every later UNORM write
  that cannot be rounded in the shader, such as a blended write, or that is not 8 bits, such as
  the sun layer's `R10G10B10A2`. Review of plan Task 6, Minor 2.) For the picture it is at most
  one level of the front target and one of the mapped target, always down. (That the emulated
  picture of the same machine goes through the same conversion at its own writes is an
  expectation, not a measurement: the SDK's writes and their formats were not looked at. Review
  of plan Task 6, Minor 3.)

*Against the game's front buffer through the ramp* (spec criterion 5's figures, from the GPU;
`t6_compare_front.txt`; the reference `_final.rgba` is the capture's front buffer with HUD and
bloom, the dump has neither, so "outside the HUD" is the line to read): median 3 levels (whole
levels here; the float replay gave 3.14, 3.05, 3.13) and **56.06, 56.19, 56.08% of the pixels
within 8 levels** for `092959`, `121331`, `132250` on the real GPU (56.12% for the software
adapter's dump of `092959`), against the float replay's 56.0, 56.2, 56.0%
(`t6_reference_ramp455.txt`) and the criterion's 55.9, 56.0, 55.9 within 0.5 points. By region
the picture is the research's: planks, trunk and the plank shadows within a few levels (median
0 to 1), the far ground, the sky and the lake 5 to 22 levels under the game's, which is the
bloom's veil that variant A does not have. The trees' capture: median 5, 48.9% within 8 (more
of it under the bloom).

*What this settles for "Native composite"*: its far and sunlit regions lay 0.02 to 0.05 above
the prediction, all on one side, and the text left open whether the native scene or the
shaders differed. Fed the game's own scene, the steps return the reference to the level (the
software adapter exactly, the real GPU within its conversion, and that goes down, not up). **The
offset is not the composite's or the ramp's shader.** That is all the feed excludes. The cause
is in what the two shaders are fed in a live frame (the native scene, and with it the frame's
exposure and unlit words: post-chain code of plan Task 5 that only the scene's draws read, and
nothing reads those draws under the feed; were it off, it would give exactly a one-sided offset
in lit regions), in the live block's path from the capture, or on the prediction's side (its
model of today's mapping, the measuring of regions in window shots), and is not separated
further here. (Review of plan Task 6, Important 1: the first writing concluded "the offset is
the native scene's" by elimination from two alternatives where there are more.)

*Shots viewed*: T6-2 at 40 s and the software adapter's at 225 s show the bridge of capture
`092959` as the game drew it (the game's own water, clouds, far trees and leaf shadows, which
the native scene does not have), still, without HUD and without the bloom's veil; the two look
the same to the eye. T6-5 at 40 s shows the trees' capture from under the bridge with a pink
sky through the leaves. In all three the picture fills the native view; nothing of the pass's
own scene shows.

*Limits*: one dump a run, one frame of each capture; daylight scenes whose largest scene value
is 4.6 (the clamp at 31.875 and the table's last texels are not reached by these scenes: the
mirrors' tests hold those); bloom off (criterion 12 is plan Task 9's); one real graphics card.
The criterion's real-GPU half stands as not met as written until plan Task 8's feed run under
ruling 25.

### Native bloom

Plan Task 8 of the post sub-project (phase 10b; spec Design 10, rulings 6, 14, 15, 16; controller
ruling 25; ruling 27 for the bloom's sample place), 2026-10-10. The code and what was found
offline come first, as written before any run; the fifteen runs are under "Runs" at the end of
this subsection. The criteria's verdicts are in "Validation (10b)".

**The switch**: `--fable2_native_bloom=on|off` (default off; the light switch's parser). It acts
only in a post frame. Nothing of the capture depends on it: the blurs' weights are part of the
post block, read with `--fable2_native_post=on` since plan Task 4.

**The steps** (`clay_pass.cpp`, `Render`; `clay_logic.h`, "Native bloom";
`fable2_native_shaders.h`), between the scene's last draw and the composite, each a full-screen
triangle through the post layout:

| Step | Game shader | Reads | Writes | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| downsample | `87E85199E1E9B260` | the scene (linear target; the oracle scene when fed), four linear samples | `bloom_d_`, 280 x 180 `R11G11B10_FLOAT` | `0.25 * (t(P + (2.5, 2.5)) + t(P + (2.5, 0.5)) + t(P + (0.5, 0.5)) + t(P + (0.5, 2.5)))`, `P = 4 * (pixel + bias)`, each sample 0 unless above 0 and at most 31.875 |
| bright pass | `EE922CFB4426EA83` | `bloom_d_` by `Load` (the sun's two layers at t1, t2 only behind the sun's flag, 0 until plan Task 14; the white texture is bound there) | `bloom_p_`, 280 x 180 `R10G10B10A2_UNORM` | `L = lum(d)`; `d * sat(L * c77.y - c77.x) / L * c31.x / c47.x`, 0 for `L = 0` |
| blur along x | `EA83C7E7E24EC4C8` | `bloom_p_`, 13 `Load`s at -6..+6 texels, clamped | `bloom_q_`, the same format | the frame's seven weights of that blur |
| blur along y | `28DBE18F313350BF` | `bloom_q_`, 13 `Load`s | `bloom_p_` | the frame's seven weights of that blur; one program for both, the direction in the step's words |
| composite | `37B186F4BD3288F7` | the scene by `Load`, `bloom_p_` by one linear sample | the front target | `b = sat(bloom * c31.x)`, `s = c + b * (1 - c)`, then as before |

The targets are `ClayPass::kWidth / 4` x `kHeight / 4` with a static assert that the division is
exact (ledger ruling 6: a quarter of the LOGICAL size, whatever the scene target's size or sample
count becomes; the blurs' weights are the game's, in texels of these). Each rests in
`kPixelShaderResource` and is a target for its own step alone; no step reads what it writes; none
is read in a frame that did not write it. They are made on the first frame that could be a post
frame with the switch on (`EnsureBloomObjects`), destroyed and forgotten with the pass's other
objects. If they cannot be made, every frame with the bloom's switch on is today's
(`post-objects`, one log line) and with the switch off the post goes on without them. Spec ruling
14's fallback format is not built (one constant, `kBloomFormat`, if the software adapter refuses
`R10G10B10A2_UNORM` as a target).

**The step's words** (cbuffer `Step`, b1 of the post layout, 8 words; `ClayPostStepConstants`,
`MakeClayPostStep`): the reciprocal of the source's width and height, the level count of the
target's format, the step's offset (the downsample's pixel position; the composite's bloom fetch
in pixels), a blur's direction, the source's last texel. No shader holds a size (the test looks
for 1120, 720, 280, 180 in every step's text).

**The verdict** (`ClayBloom`, `DecideClayBloom`): `on` in a post frame with the switch on whose
steps' constants carry the blurs' weights; `no-weights` in a post frame with the switch on whose
block has no blur part (drawn without bloom, counted); `off` otherwise. The Post line: `Post: on,
block valid, age A, drawn, bloom on | c20.w S, unlit scale U | frames since start N: drawn D
(bloom B, no-weights W), post-block ...`, and one `post changed` line when the bloom's verdict
changes. Two more words on that line come from the review of plan Task 5: behind `post-block` of
a valid block the pass's own rule that refused it (`age`, `pairing`, `values`, `words`: Minor 11),
and `(c46.x X: the gain at scene luminance L, not 1)` after the unlit scale when the composite's
`c46.x` is not the 0.25 that makes table texel 128 scene luminance 1 (Minor 8).

**Bloom off is plan Task 5's picture** (spec criterion 15, shown as criterion 8's first half
was). The composite reads the bloom only inside a test of the block's flag. Shader test case 237:
with the flag the literal 0 the composite reads no second texture, no sampler and of the step's
words the level count alone; with the write's rounding (below) taken out as well it is,
instruction for instruction, the program of plan Task 5's committed text, which the test holds as
a string; the ramp likewise. What the two programs do more than Task 5's is the rounding: 3
instructions each. With the switch off no bloom object is made and no bloom step is drawn.

**The write's own rounding (controller ruling 25).** On the real card 0.5 to 0.7% of the pixels
of an oracle dump were one level under the reference ("Oracle feed"): the card cuts a float to 12
fractional bits before it takes the nearest 8-bit level. Every step into a UNORM target now ends
in `floor(v * levels + 0.5) / levels` of a value already in [0, 1] (`post_level`; `PostLevel` is
its mirror), `levels` in the step's words from the target's format (`UnormLevels` in
`clay_pass.cpp`: 255 for `R8G8B8A8_UNORM`, 1023 for `R10G10B10A2_UNORM`; review of plan Task 6,
Minor 2). A value that is a level already loses less than a level under that card's rule and
comes back as itself (test case 610, every level of both counts). **The 10-bit writes are rounded
the same way**, decided by what the game's targets and the reference do: the game's bright and
blur targets hold only 10-bit levels, and the reference rounds each stage to the nearest of 1,023
(`post_replay.q10`). What this card does at a 10-bit write was not measured; with the rounding in
the shader it does not matter within Direct3D's tolerance. Expected of the feed run after this
change: the real GPU's dump equal to the software adapter's but for a handful of channels;
anything else is a new finding.

**Two conventions, decided offline against the game's front buffer** (four read-back captures,
frame 1; `out/native-evidence/post/t8_downsample_forms.txt`, `t8_bloom_fetch.txt`; scripts in
`out/tests/post-task8/`). Median absolute difference in 8-bit levels of the replay's variant B
against the front buffer, whole picture outside the HUD (`092959`, `121331`, `132250`; `134312`,
towards the sun, where the sun layer is missing):

| Downsample | Bloom sampled | Bridge captures | `134312` | Within 1 level (bridge) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| four texels, bias 0 | composite's fetch, `x / 4 + 0.5` | **0.578, 0.565, 0.573** | 1.129 | 52.4, 53.2, 52.8% |
| box of sixteen | composite's fetch | 0.620, 0.608, 0.617 | 1.422 | 50.3, 51.0, 50.6% |
| four texels, bias 0.5 | composite's fetch | 0.761, 0.753, 0.765 | 1.713 | 44.4, 44.6, 44.2% |
| four texels, bias 0 | centres aligned, `(x + 0.5) / 4` | 0.732, 0.716, 0.727 | 1.521 | 45.7, 46.3, 45.9% |
| four texels, bias 0.5 | centres aligned | 0.639, 0.629, 0.640 | 1.351 | 49.4, 49.9, 49.4% |
| box of sixteen | centres aligned | 0.693, 0.678, 0.689 | 1.511 | 47.2, 47.8, 47.4% |

1. *Where the composite samples the bloom* (`kPostBloomFetch`). The game's composite fetches the
   bloom at the scene's interpolated coordinate with `OffsetX = OffsetY = 0.5` (`37B1`
   instruction 6, as instruction 3 fetches the scene). The two fetches share the coordinate and
   the half-texel offset, each in its own texels: the scene is read at `s + 0.5` scene texels,
   which is `(s + 0.5) / 4` bloom texels, and the bloom at `s / 4 + 0.5`: 0.375 of a bloom texel
   (1.5 pixels) further on, whatever `s` is at a pixel. So the place needs no reading of the
   interpolator (review of plan Task 8, Minor 4; the first writing argued from it); what stays
   inference is that the emulator's fetch offsets are the console's. With the interpolator
   `x / width` at pixel `x`, which is what makes the scene's fetch a texel centre, the bloom's
   coordinate is `x / 4 + 0.5`: pixel 0 reads bloom texel 0 itself. The research's replay, the spec
   and the plan had "texel centres aligned" (`(x + 0.5) / 4`), stated then as the tool's own
   choice. The fetch's place fits better on all four captures (first against fourth row), and it
   is what the microcode says; the native composite, `PostBloomFetchMirror` and `post_replay.py`
   (`--bloom-place fetch`, now the default of `replay` and `predict`; `aligned` reproduces the
   earlier figures) use it. Controller ruling 27 accepts it. Variant C (`post_sun_layer.py`)
   and the stored excerpt (`tests/post_replay_excerpt.json`, written again) sample there too
   since the commit after the runs (`bloom_sampler`'s own default); variant C on `134312` frame
   1 then reads median 0.48 and 90.2% within 8 levels against variant B's 1.13 and 70.7%
   (`t8_variant_C_134312_fetch.txt`; with the centres aligned 0.72 and 88.5% against 1.52 and
   69.9%).
2. *The downsample's pixel position* (`kPostDownsampleBias` = 0: the four texels (0, 0), (2, 0),
   (0, 2), (2, 2) of each 4 x 4 block). Under the aligned centres bias 0.5 had looked better
   (fifth row against fourth); that was the missing 1.5 pixels of the fetch, which a shift of the
   downsample by two texels makes up for. With the fetch's place bias 0 is the best of the three
   forms. It is also what the emulated picture's own shader is handed: the SDK's translator gives
   `param_gen` as `floor(SV_Position.xy)` (`dxbc_translator.cpp`, `StartPixelShader`). The front
   buffer of a capture is the emulator's picture, so this settles the constant for the picture the
   native one is held against; that the console's rasteriser hands the same position is
   inference, and discovery question 6 (the game's own downsample buffer, which is in no capture)
   stays unsettled.

answer. (2) A linear sample at a texel centre takes its neighbours with weight 0: on a GPU a
neighbour that is no number, or an infinite one (0 times infinity), makes that sample no number,
which the step then reads as 0, where the mirror reads the centre's texel; the lit paths write no such value. (3) The sun's two layers

measured ("Runs", item 5: a tenth of a level, one-sided). (6) One save, late morning, three
places, a standing camera; no `no-weights` frame, no night, no interior. (7) Cost not measured.

### The base map's gamma sign

Task 8b of the post sub-project (2026-10-10): why the native scene's ground was brighter than the
game's. Scripts and outputs: `out/native-evidence/post/t8b_*` (`t8b_scene_space.py`,
`t8b_ratio_map.py`, `t8b_ground.py`, `t8b_fc.py`, `t8b_rows.py`; their `.txt` and `.png`).

**The finding.** Every terrain row of the captures read fetches the base map tf3 (the baked light
map of `terrain_layer` and `terrain_far`: `pow(tf3, c21.w) * c21.xyz * L + c20.xyz`) with the
sign fields 3, 3, 3, 0 in its fetch constant (dword 0, bits 2 to 9; 3 is "gamma";
`t8b_fc.py` on capture `023443`: 567 of 567 in-scene tess rows, and no other texture of a tess or
mesh row has a gamma field; the review of Task 8b scanned every row of every kind and frame of
captures `034554` and `034918`: 4,976 of 4,976 and 4,896 of 4,896 tess rows, DXT1, identity
swizzle, exponent adjust 0, and the same single entry in seven older captures:
`out\tests\review-task8b\scan_signs.py`, `scan_gamma.py`; every capture is of one save and one
region of the world). With that field the console's fetch takes the filtered texel from
gamma to linear through its piecewise curve before the shader sees it (the SDK's
`PWLGammaToLinear`, applied by its translators in the case `TextureSign::kGamma`). The native
pass, the capture's material inputs and `terrain_replay.py` read the texel as stored. A stored
0.6 is 0.349 through the curve; after the power 1.3 the baked term is half. So **the ambient part
of all lit ground was 1.8 to 2.5 times the game's** (a factor of 0.40 to 0.55 on it explains the
far regions channel by channel; a factor on the sun does not: blue would need a negative one).
The light formulas were checked against the microcode with a random texture as tf3, which cannot
see what the fetch does to a texel; the fixed exposure 2.22 was then fitted on the dirt patch,
which hid it there.

**It is section 16's finding.** The offset "Native composite" and "Native bloom" report is the
table of section 16, "After the reviews: the fix wave" (criterion 4: far rock 1.13 and 1.18, far
slope 1.19, island 1.18, the ranges 1.22, 1.28, 1.45, dirt patch 1.21, rock face 1.23, with the
peak, the sky and the lake at 0.99 to 1.07), measured there with the post chain off. Measured
again here in the scene's own unit (`t8b_scene_bridge_off.txt`: the native shot of run T8-10 at
57 s taken back through the composite's and the ramp's grey response, over the stored scene of
capture `023443`, frame 1): dirt patch 1.20, rock face 1.24, far rock 1.13 and 1.19, far slope
1.19, island 1.18, the ranges 1.21, 1.28, 1.46, lake 1.06; far peak 0.985, sky 0.974 and 0.975,
grass beside the dirt 0.97, planks 0.97, trunk 1.01. The same regions at the same values with the
post steps on and off: **the post frame's words (the exposure, the unlit scale, the fog under
them) are not the cause**, and neither is the oracle: the emulated shot 3 s before is 0.98 to
0.99 of the replay's variant B of that capture in every region that holds still.

**Like for like, the excess was larger than the earlier tables say** (review of Task 8): "native
against emulated without bloom" set a native picture without bloom against the game's with it.
Native over the replay's variant of the same capture (`023305`; display luminance, in brackets to

1.156 (1.38) and 1.176 (1.43), right 1.126 (1.30) and 1.121 (1.29), far slope 1.101 (1.24) and
1.131 (1.31), island 1.095 (1.22) and 1.115 (1.27), dirt patch and rock face 1.117, 1.132 (1.28,
1.31) and 1.136, 1.150 (1.32, 1.36); peak, sky and lake 0.99 to 1.04 both ways. The bloom moves
the error by -0.03 to +0.13, not from 1.33 to 1.70: the bright pass has a threshold the game's
haze sits just above, so a scene 1.3 times too bright there adds a little more of itself.

**The measurement that separates it** (`t8b_ground_bridge.txt`, `t8b_ground_bridge_gamma.txt`;
`t8b_ground_third*.txt` for capture `023809`). Per pixel of a region: the game's colour before its
fog (the stored scene over `c20.w`, the in-scatter taken off and divided by the transmittance at
the pixel's world position from the stored depth, with the frame's own block and tables) against
what the native pass draws at that world position without shadows (`terrain_replay.py`'s lit
replay, far terrain under the layers), counted only where the terrain's own height is the depth's
(ground, not a tree or a post in front of it). Median of model over game, r / g / b:

| Region (pixels) | tf3 as stored | tf3 through the curve |
|---|---|---|
| dirt patch (167; near, inside the fog's start) | 1.21 / 1.29 / 1.43 | **1.00 / 1.02 / 1.00** |

The two grass regions of the bridge are left out of the table: they are covered by grass
plants, not bare terrain, and the terrain model does not describe them (with the curve its red is
1.51 and 1.60 of the game's on "grass beside it" and "grass in leaf shadow", its green 1.01 and
0.88: `t8b_ground_bridge_gamma.txt`). The native shots of "grass beside it" did not move with the
fix (0.994 -> 0.995 like for like: "Runs", item 2).

With the stored reading the model reproduces the native shots' excess (far slope: 1.34 to 1.40
before the fog is 1.2 after it, as measured); with the curve it is the game's within 1 to 4% on
bare ground in all three channels, near and far, at two places. The alternatives the task named:
the fog's in-scatter or its place against the exposure (a, b): excluded by the peak and the sky
(0.985, 0.975) and by the dirt patch, which is inside the start; the clamp and the target's format
(c): the regions are at 0.4 to 2 of a target that holds 64; the unlit scale (e): the regions are
lit terrain; the oracle (f): above. (d), the baked map, is it.

**What it does not explain.** (1) *The wooded hills.* On the three ranges 45 to 87% of the pixels
are not ground at the terrain's height: the game's distant trees (`t8b_bridge_off_ratio.png`:
the excess has the trees' outlines; `t8b_crop_far_mountains_left_*.png`). They are not drawn
natively (section 16, follow-up 2) and stay brighter than the game's dark crowns. This, not the
ground, is most of the left range's 1.46. (2) *The rock face* stays 15 to 23% over in the model:
steep ground, where the game lights with the side normal maps (tf14) the pass does not read, and
the model has no shadow mask (in the runs it is not over: "Runs", item 5). (3) *Ground under leaf shadow* (the grass regions, the third spot's
near ground) cannot be judged by a model without the mask. (4) *The lake* is an unlit placeholder.

**The fix** (one change): the two terrain shaders take tf3's r, g, b through `base_linear`
(the SDK's curve, after the filter, as its translator applies it) where the record's word
`t_base_gamma` (cbuffer Terrain, byte 188, until now a pad) has the component's bit;
`TerrainBaseGamma` (`clay_logic.h`) makes the mask from the record's own fetch constant, through
its swizzle as the SDK's `SwizzleSigns` does, and `SetClayTerrainLight` refuses a base map with a
signed or biased colour component (none occurs): such a record is not lit. `PwlGammaToLinear` is
the C++ mirror, `light_formulas.pwl_gamma_to_linear` the reference, and `terrain_replay.py` reads
every texture through its fetch constant's signs. Only the lit programs of the two terrain shaders
change (a program without light reads no base map: the shader test compares). `DrawRecord` is
untouched; no binding, no target and no SDK file changes. **The sign is checked for tf3 alone**: the other
textures the pass reads as stored (the terrain's tf0, tf13 and weights, every mesh material
texture) have no sign check and no census, so a gamma or biased field there would be drawn as
stored without a word, and tf3's exponent adjust (0 in every row) is not checked either. None
occurs in the captures scanned, all of one save and one region; a census line (bound textures
with a non-zero sign field a frame) is a follow-up (review of Task 8b, Minors 1 and 2). Tests: `tests/native/test_clay_logic.cpp`
cases 618 to 620, `tests/native/test_native_shaders.cpp` case 241 and the pins,
`tests/test_terrain_replay.py` (`GammaSignTest`).

**What changes in the picture, by the formula** (written before the runs; "Runs" below has what was seen): lit ground's ambient
part falls to 0.40 to 0.55 of what it was, in post frames and in today's frames alike. So ground
in shadow gets darker by about that factor and sunlit ground by 13 to 20%, and the fixed exposure
2.22, fitted on the dirt patch with the stored reading, now leaves the post-off picture's sunlit
ground about 17% under where it was fitted (it is not fitted again: no constant is tuned). The
figures of sections 14 to 16 for terrain regions are of the stored reading.

**When a run counts.** All four, or the run is made again and not used:

1. Its shots are **1942 pixels wide** (any `shot_<s>s.png` of the run). 1296 means the window
   opened on the 100%-scaled monitor: the run is repeated, up to three tries, and is otherwise

2. The driver's last line and exit code as the implementer rules ask (`RUN CLEAN`, or `RUN

3. No freeze signature (section 13: 23 to 26 fps with a guest work median near 40 ms) in any

4. A quiet machine: no other 3D load above about 20% (the ledger's limit).

--fable2_native_render=true,--fable2_native_post=off`, and run 13 `tools\drive_game.ps1 -BootSave
Hero000 -Total 300 -Shots "36,39,150,295" -Plan "32:VIEW=off,37:VIEW=native" -GameArgs
--fable2_native_render=true,--fable2_native_post=on,--fable2_native_bloom=on,--fable2_exposure_readback=on`.
The two rounds of a spot are made back to back, without another program started between them.
**On against off is decided only between runs of one round, and only if both rounds agree**: in
round 1 every "off" of a pair runs before its "on", in round 2 after it, so a drift of the machine
over the session shows as opposite signs in the two rounds and is not taken for a cost. Two runs
of different sessions decide nothing against each other ("Native composite", "Cost": the review of
plan Task 5, Minor 6). The pairs: post on against off is `post` against `off` (and `post_rb`
against `off_rb`); the bloom is `bloom` against `post` (`bloom_rb` against `post_rb`); the
read-back switch is each `<x>_rb` against `<x>`. A decision that needs only some pairs may be made
from those runs alone, if both rounds of them were made in the order above.

**What is read from each log.**

- *Steady windows*: every line `frames: view native (window): 150 frames, mean M ms (F fps), ...
  max X ms`, but for the three windows of a capture: the one in which `[native-discovery] capture
  requested` falls and the two after it (controller ruling 26: "not within three windows after a
  capture"). In logs 451 to 454 those three read 20.3 to 21.1, 16.4 to 17.7 and 27.8 to 30.0 fps.
- *The third window from the capture* of every S and T run, with its largest frame: reported for
  each run, the runs with the switch beside those without. It does not enter a bound (ruling 26).
  This is the window that read 27.8 fps (largest frame 146 ms) in log 453, post on with the
  switch, and 29.9 to 30.0 in logs 451, 452 and 454: unexplained ("Validation (10a)").
- *The capture's records-on median*: the `median` of every line `capture: frame N ... | records
  on | capture C ms (median M, ...over 300 frames)` whose 300 frames lie wholly in the native
  stretch before the capture (from 43 s in S, from 51 s in T); a run's figure is the mean of
  those lines' medians, and the lines are given.
- *The view-off median* (S and T): the `median` of the `capture:` lines with `records off` whose
  300 frames lie wholly after the last `VIEW=off`.
- *The exposure*: in a run with a capture, `c20.w` of every main-scene row of its 8 frames
  (`post_tables.py table` on the capture, as spec criterion 2 was read). Run 13 has no capture: a
  rule cannot ask capture rows of it; there it is the `c20.w` of every `Post:` line after 60 s.

**(a) Criterion 9, and criterion 15's cost part.**

- *Bridge, by ruling 26*: every steady window of runs 3 to 6 and 7 to 10 (post on; with the bloom
  and with the switch among them) and of run 13 at **29.7 fps or more**. Criterion 9 as written
  ("30.0 in every steady window") is not what is judged: the valid post-off run 454 itself reads
  29.8 in one window. The verdict's words are then "met by ruling 26", with the lowest window.
- *Third spot*: no steady window of runs 16 to 19 and 20 to 23 below **29.2 fps** (the fog
  sub-project's worst there).
- *The capture's median*: for each pair and each round, the on-run's records-on median less the
  off-run's, at the bridge and at the third spot; **at most 0.10 ms in both rounds** for post on
  against off (criterion 9) and for the bloom on against off (criterion 15). The third spot's
  figures are stated beside the fog's 2.64 to 2.92 ms. If the two rounds of a pair disagree (one
  within 0.10, one not), the pair is not decided and is run again.
- *View off*: under **0.5 ms** in every S and T run.
- A steady window below its bound in an "off" run of the same round as well is the machine's, not
  the post's: that round is made again and no verdict is drawn from it.
- Criterion 9 is met (by ruling 26 at the bridge) when all four hold for the `post` and `post_rb`
  runs against `off` and `off_rb`; criterion 15's cost part when they hold for `bloom` and
  `bloom_rb` as well, with the bloom's pairs. Anything else: not met, with the window or the
  difference that failed.

**(b) Ruling 2, the read-back switch's default.** Default ON only if all of:

1. every steady window of the bridge runs with the switch (2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 11) is at 29.7 fps or
   more and of the third spot's (15, 17, 19, 20, 22, 24) at 29.2 or more, as the runs without it
   in the same round are;
2. run 13 has no freeze signature and every window after its first at 29.7 fps or more;
3. the game adapts in each of those runs: `c20.w` below 12 in every main-scene capture row (16.000
   is the blind value), and in run 13 in every `Post:` line after 60 s;
4. the third window from the capture is not slower with the switch than without it in both
   rounds. If it is (the 27.8 of log 453 repeating), the switch costs something in the seconds
   after a diagnostic capture: that is put before the controller with the figures and the default
   is not changed without a ruling on it.

All four: one default changes (a builder's commit: the switch's test, the README's row, the

runs without it do not have: default OFF, with the figure. Anything mixed (a slow window without
the switch too, a freeze in run 13, an invalid run): no change, reported. The earlier text counted
"29.8 to 30.1 in every steady window with the switch" for it; that left the 27.8 out and is
withdrawn.

### Sun layer discovery

Plan Task 10 (2026-10-10; offline on captures that existed, then run 3, towards the sun with the current binary: the last paragraph). Tools: `tools/xdk_sigmatch/post_tables.py graph`, `quads`, `occluders`, `signs`. Captures, all `-BootSave Hero000` under full read-back, in `out\build\win-amd64-release\logs\`: `native_discovery_20261010_034415`, `_034554`, `_035057` (bridge), `_034736`, `_034918` (third spot), `_010653` and `20261009_205645` (trees), and the older `20261009_134312` (towards the sun, run 413, made before the `"cmdgap"` rows). Outputs: `out\native-evidence\post\t10_*.txt`.

**The graph, by the resolves' addresses** (`t10_graph_034415_f1.txt`, `_034918_f1.txt`, `_010653_f1.txt`; the same in frames 1, 4 and 8 of five captures wherever the capture skipped no stretch of the command stream). After the main scene, at half the scene's size (pitch 560):

1. The layer's depth: `5D67` writes the scene's depth copy (`0x1A02A000`) as depth; then, colour mask 0, depth tested and written, the three cloud quads (`3FF7`), three unit cubes (`D1CC`) and up to three tree draws (`F1EB`).
2. A colour clear, then the beam source (`8E4D`, colour format 2), resolved to `0x12AE1000` (576 x 360, format 7).
3. The colour target is switched to format 0 (`k_8_8_8_8`), cleared, and resolved to `0x12CFD000` (format 6) **with nothing drawn**; `0A96` (C1 of the research) reduces that into `0x12CC7000` (288 x 180, format 6). No row of any frame samples `0x12CC7000`. C1 has no drawn input and no reader in this save.
4. A colour clear, then layer 2: the flares (`D72F`), the moon glow (`4B58`, colour format 10), the sun disc (`3E77`), resolved to `0x12CFD000` (format 7); `0A96` (C2) reduces it into `0x12BB9000`.
5. `0A96` (C3) reduces the beam source's picture, `0x12AE1000`, into `0x12CFD000` at a quarter of the scene's size; the two radial blurs (`4BE4`) each sample `0x12CFD000` and are each resolved to `0x12CFD000` (the target is the GPU's own memory; the base is where a resolve copies it).
6. The bright pass (`EE92`) samples tf1 = `0x12CFD000`, tf2 = `0x12BB9000`.

So **tf1 is the beam source, reduced and blurred radially twice; tf2 is the second layer, reduced**: discovery question 3 is settled, and it is what the research read from the weights. *By content it cannot be settled in this emulator*: the dumps kept at the rows and the capture's memory dump hold no picture at these bases (`0x12BB9000` of `mem_12A00000_f1.bin`, `034415`, read as 280 x 180 format 7, is noise; Task 1 found the same of the downsample). *Limit of the method*: a resolve issued inside a stretch of the command stream the capture did not look at is in no row (63 stretches in `034918`, 6 in `034415` frame 1); `034918` frame 4 then shows tf1's chain ending in a cleared picture. The tool names the skipped stretches after the main scene; the 13 of 15 frames without one in the layer give the graph above. Not looked at: whether the depth-only rectangle beside layer 2's colour clear resets the layer's depth (Task 11's replay, in which the sun disc lies behind the depth at 1,984 pixels and fits the game's picture, speaks against it: inference).

**The occluders bring the layer's depth up to the whole scene's** (`t10_occluders_*.txt`). The scene's depth copy is resolved mid-frame, before the water, the late leaf draws and the clouds.

- *The cubes are the far water.* The main scene's far lake (`5763` / `2B09`, section 16 "The lake") is the same unit cube through the same builder (8 vertices, 30 indices), with vertex `c119.x` = 18.471556, bit for bit the first layer cube's, and it is drawn after the depth copy. By `D1CC`'s formula (`light_formulas.post_cube_point`): a floor 5,700 x 5,700 about the world's origin at the height `c119.x`, four walls up to a square about the eye at the eye's height, no top. The scene depth of `034415` frame 1 unprojected (`out\tests\post-task10\heights.py`): a flat bed at height 14.7 (8,603 pixels, about 188 units away) and 14,769 pixels (1.83%) below 18.47: the cube's floor is the lake's surface over the lake's bed. The two cubes at 20.002409 have no main-scene draw of that height in the frames read: not identified.
- *The tree draws are the scene's late leaves.* Each has the index buffer, index count, vertex buffer and vertex `c0..c3` of one main-scene leaf draw (`A584` or `D7DD` / `7CD5`), and those are exactly the leaf draws issued after the depth copy: 3 of 22 at the bridge, 3 of 35 at the third spot, 1 towards the sun, none by the trees (41 before the copy, no occluder draw). Index counts 24,463 / 18,722 / 9,319. State: depth test and write, colour mask 0, register `0x2202` = `0xAA00001C` (alpha test greater than 0, with alpha-to-mask).
- *The cloud quads* are the scene's clouds with their own alpha as the test (`3FF7`, greater than 0.149).

A native layer whose depth is the native depth at the end of the scene therefore needs the clouds only; the cubes only if the native water writes no depth.

**The quads** (`t10_quads_034415.txt`, `_034918.txt`, `_010653.txt`, `_134312.txt`). Every furniture quad is an `"indx"` row of `DrawIndx:82217EE8`: 4 vertices of 20 bytes (x y z u v), indices 0 1 2 1 3 2; no furniture shader passes another builder (the tree draws, which are no quads, apart). Rows a frame: moon 1, clouds 3, glare 1 (the moon's; 2 with the sun's, towards the sun and by the trees), layer depth 1, cloud occluders 3, cubes 3, tree draws 0 to 3, beam source 1, layer flares 0 (towards the sun), 2 (bridge, trees) or 4 (third spot), moon glow 1, sun disc 1, previous-frame blend 1: at most 16 quad records a frame against the bound of 24. *The alpha test per kind is the same in all 28 frames*: moon greater than 0.0039 (`0x3B808081`), clouds 0.0196, cloud occluders 0.1490, moon glow 0.0392, sun disc 0.5020; off for glare, beam source, flare, layer depth, cubes and the previous-frame blend (register `0x210E` then still reads the sun disc's 0.502).

**`D72F` at pitch 280** (ruling 24): before the main scene the game renders 4 (bridge), 8 (third spot) or 2 (trees) small views of the world with four samples (terrain, a sky cube `8262` / `F760`, and the same two flare quads), each resolved to a 256 x 256 texture (`0x13401000`, `0x13481000`, `0x13501000`, `0x13581000`) that the near-shore water (`F6D9`, `A17D`) samples at slot 13: the water's reflection views. Not the layer's flares.

**The 24 point draws** (`B6C9` / `A4A9`): one indirect buffer, `0x1FA98980`, 48 dwords, called 11 times a frame at the bridge; each draw is one point at the clip origin (the vertex shader's two instructions write (0, 0, 0, 1) and zeros; no fetch, no export) with colour mask 0 and the depth word 0 (`gpu_state_bridge.log`). They write nothing.

**The clouds** (`out\tests\post-task10\clouds.py`). Their texture is fetched with linear filters and mips 0 to 5 (`... 00A80D10 00000143 ...`), so the size of `6197`'s neighbour step matters: the emulator takes it in texels of the base level, and a native shader measured against emulated pictures takes that. Over open sky the three layers' cover has medians 0.05 (bridge), 0.02 (third spot), 0.24 (towards the sun) and maxima near 0.5; the scene colour's luminance under the most covered quarter of a picture row is 0.98 to 1.00 of that under the least covered, its blue share 0.012 to 0.022 lower: the clouds show as a faint warm tint, not as shapes.

**Regions** for criteria 18 and 19: `docs/native-renderer/post-regions.json` ("sun", "beams left", "beams right", "sky beside the sun"), chosen on `134312`'s front buffer and confirmed on run 3's (below). The reference with the sun layer on `134312` frame 1 (`t10_variant_c_134312_f1_regions.txt`): 90.2% of the pixels within 8 levels against 70.7% without the layer; the regions at 1.012, 1.120, 1.109 and 1.000 of the front buffer's luminance (0.967, 0.815, 0.782, 0.977 without). Earlier texts give 88.5% and 69.9% for this frame: those are with the bloom sampled at aligned texel centres, and the tools' default has been the fetch's own place since ruling 27 (`t10_variant_c_134312_f1_aligned.txt` reproduces 69.9% and 88.5% exactly with the old place).

**Sign fields** (review of the base map's gamma sign): `post_tables.py signs` over eight captures, 585,108 bound textures of every decoded row: nothing but the terrain's base map (signs 3 3 3 0) and float formats with 1 1 1 1; no exponent adjust (`t10_signs.txt`). One save, one region of the world.

**Not observed in this save** (late morning): the moon and its glow lit (their quads are drawn every frame, below the horizon, the moon with `c31.w` = 0); the moon's glare at a visible strength; any register's value at night, dawn or dusk; C1's layer drawn into; a flare's part in the picture. 

**Run 3, towards the sun** (the controller's, `RUN UNCHECKED`, 2026-10-10 05:21; binary of 05:13:02, commit `967c3e0`; plan line SUNWARD with `--fable2_native_fog=on,--readback_resolve=full,--native_render_collect_stats=true`; log 490, exit 0, no `d3d ERROR` line; shot width 1296, so nothing here is timing; evidence `out\native-evidence\post\t10_run3_*`; capture `native_discovery_20261010_052158`, 8 frames).

- *The graph* (`t10_run3_graph_f1.txt`, `_f4`, `_f8`): as at the other spots. tf1 (`0x12CFD000`) <- radial <- radial <- reduce <- beam source; tf2 (`0x12BB9000`) <- reduce <- moon glow + sun disc (frame 8: with the flares); C1 reduces the cleared picture into `0x12CC7000`, read by nothing. Five is the largest count of layer flares seen; with it a frame has 17 quad records at most.

## Pending

1. **Pitch ablation** (done 2026-10-01, results in section 4; kept for re-runs). One run per significant pitch `<p>` (1120, 1040, 320, 1280, 560, 280):
```
cd out\build\win-amd64-release
& .\fable_2.exe --fullscreen=false --native_render_suppress_debug=true --native_render_suppress_pitches=<p>
```
   Record what disappears or breaks on screen and name the pass (shadow map, main scene, water, post, UI). Fill section 4 with `pitch | draws | observed effect when suppressed | pass name`. Suppression debug mode also fakes all occlusion queries, so objects that are normally culled may appear.
2. **Tiling re-capture** (done 2026-10-01, results in section 3b; kept for re-runs). The counters and hooks are in place: census rows now carry `gpu.bin_selects` (SET_BIN_SELECT* writes), `gpu.tiles` and `gpu.tile_selects` (distinct non-zero bin-select values; LO/HI half-writes can add an intermediate value), `gpu.pred_draws` (predicated draw packets executed), `gpu.pred_skips` (predicated packets skipped) and `gpu.extents` (per pitch: max window-scissor corner, i.e. tile size in EDRAM, and max viewport size). The 15 extra hooks from section 7 item 1 come from `tools\xdk_sigmatch\fable2_extra_hooks.json` (`0x822A6318` is skipped: `src/diagnostics/fps_probe.h` already overrides it). Regenerate with:
```
python tools\xdk_sigmatch\gen_census_hooks.py --map docs\native-renderer\xdk-map.json --init generated\default\fable_2_init.cpp --src src --out src\native\capture\xdk_hooks.inc --ids-out src\native\capture\xdk_hook_ids.h --extra tools\xdk_sigmatch\fable2_extra_hooks.json
```
   Re-run the capture procedure below in the world and summarize; the summary gains a Tiling section and an extents table. Menu smoke run (2026-10-01): predicated tiling is active even in the menu (about 11 bin-select writes, 181 predicated draws and 130 skipped predicated packets per frame).
3. **F3 attribution** (user, in the world). Run `fable_2.exe --fullscreen=false --vsync=false --guest_vblank_pacing=false`, open F3, and record the Guest line, the GPU emu line and the Verdict. Fills the gameplay attribution in section 5.

Capture procedure, for re-runs: from `out\build\win-amd64-release`, set `FABLE2_D3D_CENSUS=900` and `FABLE2_D3D_CENSUS_DELAY=<seconds until in the world>`, run `fable_2.exe`, wait for `[census] complete` in the game log, then clear both variables. Summarize with `python tools\xdk_sigmatch\summarize_census.py <capture> [--from-frame N --to-frame N]`.
